| `dsh-provider-retry` | Хост-надстройка над `agent/request-error`: ловит ошибки лимита/квоты провайдера (Z.ai 429 `code 1308/1310…`, `Retry-After`, OpenRouter `resets_at`, DeepSeek `QUOTA`) и вместо in-turn ретрая ставит один durable `schedule`-повтор на время сброса лимита; в момент сброса сессия получает промпт «продолжи с проверки состояния». Naive-штампы Z.ai читаются в UTC+8, терминальные ошибки (недостаток баланса, `openrouter_credits`) не ретраятся, дубли задач не копятся. Host-only, без своего UI. |
| `dsh-halt-jobs` | Пилюля «остановить все фоновые задачи» в шапке сессии: показывает число живых задач сессии и гасит все `running`-задачи одним кликом. |
| `dsh-plugin-workspace-policy` | Per-workspace политика маршрута LLM: `.dsh/workspace.yaml` в корне воркспейса задаёт модель мастер-сессий, модель всех дочерних агентов, per-preset маршруты (`model.presets`, например `cursor/vv-controller`) и цепочку деградации; применяется на шве `agent.model.select()` при создании агента, не трогая глобальный `agent-default-model`. |
| `dsh-task-scheduler` | Persistent-планировщик задач: панель в Настройках, AI-задачи из `.md`, скрипты (`bun run`), cron с тикером 15 с и тул `task_trigger`. |
| `dsh-vv-panel` | Панель управления vv-циклом в Web-GUI: шесть кнопок `vv-spec`/`vv-plan`/`vv-execute`/`vv-review`/`vv-reflect`/`vv-handoff` в тулбаре композера между селектором доступа и Vision. Клик сразу отправляет жест скилла `/vv-<name>` (набранный в поле текст дописывается контекстом); видна только в сессиях с пресетом `vv-controller` или `cursor/vv-controller`. Седьмой чип — live operational-состояние активного `.vvoc/specs/`-пакета (draft-spec → spec-approved → draft-plan → ready-to-execute → executing → applied; `stale-approval` перекрывает всё) через host-мост `workspaceFiles` (read-only, host читает байты, клиент выводит состояние; клик отправляет контекстно-правильный жест). Без моста — честный fallback-чип `state` с self-contained промптом для `spec_guard_lint`; состояние никогда не выдумывается. Чистый web-client плагин, host-половина — no-op. |

## Пресеты

| Директория | Что это |
| --- | --- |
| `agent-presets` | Бандл с тремя пользовательскими агент-пресетами: `vv-controller` (порт [vv-opencode](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode) — spec → plan → execute с review-гейтами, скиллы `vv-spec`/`vv-plan`/`vv-execute`/`vv-review`/`vv-reflect`/`vv-handoff`, `.vvoc`-артефакты), `cursor/vv-controller` (тот же цикл на моделях Cursor через плагин [cursor-to-dsh](https://github.com/lukeinx/cursor-to-dsh); маршруты — `model.presets` в workspace-policy) и `standard-browser` (штатный `standard` + браузерные субагенты через `subagent_browser`), плюс служебные дочерние пресеты `vv-worker` / `cursor/vv-worker` / `browser-subagent` для их субагентов. Hive-волна 2026-11: скиллы несут контракты из [hive](https://github.com/ivankuznetsov/hive) — двухосевая классификация находок (severity × decision authority), evidence anchors с байт-сверкой, бюджеты конвергенции ревью + reason codes + grants, статус-конверт и headless-контракт субагентов, stale-artifact rule, retry-fingerprints, nonce-обёртки untrusted-контента, adversarial-линза + coverage ledger, split reviser/verifier, triage bias с decision dossiers, digest-bound одобрения, verification receipts, pre-commit diff guardrail (норматив: `hive-research/vv-contract-vocabulary.md`, разбор: `hive-research/hive-practices-analysis.md`). |

Пресет в 0.2 — это declaration-строка `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` в патче бандла, а не каталог. Ставится как обычный бандл:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./agent-presets
# затем перезапуск dsh web: строка пресета грузится на старте процесса
```

Проверка: в списке пресетов все шесть карточек без бейджа «Failed to load»; новая сессия с пресетом `vv-controller` должна показать шесть `vv-*` скиллов в каталоге; сессия с `standard-browser` — инструмент `subagent_browser`; сессия с `cursor/vv-controller` — те же шесть `vv-*` скиллов и старт на `cursor`-маршруте в workspace с `model.presets` (требуется плагин cursor-to-dsh и Cursor API Key).

Состав:

- `cordis.patch.yml` — шесть строк-деклараций: три пользовательских пресета (`vv-controller`, `cursor/vv-controller`, `standard-browser`) и три служебных дочерних (`vv-worker`, `cursor/vv-worker`, `browser-subagent`), которые субагент-строки выбирают через `agentPreset` (в DSH 0.2.1 персона и тулсет ребёнка задаются только отдельным пресетом — `persona`/`toolFilter` в `tool-subagent` больше не принимаются); каждая список `plugins` — это текущий shipped-пресет того же семейства (`cordis` / `standard`) плюс дельты, поэтому имена пакетов не устаревают вместе с бандлом;
- `skills/*/SKILL.md` — шесть vv-скиллов; роли ревьюеров и имплементера живут как самодостаточные промпты суб-агентов внутри `vv-execute`/`vv-review` (в DSH нет реестра именованных агентов — роли spawn'ятся через `subagent`);
- артефакты совместимы с vv-opencode: `.vvoc/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/{spec,plan,design-context}.xml`, `archive/`, `.vvoc/lessons`, `.vvoc/runbooks`, `.vvoc/handoff` — те же пути и XML-формат, так что один проект можно вести и из OpenCode, и из DSH.

Подробности миграции с 0.1 (старый `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/<id>/` больше не читается) — в `agent-presets/README.md`.

## Установка у коллеги

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AlexQuidditch/dsh-plugins.git
cd dsh-plugins

# бандлы (все или выборочно; `dsh plugin add` принимает путь к локальному пакету):
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-peak-hours
dsh plugin --profile web add ./hello-world
dsh plugin --profile web add ./scope-router
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-guardian
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-context
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-spec-guard
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-managed-sessions
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-halt-jobs
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-plugin-workspace-policy
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-task-scheduler
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-panel
dsh plugin --profile web add ./agent-presets     # пресеты vv-controller + standard-browser

dsh web --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3080 --no-open   # перезапуск, чтобы подхватить бандлы
```

Примечания:

- `dsh plugin add` сам добавляет пакет в `dsh.profile.bundles` (ручная запись в `cordis.patch.yml` профиля не нужна). Аргументы после `add` уходят в pnpm, поэтому путь `./<dir>` — это локальный пакет, а голое имя — пакет из реестра (эти пакеты в npm не публикуются).
- Если `dsh` не на PATH — запустите через `pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 plugin --profile web add ...` или `node <путь-к-репо-deepseek-harness>/apps/cli/lib/bin.js plugin --profile web add ...`.
- После установки обязателен **один перезапуск** `dsh web`. Если на порту уже висит старый `dsh web`, сначала остановите его (Ctrl+C / `kill <PID>`), иначе порт занят.
- Имя профиля (`--profile web`) подставьте своё, если ваша установка использует другое.

## Пересборка (необязательно)

`lib/` закоммичены, поэтому на обычной установке сборка не нужна. Пересобрать можно не всё: исходники (`src/` + `tsconfig.json`) есть только у части пакетов.

- Клиентские бандлы (`hello-world`, `dsh-halt-jobs`, `dsh-vv-context`) требуют чекаут исходников DSH, лежащий сестринской папкой: их `tsdown.config.ts` импортирует `../../deepseek-harness/packages/client/tsdown.client.ts`.
- Серверные `scope-router`, `dsh-vv-guardian`, `dsh-vv-spec-guard` собираются обычным `tsc`; `dsh-plugin-workspace-policy` — `tsdown` (+ тесты `vitest`).
- У `dsh-peak-hours`, `dsh-task-scheduler`, `dsh-managed-sessions` и `agent-presets` исходников в репозитории нет — только готовые `lib/`; в репозитории они не пересобираются.

```bash
# клиентские (нужен сестринский чекаут DSH):
cd hello-world        && pnpm install && pnpm run build
cd ../dsh-halt-jobs   && pnpm install && pnpm run build
cd ../dsh-vv-context  && pnpm install && pnpm run build

# серверные:
cd ../scope-router && pnpm install && pnpm run build   # и так же dsh-vv-guardian, dsh-vv-spec-guard
cd ../dsh-plugin-workspace-policy && pnpm install && pnpm run build && pnpm test
```

# dsh-scope-router

Host-плагин DeepSeek Harness: **автоматическое внедрение инструкций проекта по скоупу работы агента**.

Определяет, над чем работает агент — в каком проекте (`projectRoots`), в каком доменном
пакете (`packages/domains/<name>`) и на каком слое (backend/frontend) — по трём сигналам:

1. текст сообщения (упоминание домена / ключевые слова слоя);
2. файловая активность (`fs/observed`);
3. shell-активность (`tools/result` для `bash`/`pwsh`: `workdir` и пути в `command`).

При смене скоупа перед шагом модели внедряется бандл инструкций: ядро (`coreFiles`) +
доменный файл (`domainCandidates`) + послойные карты (`layerFiles`). Новая подборка
текстуально заменяет предыдущую. Вне проекта роутер бездействует.

## Workspace-гейтинг (с v0.2.0)

Роутер учитывает **workspace сессии агента** (`agent.session.header.cwd`):

- root из `projectRoots` элиджиблен для агента только если его cwd равен root'у или
  лежит внутри него. Агент, работающий в другом репозитории, **не получает никаких
  инструкций**, даже если текст диалога упоминает домены проекта (постмортем:
  инструкции `platform` утекали агентам в чужих репо через упоминания и активность);
- вся файловая и shell-активность атрибутируется **конкретному агенту**
  (`ToolExecution.agent`; `actor` события `fs/observed` несёт того же агента) и
  хранится в пер-агентских картах — в многосессионном `dsh web` активность одного
  агента не повышает скоринг root'а для другого;
- относительные фрагменты путей (`packages/...`, `apps/...`) из shell-команд
  резолвятся только против root'ов, содержащих cwd **действующего** агента:
  команды из чужого репозитория больше не фабрикуют пути внутри сконфигурированных
  root'ов;
- заголовок бандла называет рабочий workspace и root проекта; пробный тул
  `scope_router_status` показывает состояние гейтинга и недавнюю активность
  с атрибуцией по агентам.

Чтобы покрыть другой репозиторий — добавьте его корень в `projectRoots` с его собственными
`coreFiles`/`layerFiles`: роутер мульти-root'овый, каждый root обслуживает агентов
своего workspace.

## Worktree-пиннинг (с v0.3.0)

Сессия, созданная внутри каталога worktree'ов (`worktrees.dir`, например
`~/projects/platform.worktrees`), получает скоуп **по имени worktree-каталога**:

- root для чтения файлов — сам worktree, т.е. инструкции берутся из чекаута
  соответствующей ветки, а не из основного репозитория;
- домен закреплён именем каталога (`worktrees.domainByWorktree` переопределяет
  соответствие «имя → домен», по умолчанию они совпадают): ни текст диалога, ни
  файловая/shell-активность не могут переключить домен или подтянуть файлы
  другого домена — например, диалог в `obnime` получает только obnime;
- `worktrees.includeCore` (по умолчанию `true`) добавляет корневые `coreFiles`
  worktree — без них worktree без доменного файла (сейчас это `obnime`,
  `pilot-school`, `monitor-sts`) не получал бы ничего, кроме правил репо;
- `worktrees.includeLayers` (по умолчанию `false`) добавляет послойные карты;
- относительные `packages/…`/`apps/…` из shell-команд агента worktree
  резолвятся против корня его worktree;
- заголовок бандла называет пиннинг; пробный тул `scope_router_status` показывает
  каталог worktree'ов и `pinned=yes/no` в последней детекции.

### Все файлы скоупа + fallback на основной root (v0.4.0)

В pinned-режиме инжектятся **все найденные** файлы скоупа из `domainCandidates`
(например, одновременно `packages/domains/<app>/AGENTS.md` и `apps/<app>/AGENTS.md` —
это дополняющие файлы, а не приоритетная цепочка; в угаданном режиме main-root
поведение прежнее — первый найденный).

Если ветка worktree ещё не содержит какой-то файл скоупа (его добавили в основной
репозиторий, но не слинковали в worktree), файл читается **из основного root**
(`projectRoots`), а заголовок бандла и лог отмечают это. После `worktree-app.sh
sync` (merge develop) файл начинает читаться из чекаута worktree.

Новый worktree подхватывается без правки конфига: создали `worktree-app.sh
ensure <app>` + workspace — плагин сам пиннит скоуп по имени каталога.

## Сборка

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run build        # tsc → lib/
node activation.test.mjs
```

## Установка в профиль

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ~/projects/dsh-plugins/scope-router
dsh --dump-config --profile web   # строка scope-router в дереве
# перезапустить dsh web
```

## Конфиг (в cordis.patch.yml пакета)

| Ключ | Описание |
| --- | --- |
| `projectRoots` | абсолютные корни проектов; без них плагин неактивен |
| `coreFiles` | root-относительные файлы ядра (всегда) |
| `layerFiles` | `{ backend: [], frontend: [] }` — послойные карты |
| `domainsDir` | каталог, поддиректории которого = домены |
| `domainCandidates` | шаблоны доменных файлов, `{domain}` заменяется именем |
| `maxBundleChars` | кап одного бандла (по умолчанию 80000) |
| `probeTool` | регистрировать отладочный тул `scope_router_status` |
| `log` | логировать инъекции |
| `worktrees.dir` | каталог worktree'ов: сессия внутри `<dir>/<name>` пиннится к скоупу `<name>` |
| `worktrees.domainByWorktree` | переопределение «имя каталога worktree → домен» |
| `worktrees.includeCore` | core-файлы в worktree-бандле (по умолчанию `true`) |
| `worktrees.includeLayers` | послойные карты в worktree-бандле (по умолчанию `false`) |

Набор бандл-плагинов для DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) и порт [vv-opencode](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode). Каждый бандл объявляет `dsh.bundle.patch`, поэтому устанавливается командой `dsh plugin add`. Собранные артефакты `lib/` уже закоммичены — **сборка не нужна**.

| `dsh-plugin-workspace-policy` | Per-workspace политика маршрута LLM: `.dsh/workspace.yaml` в корне воркспейса задаёт модель мастер-сессий, модель всех дочерних агентов, per-preset маршруты (`model.presets`, например `cursor/vv-controller`) и цепочку деградации; применяется на шве `agent.model.select()` при создании агента, не трогая глобальный `agent-default-model`. |
| `dsh-task-scheduler` | Persistent-планировщик задач: панель в Настройках, AI-задачи из `.md`, скрипты (`bun run`), cron с тикером 15 с и тул `task_trigger`. |
| `dsh-vv-panel` | Панель управления vv-циклом в Web-GUI: шесть кнопок `vv-spec`/`vv-plan`/`vv-execute`/`vv-review`/`vv-reflect`/`vv-handoff` в тулбаре композера между селектором доступа и Vision. Клик сразу отправляет жест скилла `/vv-<name>` (набранный в поле текст дописывается контекстом); видна только в сессиях с пресетом `vv-controller` или `cursor/vv-controller`. Седьмой чип — live operational-состояние активного `.vvoc/specs/`-пакета (draft-spec → spec-approved → draft-plan → ready-to-execute → executing → applied; `stale-approval` перекрывает всё) через host-мост `workspaceFiles` (read-only, host читает байты, клиент выводит состояние; клик отправляет контекстно-правильный жест). Без моста — честный fallback-чип `state` с self-contained промптом для `spec_guard_lint`; состояние никогда не выдумывается. Чистый web-client плагин, host-половина — no-op. |

## Пресеты

| Директория | Что это |
| --- | --- |
| `agent-presets` | Бандл с тремя пользовательскими агент-пресетами: `vv-controller` (порт [vv-opencode](https://github.com/osovv/vv-opencode) — spec → plan → execute с review-гейтами, скиллы `vv-spec`/`vv-plan`/`vv-execute`/`vv-review`/`vv-reflect`/`vv-handoff`, `.vvoc`-артефакты), `cursor/vv-controller` (тот же цикл на моделях Cursor через плагин [cursor-to-dsh](https://github.com/lukeinx/cursor-to-dsh); маршруты — `model.presets` в workspace-policy) и `standard-browser` (штатный `standard` + браузерные субагенты через `subagent_browser`), плюс служебные дочерние пресеты `vv-worker` / `cursor/vv-worker` / `browser-subagent` для их субагентов. Hive-волна 2026-11: скиллы несут контракты из [hive](https://github.com/ivankuznetsov/hive) — двухосевая классификация находок (severity × decision authority), evidence anchors с байт-сверкой, бюджеты конвергенции ревью + reason codes + grants, статус-конверт и headless-контракт субагентов, stale-artifact rule, retry-fingerprints, nonce-обёртки untrusted-контента, adversarial-линза + coverage ledger, split reviser/verifier, triage bias с decision dossiers, digest-bound одобрения, verification receipts, pre-commit diff guardrail (норматив: `hive-research/vv-contract-vocabulary.md`, разбор: `hive-research/hive-practices-analysis.md`). |

Пресет в 0.2 — это declaration-строка `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` в патче бандла, а не каталог. Ставится как обычный бандл:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./agent-presets
# затем перезапуск dsh web: строка пресета грузится на старте процесса
```

Проверка: в списке пресетов все шесть карточек без бейджа «Failed to load»; новая сессия с пресетом `vv-controller` должна показать шесть `vv-*` скиллов в каталоге; сессия с `standard-browser` — инструмент `subagent_browser`; сессия с `cursor/vv-controller` — те же шесть `vv-*` скиллов и старт на `cursor`-маршруте в workspace с `model.presets` (требуется плагин cursor-to-dsh и Cursor API Key).

Состав:

- `cordis.patch.yml` — шесть строк-деклараций: три пользовательских пресета (`vv-controller`, `cursor/vv-controller`, `standard-browser`) и три служебных дочерних (`vv-worker`, `cursor/vv-worker`, `browser-subagent`), которые субагент-строки выбирают через `agentPreset` (в DSH 0.2.1 персона и тулсет ребёнка задаются только отдельным пресетом — `persona`/`toolFilter` в `tool-subagent` больше не принимаются); каждая список `plugins` — это текущий shipped-пресет того же семейства (`cordis` / `standard`) плюс дельты, поэтому имена пакетов не устаревают вместе с бандлом;
- `skills/*/SKILL.md` — шесть vv-скиллов; роли ревьюеров и имплементера живут как самодостаточные промпты суб-агентов внутри `vv-execute`/`vv-review` (в DSH нет реестра именованных агентов — роли spawn'ятся через `subagent`);
- артефакты совместимы с vv-opencode: `.vvoc/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/{spec,plan,design-context}.xml`, `archive/`, `.vvoc/lessons`, `.vvoc/runbooks`, `.vvoc/handoff` — те же пути и XML-формат, так что один проект можно вести и из OpenCode, и из DSH.

Подробности миграции с 0.1 (старый `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/<id>/` больше не читается) — в `agent-presets/README.md`.

## Установка у коллеги

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AlexQuidditch/dsh-plugins.git
cd dsh-plugins

# бандлы (все или выборочно; `dsh plugin add` принимает путь к локальному пакету):
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-peak-hours
dsh plugin --profile web add ./hello-world
dsh plugin --profile web add ./scope-router
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-guardian
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-context
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-spec-guard
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-managed-sessions
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-halt-jobs
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-plugin-workspace-policy
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-task-scheduler
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-vv-panel
dsh plugin --profile web add ./agent-presets     # пресеты vv-controller + standard-browser

dsh web --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3080 --no-open   # перезапуск, чтобы подхватить бандлы
```

Примечания:

- `dsh plugin add` сам добавляет пакет в `dsh.profile.bundles` (ручная запись в `cordis.patch.yml` профиля не нужна). Аргументы после `add` уходят в pnpm, поэтому путь `./<dir>` — это локальный пакет, а голое имя — пакет из реестра (эти пакеты в npm не публикуются).
- Если `dsh` не на PATH — запустите через `pnpm dlx @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2 plugin --profile web add ...` или `node <путь-к-репо-deepseek-harness>/apps/cli/lib/bin.js plugin --profile web add ...`.
- После установки обязателен **один перезапуск** `dsh web`. Если на порту уже висит старый `dsh web`, сначала остановите его (Ctrl+C / `kill <PID>`), иначе порт занят.
- Имя профиля (`--profile web`) подставьте своё, если ваша установка использует другое.

## Пересборка (необязательно)

`lib/` закоммичены, поэтому на обычной установке сборка не нужна. Пересобрать можно не всё: исходники (`src/` + `tsconfig.json`) есть только у части пакетов.

- Клиентские бандлы (`hello-world`, `dsh-halt-jobs`, `dsh-vv-context`) требуют чекаут исходников DSH, лежащий сестринской папкой: их `tsdown.config.ts` импортирует `../../deepseek-harness/packages/client/tsdown.client.ts`.
- Серверные `scope-router`, `dsh-vv-guardian`, `dsh-vv-spec-guard` собираются обычным `tsc`; `dsh-plugin-workspace-policy` — `tsdown` (+ тесты `vitest`).
- У `dsh-peak-hours`, `dsh-task-scheduler`, `dsh-managed-sessions` и `agent-presets` исходников в репозитории нет — только готовые `lib/`; в репозитории они не пересобираются.

```bash
# клиентские (нужен сестринский чекаут DSH):
cd hello-world        && pnpm install && pnpm run build
cd ../dsh-halt-jobs   && pnpm install && pnpm run build
cd ../dsh-vv-context  && pnpm install && pnpm run build

# серверные:
cd ../scope-router && pnpm install && pnpm run build   # и так же dsh-vv-guardian, dsh-vv-spec-guard
cd ../dsh-plugin-workspace-policy && pnpm install && pnpm run build && pnpm test
```

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # DSH Bot Team A persistent roster of AI bots in the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) sidebar. Every bot is a real DSH Session backed by its own folder, persona, and conversation history — talk to one like a teammate in a contact list instead of hunting through the session log. **English** | [中文](README.zh.md) ``` ┌ Your bot team ───────────────────────── [ + New bot ] ┐ │ 🧭 Scout │ 🧭 Scout · Researcher ● Idle │ │ Researcher │ ┌ transcript ────────────────────┐ │ │ 🛠️ Forge │ │ │ │ │ Builder │ └────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ 📊 Ledger │ [ Message Scout… ] [Send] │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ## Why? DSH already runs agents well. What a chat-style roster adds is **persistence and organization**: a stable identity per bot (name, emoji, role), a dedicated workspace folder, and an ongoing conversation reachable in one click. The roster has a **chief of staff**: one bot whose job is to take a request, name the right teammate, and hand the work over. It never does the work itself, and it cannot send anything without your click. The panel acts as a messenger interface over native DSH Sessions rather than a separate runtime. Sending a message here invokes `session.prompt()` — the exact same path used by the main composer — so replies stream into both this panel and the bot's native session simultaneously. Clicking **Open chat** hands you the full DSH workspace (tools, approvals, files, and terminals) whenever you need deeper control. ## How It Works: One Workspace, One Persona per Session The whole team lives in **one Workspace** — the roster's own directory — so the sidebar shows a single group with one conversation per bot, named after that bot. Inside it: - **A persona per Session** — the host backend contributes a prompt section that reads the bot the Session belongs to and stays empty for any other conversation, so no other Session picks up a bot's character. - **Plain-text persistence** — the same instructions are written to `/AGENTS.md`, readable, diffable, and editable on disk. - **A folder of its own for files** — each bot keeps `bots//` for the files it makes; the plugin tells it that path in its persona. ## How Work Gets Handed Out Ask the chief for something and it answers with a proposal, not with a claim that work started: 1. The chief calls `team_assign`, which **records** the assignment for each named bot and returns `awaiting-confirmation`. Nothing has been sent. 2. The Team panel lists them in a queue, the sidebar entry carries a count badge, and a small pill follows you across panels — click it to come back. 3. You dispatch one, or **Dispatch all** to send the whole queue at once — that click is the confirmation. The task arrives in the target bot's own conversation as a user message, attributed to this plugin, and the bot starts working. 4. When that bot goes idle again, the assignment settles and the panel says so. You can also dispatch directly: select any bot, press **Assign a task**, and type it. The click is the confirmation, so the chief is not involved. A delivery that could not start — usually because a bot has no conversation yet — stays in the queue with its reason and a **Retry** button instead of vanishing. **Unattended mode** is the explicit switch for the case where nobody is watching. Set `unattended: true` and `team_assign` delivers immediately; leave it off and an agent can only propose. The panel shows the mode, so it is always clear which one is in force. ## Features - **Sidebar integration** — Adds a global **Team** icon (two bot heads) to the left sidebar and opens the roster view in the main column. - **A chief of staff** — a built-in bot, pinned first in the roster, that decomposes a request and proposes assignments. Fired by accident, it is hired again on the next start, and its folder keeps the conversation. - **A confirmation gate** — proposals wait in the panel until you dispatch them; the sidebar entry shows how many are waiting, and each dispatch lands in the target bot's own session. - **Named in the sidebar** — one **Bot team** Workspace holds every bot conversation, each titled with its bot's name, instead of an untitled chat in an ungrouped bucket. - **Live roster** — Displays each bot's avatar, name, role, and real-time working/idle indicator. Auto-refreshes while open, so bots hired from other windows or chats appear automatically. - **Inline chat** — Includes a message transcript that renders Markdown (headings, lists, tables, fenced code, quotes, links) as real elements — never as injected HTML — plus tool-call chips, a live status indicator, and a composer wired into the underlying DSH Session. - **Lazy session startup** — A bot's Session is created on its first message inside its dedicated folder, ensuring `AGENTS.md` instructions are loaded before its first turn. - **Built-in role templates** — Ships with **Scout** (Researcher), **Forge** (Builder), **Ledger** (Analyst), and **Quill** (Writer). Three starter bots are pre-hired on first launch. - **Start a bot over** — archives the conversation a bot owns and clears the binding, so the next message opens a fresh conversation in the team workspace; the old one stays recoverable in the session archive. - **Agent-manageable** — Built-in agent tools let any DSH chat hire, brief, or fire bots conversationally. - **Bilingual UI** — Supports English and Simplified Chinese (`简体中文`), automatically matching your DSH locale. ## Team Recipes You do not have to design a roster from scratch. Two shapes work well, and you can edit either into your own after one conversation. **Research desk** — a paper or an experiment goes in, a reviewed judgement comes out: | Bot | Role | Persona you can paste | |---|---|---| | Reviewer | 审稿人 | Read like a hostile but fair referee: is the claim supported by the evidence, is the baseline fair, what would falsify this? | | Replicator | 实验复现 | Re-run the method in your folder, on the data you have, and report exactly what reproduces and what does not, with the command that shows it. | | Librarian | 论文检索 | Find related work, read it, and return a short brief with links: what is new, what is contested, what to read next. | **Shipping desk** — code and operations: | Bot | Role | Persona you can paste | |---|---|---| | Builder | 实现 | Write the smallest working change, run it, and report the command that proves it. | | Reviewer | 评审 | Read the diff before it ships: correctness, tests that would have caught the bug, anything that breaks a caller. | | Operator | 运维 | Watch what runs, reproduce failures from the logs, and hand back a fix or a precise question. | Create them in the panel (**New bot**, then type the role and persona), or just ask in a chat: *"hire a reviewer bot that reads like a hostile but fair referee, and a librarian that returns briefs with links."* Names, emoji, and roles are yours — the persona is what the bot actually follows, and you can rewrite it any time. ## Installation **Prerequisites:** DSH `0.2.x` or newer with the Web GUI enabled. 1. Clone this repository: ```sh git clone https://github.com/BaiGang/dsh-bots-team.git ``` 2. In DSH, navigate to **Plugins → Add plugin** and select the cloned directory. 3. Reload the browser page so the client bundle joins the boot graph. **Team** will appear in the left sidebar. ### Configuration (Optional) You can customize the storage directory in your plugin configuration: ```yaml - id: bots-team name: 'dsh-bots-team' config: dataDir: /absolute/path/to/team-data # default: $DSH_HOME/bots-team unattended: false # true lets team_assign deliver without a panel click guidance: true # standing "## Bot team" note in every Session's prompt ``` ## Quick Start 1. Click **Team** in the left sidebar. 2. Select a starter bot, or click **+ New bot** to create one from a template. 3. Send a message. The first message initializes the bot's Session in its folder; subsequent messages continue the same thread. 4. Click **Open chat** anytime to jump into the full DSH session view in the main column. 5. Click **Edit** to update a bot's name, emoji, role, or instructions (`AGENTS.md` updates immediately for the next turn). ## Agent Tools Other agents in DSH can inspect and manage your roster programmatically: | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `team_roster` | Lists all bots along with their role, persona, folder path, and session status. | | `team_hire` | Creates a new bot (name, role, persona, emoji) and initializes its workspace folder. | | `team_brief` | Updates an existing bot's persona instructions or role. | | `team_fire` | Removes a bot from the roster while leaving its folder and Session intact on disk. | | `team_assign` | Records one or more assignments for named bots. Delivers them only in unattended mode; otherwise the person confirms in the panel. | | `team_status` | Reports each bot's session, whether its agent is live and running, and the state of recent assignments. | > **Example:** Ask any DSH chat to *"Hire a reviewer bot that is strict about unit tests"* — the new bot will appear in your Team panel on the next refresh. ## Data & Storage - **Roster manifest:** `$DSH_HOME/bots-team/team.json` (defaults to `~/.dsh/bots-team/team.json`), which also holds the last 100 assignment records. - **Bot workspaces:** `$DSH_HOME/bots-team/bots//`, each containing `AGENTS.md` and a `.git` root marker. - **API transport:** The browser panel communicates with the host backend over the loopback endpoint `/bots-team/api`. **Safe deletion:** Firing or deleting a bot only removes its entry from `team.json`. Its workspace folder, files, and DSH Session remain untouched on disk for easy recovery. ## Project Structure | Path | Purpose | |---|---| | [`index.js`](index.js) | **Host backend:** Roster store, workspace/`AGENTS.md` provisioning, `/bots-team/api` routes, and agent tools. | | [`client.js`](client.js) | **Browser client:** Registers the `sidebar.panellist` icon and `main` panel via a single `__ModuleLoader__` factory. | | [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) | Bundle patch that registers the host plugin row. | | [`locale/`](locale) | Localized plugin metadata (titles, descriptions, and detail doc paths). | | [`docs/DETAIL.md`](docs/DETAIL.md) | Plugin overview displayed inside the DSH Plugin Manager. | | [`assets/`](assets) | Storefront tile for the plugin catalog, and the framed SVG it is rendered from. | | [`test/smoke.mjs`](test/smoke.mjs) | Headless test suite (24 checks covering both host and client). | **Zero external dependencies:** The host backend uses only Node.js built-ins so it runs cleanly across any DSH profile. The browser client imports only React from DSH's runtime module table. ## Development Run the smoke test suite: ```sh node test/smoke.mjs # runs 24 checks; exits non-zero on failure ``` The test suite exercises the HTTP routes via mocked Node request/response pairs, verifies CRUD operations and all four agent tools against a temporary directory, and loads `client.js` through a `__ModuleLoader__` stub with a lightweight React shim to assert component trees and data flow — no browser required. ## Known Limitations - **One shared working directory:** every bot Session runs in the roster directory, so a bot that changes its own working directory leaves the group. - **Requires HTTP loopback:** Desktop shells serving the UI over `file://` cannot reach `/bots-team/api` (the panel displays an explicit notice in this environment). - **Profile-scoped:** One roster is shared across the active DSH profile rather than scoped per project. - **Single thread per bot:** Each bot maintains one continuous conversation. Starting fresh requires hiring a new bot, while conversation forking must be done from the main session list. - **Shared model config:** Bots inherit the active profile's model; per-bot model overrides are not yet supported. - **Manual session cleanup:** Removing a bot from the roster does not delete or archive its underlying Session in DSH's main session list. - **A bot needs a conversation before it can be dispatched to:** the panel creates and binds one on the first dispatch, and a bot nobody has opened yet fails with that reason rather than silently doing nothing. - **Completion is polled, not pushed:** the panel notices a finished assignment on its next refresh and shows a short notice; there is no notification outside the panel yet. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 BaiGang

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Bosi Programming Skills

Thirty-nine Claude Code skills, packaged as an installable plugin. Two of them carry the rest:

- **`recipe-relay`** takes one ticket from the tracker to a reviewed pull request, ready for review, with nobody answering questions on the way. Every phase runs in its own sub-agent, every checkpoint takes its own recommendation and logs it, and the run stops only at a question with no reasonable default.
- **`open-restaurant`** is an LLM factory. Hand it a parent issue and it runs the parent's line and each sub-issue's line through `assembly-line`, in parallel across repos, then integrates the branches, QAs them as one system, writes proof and stops only at the human gates the lines name.

The other thirty-seven feed those two or stand alone. `assembly-line` runs the stages a ticket's line names, and `plan-assembly-line` suggests each ticket's line and saves it as a comment on the ticket. `plan-work` turns a feature into tickets the two can build. `feature-recipe` is the six-phase workflow the relay runs, and `evaluate-ticket`, `plan-code`, `test`, `code`, `prepare-pr` and `code-docs` are its six stages as skills of their own, and `review-fix` runs the relay's closing review and fix as a skill of its own, and `ui-review` runs its UI review as a skill of its own, and `a11y-check` runs its accessibility check as a skill of its own, and `security-review` runs its security review as a skill of its own, and `judge` runs `open-restaurant`'s readiness gate as a skill of its own, and `contract` runs its contract step as a skill of its own, and `reproduce` runs its bug reproduction step as a skill of its own, and `research` answers a spike ticket's questions as a skill of its own, and `design-gate` stops a plan that changes a schema, a migration or a public contract for a person to read as a skill of its own, and `integrate` runs its integration step as a skill of its own, and `qa` runs its QA and fix step as a skill of its own, and `proof` runs its proof step as a skill of its own, and `review-request` runs its review request as a skill of its own, and `follow-ups` opens a ticket for each item a run left open as a skill of its own, and `merge` runs its merge gate as a skill of its own. `better-code-review` reviews a diff along three axes, and `code-standards` is the catalog it reads from. `ship-pr` commits, pushes and opens a PR from the repo's template. `uml` draws UML diagrams of a codebase or a description, and `non-functional-requirements` writes and reviews NFRs. `summarize-llm-response` and `epistemic-action` check the model's own writing and reasoning before it reaches you. `work-summary` writes up a work session as a dated note, `pause-work` parks half-done work as a task for tomorrow, `weekly-planning` fits the week's tickets around your meetings, `week-summary` turns a week of those notes and your tracker, GitHub and chat activity into a review, and `setup` writes the settings file the others read their defaults from.

The same thirty-nine install into Codex, DeepSeek Harness, Pi and opencode, from the same `skills/` directory. One plugin source, five harnesses, nothing copied — so a skill cannot drift between harnesses. The one exception is opencode, which fetches a skill list over HTTP: `skills/index.json` is generated from that same tree and kept honest by `opencode/build-index.py --check`.

## Install

### Claude Code

```
/plugin marketplace add bosi-programming/skills
/plugin install bosi-programming-skills@bosi-programming
```

Then run `/reload-plugins` if the install summary asks for it.

Plugin skills are namespaced, so the commands are `/bosi-programming-skills:epistemic-action`, `/bosi-programming-skills:better-code-review`, and so on. Claude also loads them on its own when a description matches.

### Codex

```
codex plugin marketplace add bosi-programming/skills
codex plugin add bosi-programming-skills@bosi-programming
```

`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` is the manifest and `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is the catalog entry. Both keep the plugin root at the repository root, so `skills/` is what Codex reads. `codex plugin list` shows what landed.

### DeepSeek Harness

```
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:bosi-programming/skills
```

`package.json` declares `dsh.bundle`, so the install contributes exactly one layer: a row mounting `dsh/index.js`, a Cordis plugin that registers a skill provider over `skills/`. Nothing else in the profile changes, and `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` shows the layer. For a plain checkout, `DSH_BUNDLED_SKILL_DIR=<repo>/skills dsh` puts the same directory at the harness's bundled-skill root without installing anything.

### Pi

```
pi install git:github.com/bosi-programming/skills
```

`package.json` carries the Pi package manifest — a `pi` key whose `skills` entry points at `skills/` — alongside the `pi-package` keyword the gallery lists on. Pi resolves those paths against the package root, so the tree survives a git install intact. `pi list` shows the install and `pi config` toggles individual skills.

### opencode

```json
{
  "skills": {
    "urls": ["https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bosi-programming/skills/main/skills/"]
  }
}
```

opencode fetches `<url>/index.json`, then downloads each skill's files relative to `<url>/<name>/` into `~/.cache/opencode/skills/`. No checkout, no clone. The index carries a digest per skill, and opencode only refreshes a cached skill when that digest changes — so the digest moves with the files, or an edit upstream would never reach anyone who had already installed. `opencode/build-index.py` writes it; the check in "Validate a change" fails when it goes stale. Restart opencode after editing your config, and keep the global skill directories free of same-named copies.

Skills live outside your project, so an agent that denies `external_directory`
denies them too — `read` fails with `DeniedError` even though the skill is
installed. opencode evaluates the *last* matching `external_directory` rule, so
the broad deny has to come first and the skill directories after it:

```json
"external_directory": {
  "*": "deny",
  "~/.config/opencode/skills/**": "allow",
  "~/.cache/opencode/skills/**": "allow"
}
```

For a plain checkout, point opencode at the tree instead and skip the index entirely:

```json
{
  "skills": {
    "paths": ["/absolute/path/to/the/checkout/skills"]
  }
}
```

## The skills

### assembly-line

Runs a ticket's line: the ordered stages its line names. Given several tickets, it reads and validates every line first, then runs them one after another, each with its own card; a ticket that stops does not stop the queue, and one report lists each ticket's end state. It reads the local line file `assembly-line.lineFile` names (`{cardsDir}/{ticket}.line.json`) and the ticket's comments through the tracker; the file wins when both exist, else it takes the line comment created last, the one with `"format": "assembly-line/1"`. A line comment may start from a saved line with `from`, edited by `add` and `drop`, and the run uses the expanded line. It changes no stage's files, and `recipe-relay` stays until BOS-112.

How the line runs:

1. **Validate.** The line goes through `validate-line.py` before any stage runs. An invalid line, no line file and no line comment or a `{"group": "sub-issues"}` line stops the run and writes nothing; it points to `plan-assembly-line`, or to `open-restaurant`.
2. **Stages.** Each stage runs in its own sub-agent, and every checkpoint takes its own recommendation, logged to the recipe card as `line:`. `judge`, `ui-review`, `security-review` and `review-fix` run in the session, because their own steps spawn sub-agents.
3. **Cooking.** `test` and `code` in parallel run as a test writer and a code writer that never see each other's files; once both return, `prove-red.py` puts the code back as it was before the code and runs each test, logging the ones that still pass as weak; the `code` after them is the fix and taste agent.
4. **Go-backs.** A failing verdict follows the stage's `return` entry in `catalog.json`, back to the stage it names, up to its `limit`. Past it, the run stops at `needs-input` or at a human gate.
5. **Gates.** A stage with `gate: human` (`merge`, `research`, `design-gate`) stops at `runStatus: gate` with a question in chat and on the card, and runs only on the person's approval. With auto gates on, `--auto` or no argument when run on its own, each takes its own recommendation instead, logged as `line: auto-gate:`, and the sub-agent prompt carries `Auto gates: on`; `--no-auto` turns it off.
6. **Signals.** After each stage the run reads `## Signals` on the card and applies the rows in `signals.json` to the steps not yet run, through `apply-signals.py`. No approval: a row is the approval. Each change posts a line comment naming the signal, the stage that raised it and the stage added or removed; a change `validate-line.py` rejects leaves the line and is logged.
7. **Run log.** After every stage run, go-back reruns and each parallel branch included, the run appends one JSON line to `runs.jsonl` (the file `assembly-line.runLog` names) through `run-log.py`: ticket, kind, line, stage, start and end times, verdict, loops, tokens and the signal that changed the line. A failed append is logged and never stops the run.
8. **Line board.** `board.py` prints every running card in `feature-recipe.cardsDir`: each ticket's stage, how many wait at each stage, and the bottleneck, the stage with the most waiting, ties going to the longest mean time in the run log. When more than one ticket is running, each step's report names the command.
9. **Close down.** At every stop it stops the sub-agents, background shells and dev servers the line started, and logs `line: closed down` on the card. A sub-agent or shell with no new output for 30 minutes gets stopped and its stage started again once; a second stall stops the run as `blocked`.

`assembly-line.codingModel`, `assembly-line.uiReviewerModel` and `assembly-line.routineModel` pick the models; `assembly-line.reviewState` (`In Review`) and `assembly-line.doneState` (`Done`) pick the tracker states; `assembly-line.runLog` (`~/.bosi-skills/runs.jsonl`) names the file the run log goes to. The line board reads cards from `feature-recipe.cardsDir` (`./recipes`). A `## assembly-line` section in a project's `.bosi-skills.md` adds rules every sub-agent follows there; the line reads `## recipe-relay` when it has none.

### plan-assembly-line

Suggests each ticket's line and saves it as a comment on the ticket or in a local line file, in the shape `assembly-line` reads. It never runs the line.

A ticket whose body holds the line Planned with `plan-work`. has already passed `plan-work`'s readiness check, so its line drops `judge` and carries `"planned": "plan-work"`; a parent keeps `judge`.

How it plans:

1. **Read.** It reads each ticket's body and comments through the tracker. A line comment already there, the one created last, is the starting suggestion.
2. **Suggest.** It starts from the saved line that matches the ticket's kind (`feature`, `bug`, `small-fix`, `parent` or `spike`) and drops or adds stages by rule, saving it with `from`: no `test`/`code` group without a `[unit]`, `[int]`, `[e2e]` or `[story]` criterion; `ui-review` and `a11y-check` for a `## Design` link or a `[ui]` or `[story]` criterion; `code-docs` only for a `feat` title or a `[docs]` criterion. A parent gets `{"group": "sub-issues"}`, and its sub-issues join the list. A ticket whose body holds both `## Questions` and `## Output` gets `spike`, checked first, and none of the `ui-review`, `a11y-check` or `code-docs` rules apply to it. Each line comes with a short why.
3. **Run log.** `stats.py` reads the run log for tickets of the same kind and suggests to add, look at or cut a stage, each with the count behind it, from 5 runs up. The suggestions are shown, not applied.
4. **Validate.** Every line goes through `validate-line.py` before it is shown. An error names the stage and rule, and the stage to add.
5. **Approve.** One table shows every ticket. The engineer confirms or edits, and an edit is validated again. Nothing is written to the tracker before approval, and a rejected line is not saved. With `plan-assembly-line.autoApprove` (`false`) on, or `--auto`, every line the validator accepts is saved without waiting; `--no-auto` turns it off for one run.
6. **Save.** `assembly-line.lineDestination` (`ticket`) picks where: one comment per ticket, in the `line-format.md` shape, or with `file` the JSON line alone at `assembly-line.lineFile`. It never edits or deletes an old line comment.
7. **Read back.** It reads each comment back and reports any difference from the approved line, with a link per ticket.

`plan-work` calls it on its new tickets when `plan-work.role` is `engineer`. It reads the run log at `assembly-line.runLog`, and `assembly-line.lineFile` and `assembly-line.lineDestination` for where lines live.

### recipe-relay

Takes one ticket to a pull request that is open, reviewed and ready for review, without asking you anything on the way. You name the task; the session runs `feature-recipe`'s six phases, each in its own sub-agent, without changing any of the recipe's files. Each sub-agent takes the recommendation every checkpoint states — the grilling, the plan, the test list, the PR description — and logs it to the recipe card as `relay:`, so you can read afterwards what it chose and why. What reaches the chat is one line per unit, and the session starts the next unit without waiting for a reply.

How the ticket moves:

1. **`evaluate-ticket` and `plan-code`** run as one sub-agent. It turns the ticket into a plan on the recipe card and names the interfaces.
2. **Cooking** splits. For each repo, a test writer, running `test`, and a code writer work at the same time on the same branch, neither opening the other's files, so the tests cannot bend to the code. The code writer runs `code` up to its code, and, once both return, `prove-red.py` runs each new test with the code put back as it was before the code and logs the ones that still pass as weak; a last sub-agent then runs `code` again to make the tests pass and run its checks: the project's scoped tests and lint.
3. **UI review** (`ui-review`). When the change reaches a screen, a UI reviewer runs after that last sub-agent. It compares the screenshots `code` captured with the design attached to the ticket, and sends critical and major differences back for up to two more rounds.
4. **`prepare-pr`** (Plating) opens the PR ready for review, never as a draft, waits on CI and fixes it, and moves the ticket to `recipe-relay.reviewState` (`In Review` by default).
5. **Review and fix** (`review-fix`). The moment the PR opens, a sub-agent runs `better-code-review --headless` against the branch; this is the run's one review. Another sub-agent checks each finding by how it was verified — `ran`, `read` or `no` — fixes the ones that hold, test first, pushes to the open PR, and logs each one it rejects with the reason.
6. **`code-docs`** (Documentation) closes the task out and moves the ticket to `recipe-relay.doneState` (`Done` by default).

It stops only at the end, or when a sub-agent reports `blocked` or `needs-input`: a one-way door or a question with no reasonable default. Then it asks you in chat, and running it again picks the card back up where it stopped. It never merges; the PR waits for a person. It is always automatic: every unit and review prompt ends with `Auto gates: on`, so any gate stage a unit reaches takes its own recommendation. At every stop it first stops the sub-agents, background shells and dev servers it started, so no shell stays open after the run. A sub-agent or shell with no new output for 30 minutes gets stopped and its unit started again once; a second stall stops the run as `blocked`.

`recipe-relay.codingModel`, `recipe-relay.uiReviewerModel` and `recipe-relay.routineModel` pick the models for the writers, the UI reviewer, and the Plating (`prepare-pr`), Documentation (`code-docs`) and review sub-agents. A `## recipe-relay` section in a project's `.bosi-skills.md` adds rules every sub-agent follows in that project; delete the section when the project ends.

### open-restaurant

An LLM factory. Hand it a parent issue — an epic or a story with sub-issues — and it delivers every sub-issue to its own PR, then puts the parts together and proves they work as one. The parent is the order and each sub-issue a dish: this session runs the kitchen and never cooks a dish itself. It runs the parent's line and each sub-issue's line through `assembly-line`, so a ticket gets only the stages its line names. A person comes in at the gates the lines name, and nothing merges without one unless auto gates are on.

The run, in order:

1. **Lines first.** It reads the line comment of the parent and of every sub-issue, and validates each with `validate-line.py` before any card exists. A missing line, an invalid line, or a parent line with no `{"group": "sub-issues"}` stops the run and points to `plan-assembly-line`. An issue with no sub-issues runs alone through `assembly-line`.
2. **The parent's line.** It runs the stages the parent's line names through `assembly-line`, on a service card. A parent line can hold `judge` (readiness gate), `contract`, `integrate`, `qa`, `proof`, `review-request` and `merge`, in the order the line gives. At the `{"group": "sub-issues"}` step it seats and cooks the sub-issues.
3. **Cooking.** Each sub-issue runs its own line on its own recipe card, without its `merge`. A bug sub-issue's line names `reproduce`; one that does not reproduce gets a `## Blocked` comment, and nothing that depends on it starts. Sub-issues in different repos cook at the same time. Those in one repo cook one at a time in its checkout, and one blocked by another in the same repo stacks its PR on the blocker's branch. A sub-issue blocked by one in another repo starts as soon as the blocker's `plan-code` stage writes it an unblock note with the shapes it needs, not when the blocker's PR opens.
4. **Review per PR.** Each PR opens ready for review, linked to its own sub-issue, which moves to `open-restaurant.implementedState`. `review-fix` runs for each PR the moment it opens, and the findings get fixed on its branch.
5. **Integrate and QA.** Once every card ends, `integrate` lists the criteria QA proves and merges the branches into a local integration branch it never pushes. `qa` then brings up one QA env for the parent and proves each criterion with saved evidence. Failures get fixed on the owning sub-issue's branch, fast-forward only, for at most two QA rounds.
6. **Proof** (`proof`). A `## Proof` on each PR, and one on the parent with each criterion and its evidence.
7. **Review request and merge** (`review-request`, `merge`). `review-request` waits on checks and posts the PRs to `open-restaurant.reviewChannel`. `merge` stops for a person every time, unless auto gates are on, then merges in blocks order and moves the sub-issues, and the parent when no criterion is left open, to `open-restaurant.doneState`.

Auto gates. `--auto` or `--no-auto` on the run, else `open-restaurant.autoGates` (`false`), picks the mode once; the service card records it as `autoGates` and `assembly-line` and each sub-issue's line get it. When on, `design-gate`, `research`, `qa` and `merge` each take their own recommendation and log it as `auto-gate:`; `merge` approves only with every check green, no open thread and no requested change, and otherwise stops at its gate. The unfinished park, `blocked` and `needs-input` still stop the run.

Every stop writes its state to a service card next to the recipe cards; running it again on the same parent goes on from there. Before it reports a stop, it stops the sub-agents, background shells and QA env it started. A sub-agent or shell with no new output for 30 minutes gets stopped and its stage started again once.

Needs a tracker tool in the session and one repo checkout per repo in the folder it runs from. Team-specific steps (the readiness lint, QA skill, env, review groups) go in the settings file's `## open-restaurant` section; see `setup`.

### better-code-review

Reviews the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point you name, along three axes at once. Standards asks whether the code follows the repo's documented coding standards. Spec asks whether the code does what the originating issue or PRD asked for. Tests asks whether the tests in the diff are sound, and whether every behaviour the diff changes has a test that would catch it breaking. The three axes run as parallel sub-agents so none pollutes another's context. Before anything reaches you, the review checks each finding the way `epistemic-action` asks: it runs the project's scoped tests, lint and type-check, and proves each missing or tautological test with a probe, breaking the line in a throwaway worktree and watching whether any test turns red. Each finding says whether it was run, read or not verified. Then the findings render as a three-tab dark-theme HTML page that opens in your browser. With `--headless` it asks nothing, takes the merge base with the default branch when no fixed point is given, skips the Spec axis when no spec turns up and the Tests axis when there is nothing to test, and returns each finding as a plain-text block with its axis, kind, `file:line`, fix and whether it was verified, so another skill or agent can act on it. `recipe-relay` and the recipe's headless `code` stage call it this way. With `--slack <link>` it reads the PR links in one Slack message, reviews each PR headless in a fresh clone it deletes afterwards, posts missing or partial requirements, scope creep, defects and hard violations as one GitHub review with inline comments, approves a PR with none of those, and posts a short English comment in the message's thread saying whether it approved or only commented. `better-code-review.reviewMode` decides whether it installs each clone's dependencies first: `fast`, the default, skips that and lists the checks it could not run as not verified; `slow` installs them.

Based on Matt Pocock's code-review skill.

### code-standards

The standards the Standards and Tests axes check against, as five files: `Common/Clean Code.md` for naming, size, structure and immutability in any language; `Typescript/Imports.md` and `Typescript/Exports.md` for how TypeScript reaches other modules and what it publishes; `Frontend/Accessibility.md` for anything that renders in a browser; `Testing/Tests.md` for how tests are written, tautological tests included. Each file is a list of rules and the failures they prevent, closing with the red flags to catch in review.

`better-code-review` reads the catalog as its baseline and only applies the files the diff can violate. The catalog defers to the project: a standard the repo documents itself always wins, and a breach is a hard violation only where the repo documents the same rule — otherwise it is a judgement call, like any smell. It is a reference rather than a workflow, so there is nothing here to run.

### feature-recipe

Takes a task from a rough idea to a merged PR, cooked in six named stages — `evaluate-ticket`, `plan-code`, `test`, `code`, `prepare-pr`, `code-docs` — most defaulting to a fresh context and handing the next one its work through a **recipe card**, a markdown file at `./recipes/{task-slug}.md` in the project being worked on (`evaluate-ticket` and `test` continue straight through instead, without a session break). `evaluate-ticket` and `plan-code` are where you and the skill agree on what is being built and why; `evaluate-ticket` runs `grill-me` only when the work is complex or leaves something undefined, and skips it for simple, fully stated work; `test` writes every mapped test and sees it fail before any code, and `code` makes them pass, commits as it goes, then holds a hard gate that runs `better-code-review` plus the project's own scoped tests and lint before anything opens; `prepare-pr` opens at most one PR per run and never stacks them unless a driver names a base branch; `code-docs` closes the task out.

It carries no opinion about which tracker, chat or docs tool a project uses — it speaks in outcomes and leans on whatever the session already has.

Phases 1 to 6 can also run **headless** — a night run. Start one with `--headless` at whatever step the card is on, even a bare task with no card yet, and it carries the work through `evaluate-ticket`, `plan-code`, `test`, `code`, `prepare-pr` and `code-docs` in one turn, taking the recommendation at each checkpoint and recording it as `unattended:` so the morning can see what was decided while nobody was watching. It stops only at the end of the recipe or when something needs a person — never merely because a phase ended — and it never opens a non-draft PR, merges, or deletes work. The run's result goes on the card as `runStatus`, `runNext` and `runQuestion` in the frontmatter, so a driver reads a file at a known path instead of parsing prose — prose gets fenced, glued to a heading, or turned into a question. The contract is `skills/feature-recipe/references/headless.md`.

### evaluate-ticket

The first build stage, once `feature-recipe`'s Reading the Recipe. It loads the task, decides whether the work is complex or leaves something undefined, runs `grill-me` only then, and writes the work card's `## Problem` and `## Goal & measure`. It takes the path to a work card; with no card it runs `feature-recipe`'s Phase 0 to find or make one. It writes `evaluate-ticket` to the card's `phase` and `phasesCompleted`, so `feature-recipe`, `recipe-relay` or a person can run it alone, for instance to redo this stage on a card. Cards from before the split, with `reading-the-recipe` in `phase` or `phase-1-reading-the-recipe.md` in `runNext`, still route here.

It is the first stage to declare a `stage.json`: what it takes from the card, what it delivers, where the line goes back to when it fails, and its gate. `skills/assembly-line/references/stage-spec.md` defines the keys.

### plan-code

The second build stage, once `feature-recipe`'s Mise en Place. It reads the work card's `## Problem`, drafts `## Solution`, `## Implementation Plan`, `## Acceptance Criteria` and `## Testing Strategy`, lists the test cases in `## TDD Test Mapping`, and names the public interfaces both a test writer and a code writer code to in `## Interfaces`. It takes the path to a work card; with no card it runs `feature-recipe`'s Phase 0 to find or make one. It writes `plan-code` to the card's `phase` and `phasesCompleted`, so `feature-recipe`, `recipe-relay` or a person can run it alone, for instance to redo this stage on a card. Cards from before the split, with `mise-en-place` in `phase` or `phase-2-mise-en-place.md` in `runNext`, still route here.

Its `stage.json` has the same shape as `evaluate-ticket`'s.

### test

The build stage after `plan-code`, once the test half of `feature-recipe`'s Cooking. It reads the work card's `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Testing Strategy`, `## TDD Test Mapping` and `## Interfaces`, writes every mapped test before any code, runs them and confirms they fail, and marks each case written. It never opens a code file the plan names, so the tests cannot bend to the code. It takes the path to a work card; with no card it runs `feature-recipe`'s Phase 0 to find or make one. It writes `test` to the card's `phase` and `phasesCompleted`, so `feature-recipe`, `recipe-relay` or a person can run it alone, for instance to redo this stage on a card. In `recipe-relay` it is the test writer of Cooking in parallel. Cards from before the split, with `mise-en-place` or `plan-code` as the last phase, or `phase-3-cooking.md` in `runNext` and no `test` in `phasesCompleted`, route here.

Its `stage.json` has the same shape as `evaluate-ticket`'s.

### code

The build stage after `test`, once the rest of `feature-recipe`'s Cooking and all of its Tasting. It reads the work card's `## Solution`, `## Implementation Plan` and `## Interfaces`, writes the code to the tests `test` wrote, runs them and fixes the code until they pass, then holds a hard gate: `better-code-review` plus the project's own scoped tests, lint and type-check, fixed until each passes or is honestly deferred to CI, all written to `## Quality Gate Results`. It takes the path to a work card; with no card it runs `feature-recipe`'s Phase 0 to find or make one. It writes `code` to the card's `phase` and `phasesCompleted`, so `feature-recipe`, `recipe-relay` or a person can run it alone, for instance to redo this stage on a card. In `recipe-relay` it is both the code writer of Cooking in parallel, which stops once the code is written and never opens a test file, and the fix and taste step after it. Cards from before the split, with `test` or `cooking` as the last phase, or `phase-4-tasting.md` in `runNext`, route here.

Its `stage.json` has the same shape as `evaluate-ticket`'s, and raises `no-screen-change` when the change touches no surface a person sees.

### prepare-pr

The build stage after `code`. It reads the work card and the commits on the branch, decides the PR delivery strategy in `## PR Delivery Strategy`, opens the PR, attaches screenshots, waits on CI, and records `## PR`, `status` and `prUrl`. It takes the path to a work card; with no card it runs `feature-recipe`'s Phase 0 to find or make one. It writes `prepare-pr` to the card's `phase` and `phasesCompleted`, so `feature-recipe`, `recipe-relay` or a person can run it alone, for instance to redo the stage on a card. Cards from before the split, with `plating` in `phase` or `phase-5-plating.md` in `runNext`, still route here.

Its `stage.json` has the same shape as `evaluate-ticket`'s.

### code-docs

The last stage, after `prepare-pr`. It asks whether the change is worth documenting, writes the docs where the team

fullManifest.name: @corvus-dsh/dsh-graft-slice

# dsh-graft-slice

<!-- INSTALL:BEGIN -->
## 安装

两条路都可用。**按你需要选一条**，不要混装同一插件。

## 路线 A：npm registry（beta 通道）

四个包都发布在 `@corvus-dsh/*` 作用域下，当前通道是 **beta**：

```bash
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise@beta
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-memory@beta
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-graft-slice@beta
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-observer@beta
```

先确认 registry 上是哪一版：

```bash
npm view @corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise@beta version
```

## 路线 B：GitHub 直装

```bash
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-memory
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-graft-slice
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-observer
```

## 两条路的区别（选之前先读这三行）

| | registry（路线 A） | GitHub 直装（路线 B） |
|---|---|---|
| 拿到的是什么 | **已发布、已固化**的产物 | **仓库当前状态**（可能含未发布提交） |
| 复现某版本 | 可以：`@corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise@0.9.1-beta.1` | 不可以（要 checkout 对应 tag 再装） |
| 适合 | 部署、回归、报 bug 时给出确切版本 | 跟进最新修复、本地开发 |

**顺序有意义**：`dsh-paradise` 是内核，其余三个都依赖它提供的协议。先装内核，后装业务插件。

## 装完确认

```bash
dsh plugin list
```

应该看到四行，`fiberPhase` 都是 `active`：

```
include:dsh-paradise       dsh-paradise        active
include:dsh-graft-slice    dsh-graft-slice     active
include:dsh-memory         dsh-memory          active
include:dsh-observer       dsh-observer        active
```

如果某个是 `null` 或显示「异常」，看宿主日志里该包的启动错误——最常见的原因是 Node 版本低于 22.5。

## 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin remove dsh-observer
dsh plugin remove dsh-graft-slice
dsh plugin remove dsh-memory
dsh plugin remove dsh-paradise
```

## 从源码运行（不装插件）

如果只是想跑独立宿主和 Web UI，不需要 DSH：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise
cd dsh-paradise
node dist/harness-server.js
# 浏览器打开 http://127.0.0.1:38080
```

详见《星火 OS 独立运行指南》。

## 要求

| 项 | 版本 |
|---|---|
| Node | ≥ 22.5.0（`node:sqlite` 需要） |
| DSH | ≥ 0.2.1-rc.5 |
| 外部依赖 | **零**。全部只用 Node 内置模块 |

## 为什么包名带作用域

npm 上的**裸名** `dsh-memory` 和 `dsh-observer` 已被第三方注册，包内容与我们无关。
我们不愿为一个名字支付赎金，也不愿让用户装到别人的包，所以改用作用域命名
（`@corvus-dsh/*`）——**请始终用带作用域的名字**，裸名指向的不是本项目的包。
<!-- INSTALL:END -->


> **里程碑 `v0.9.0-freeze`（2026-11-05）** —— 本项目已进入架构冻结点，用于沉淀副脑插件的前置重构成果。
>
> **核心功能**：在源会话最后一个 `turn/end` 处切取高保真磁带，生成零继承、可冷恢复的交接会话；不 fork、不引入 SQLite、不单独注入 `tool/result`。转生后广播 `graft/session-transferred`，由旁路插件自行决定是否跟随。
>
> **v1.3 重构时**（historical）：`src/index.ts` 14,354 → 13,425 行，抽出 5 个内联模块（`utils/serialize`、`utils/logger`、`core/ledger`、`core/watermark`、`core/txn`），行为不变、545 → 542 条测试全绿；6 条副脑测试随代码迁往 `dsh-observer`。
> **现状**（0.9.1-beta.1）：**13,271 行 / 12,742 非空**；测试 **591**（`check-docs` 实时校验）。
>
> **已知结构性限制**：宿主 `commands.execute` 是广播语义（每次调用必留一行）；第三方客户端没有插件自有 Remote。因此副脑类功能不能靠「客户端命令 + UI 按钮」实现，只能由模型工具或宿主侧动作触发 —— 详见 [副脑插件架构复盘与底层缺陷报告](https://github.com/corvus-dsh/dsh-observer) 同期的复盘文档。
> 兄弟项目：[dsh-memory](https://github.com/corvus-dsh/dsh-memory) —— 能力记忆（SKILL.md / 负知识），与本插件只通过台账文件耦合。

**DSH 日志切片与最小注入插件。** 在源会话最后一个 `turn/end` 处切取高保真磁带，创建一个零继承、可冷恢复的交接会话；不 fork，不引入 SQLite，不单独注入 `tool/result`。

> 当前版本见 `package.json`（语义化版本从 0 起；能力线见本文各版本小节）。
> 发布说明：[RELEASE_NOTES.md](./RELEASE_NOTES.md)（v0.8.1 归档见 [RELEASE_NOTES-v0.8.1.md](./RELEASE_NOTES-v0.8.1.md)）。
> 目标运行时：DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.5**（当前桌面端）。
> 规格书 v2.1 写的是 rc.4；本实现已按 rc.5 的真实源码校正了两处会导致冷恢复失败的问题。

## 愿景：事实记忆只需可查，能力记忆才需要持久化

上下文窗口会腐蚀：窗口越长，注意力越散，结论越容易被自己的历史淹没。所以这个生态不打算把所有东西塞进一个窗口，
而是把「记忆」拆成两类，按**不同的成本**分别对待：

| 记忆 | 需要什么 | 承担者 |
|---|---|---|
| **事实记忆**：做过什么、当时的原文、工具输出 | **只需可查** | 会话日志 + 按 seq 回读（`graft_read_result` / `graft_search_history`），不重放、不摘要 |
| **能力记忆**：怎么做才对、踩过哪些坑、有效方法 | **必须持久化** | 记忆系统插件：记忆的存储与转化，长期记忆与能力飞轮的基础设施 |

**持久化能力层**由三件插件组成：

| 插件 | 职责 |
|---|---|
| **嫁接切片插件**（本仓库 `dsh-graft-slice`） | **工作能力连续性**：在上下文爆掉之前换一个干净窗口，摆脱上下文腐蚀、重置注意力；切片 / 两阶段审核 / 崩溃可恢复 |
| **记忆系统插件**（规划中） | **记忆的存储与转化**：把做过的事沉淀成可复用的能力，作为长期记忆与能力飞轮的基础设施 |
| **副会话插件**（规划中） | **隔离用户消息**：为主会话提供专业、具体的方案，并维护记忆系统 |

三者共享的硬约束：不 fork、不改写源日志、只追加、每个指针都能被 `graft_read_result` 打开；
迁移不能带走现场——`.txn/` 写前日志 + 幂等恢复，任何时刻 `sourceUsable ∨ targetUsable`。

本项目是 **DSH 开源生态**的一部分：GitHub topics 标 `dsh-plugin`，发布以预发布（prerelease）先行。
### 真机自我切片（本项目第一次）

| 项 | 数值 |
|---|---|
| 源会话 | 48 轮 / 14,978 事件 / 9.5 MB 压缩日志 |
| 交接注入 | **14,252 字符**（system 1,125 + 磁带 13,127），源的 0.15% |
| 磁带结构 | 1 轮封闭骨架 + 8 个回顾块（goal / task-status / workspace / carryover / readback / pending …） |
| 断点 | `open-turn-carryover` 370 字符（Turn 47，进行中）+ `recent-turn` 5,889 字符（Turn 46 全文） |
| 回读 | 指针 1,860 处；可回读索引 1,982 条 |
| 结果 | 新会话**零澄清提问**接上工作，并自行发现 pending 与断点的矛盾 |

## 安装与准入校验

本插件是 **DSH bundle**：加载器只认 `package.json` 里的 `dsh.bundle.patch`，普通依赖会被静默忽略。

```bash
# 用户安装（dsh CLI）
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-graft-slice
dsh --profile <name> --dump-config        # 配置树里应出现 dsh-graft-slice 条目
```

仓库自带的契约校验器（不依赖 dsh CLI，可在 CI 里跑）：

```bash
node scripts/verify-bundle.mjs   # 28 项：bundle 声明 / files 白名单 / ESM / manifest 一致 / patch 形状 / 来源审计 / 导出面契约 / 脱敏
```

三条高频致命错误，本仓库都用校验器兜住：

| 错误 | 后果 | 本仓库 |
|---|---|---|
| 只声明 `main`/`exports`，漏 `dsh.bundle` | 被当成普通依赖，静默不激活 | `dsh.bundle.patch` 已声明并校验 |
| `files` 漏 `cordis.patch.yml` | 装上了但没有配置层，挂载失败 | 白名单含 patch + `index.js` + `manifest.json` |
| 未设 `type: "module"` | CJS 引 ESM 核心包，启动即崩 | `type: "module"` 已校验 |

`cordis.patch.yml` 用**包名**引用（`name: dsh-graft-slice`），不写相对路径——相对路径只在本机成立。

## v0.22.0：跨仓布局契约（`LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED`）与客户端载荷守卫

**测试专用出口（批次 3 第 1 组）：** 入口导出 185 个名字，按形状算 seam 的 13 个，其中 10 个是测试专用。
这里锁**子集**而不是全量，标准写明并按比例执行：入口小到能读完就锁全量（observer 16、memory 31），
入口是巨石就锁 seam 形状子集。`test/v103-seam-inventory.test.mjs` 断言任何 seam 形状的导出都必须已登记，
并逐个断言仍可调用——**新增 seam 必须是有意动作**。

**一个不是 seam 的反例（这条最值得读）：** `scanAgentCommand` 看着像测试专用，其实**不是**——
`scripts/check-docs.mjs` 引用它、README 也点名它，它是**文档门禁的契约**。把它当"只给测试用"删掉会让
文档检查器变红。测试里有一条专门的断言把这个区别钉住（不能把它登记进 seam 清单）。

**待第 2 组删除的三个 seam：** `debugLastLockCleanup` / `debugLastRecovery` / `debugStorePaths`（**完全无消费者**）。
删它们时必须同步改清单测试——这正是清单锁存在的意义。

- **`.layout.json`（P1-2）**：本插件在台账目录写入 `{layout: 1, producer: 'dsh-graft-slice',
  files: ['.retired.json', '.transferred.json']}`；读取 `dsh-memory` 的存储目录前先校验它的 `.layout.json`
  （memory 侧在激活时写入）。读到不认识的 `layout` → **拒读**并报 `LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED`；调试面板给出
  `available: false` + 原因，而不是一份看起来"没有记忆"的零计数。缺失标记 = 旧目录，**继续读**。
- **为什么已经有 epoch 还需要它**：epoch 覆盖的是文件**内容**格式。四个按名字读的文件一旦被改名，
  读取端一律降级为 `[]`——与"这个工作区什么都没记"同形，静默的零而不是错误。
- **`api-session/added` 载荷守卫（P1-3）**：冷目标与归档 fork 的会话通告是本插件自己 emit 的（宿主只为
  已发布会话发这个事件），而宿主的 `assertJsonArgs` 只校验可序列化、**不校验 `sessionId` 是字符串**。
  两个发出点在 emit 前一律过 `assertSessionSummary`：不合格就记 warning 并跳过，绝不发一个对方的
  `resources.session` 读不出 key 的载荷。

## v0.20.0：交接任务看板（Task Board）

v0.19 蒸馏得对，但**渲染成了一段话**。读散文的模型必须自己推导"哪些做完了 / 哪些在跑 / 哪些没开始"，
而这一步推导正是恢复的会话开始重做已完成工作的入口。看板把四列**写明**：

```
## 交接任务看板（第一轮只要读这里）
**原始用户要求**：把两个插件升级到 v0.20 并跑通全量测试

**✅ 已完成**
- git commit abc1234 成功（seq=88）

**🔄 进行中**
- 正在改 retrieve.ts 的任务对齐过滤

**⏭️ 待开始**
- 提交并推送两个仓库
```

- **「🔄 进行中」是 v0.19 缺的那一列**：断点落在开放轮次时，那里的工作既不是"已完成"（还没有结果），
  也不是"待开始"（已经开工）。并进「待开始」会让目标重做，并进「已完成」会让它以为已落地。它取自开放轮次
  **自己的**未执行指令，与 `open-turn-carryover` 共用同一提取器，两者不会互相矛盾。
- **空列要声明**：缺失的列读作"未知"，显式 `- 无` 读作"确实还没有"——两条不同的指令。
- **发 seq 就点名读它的工具**：`graft_read_result` / `graft_search_history` 那一行补在停泊点之后，
  否则目标手里只有坐标、没有用法。
- **正文不再整段搬运**：散文的"我接下来需要 X"被**移进**「⏭️ 待开始」（模型没写 todo 时它就是唯一计划）；
  排除项与回读提示保留为注记；其余判重丢弃——看板复述自己只会更长，不会更清楚。
- **尾部规则常驻**：`旧会话的历史执行日志和临时错误无需理会……请直接执行上面「⏭️ 待开始」里的待办项。`
  同一句话也写进点火 Prompt：一次性消息会过期，常驻块才是长期规则。

## v0.19.0：切片极限瘦身 + 物理点火（最后两块拼图）

前两个版本让交接**正确**；这一版让它**干净**并且**自己会跑**。

### 1. 语义状态提取（不再搬运旧房子的报错）

`open-turn-carryover` 以前把开放轮次「基本原样」搬过去：助手叙述逐字、指针逐行，加上
`renderLastStepScene` 里那条**完整报错正文**（上限 2000 字符的栈回溯）。这是目标既不能执行、
也不能验证的最大一块文本，而且它把旧会话的问题带进新上下文——**新会话开局先修一个早就修好的东西**。

现在只提炼两件事 + 一个指针，构成一张**指令卡**：

```
## 交接指令卡（第一轮只要读这里）
【最终结果】git commit e8da8f6 成功（seq=14821）
【未决报错】pwsh 失败：Cannot find module 'left-pad'（原文 seq=14903）   ← 只有未解决的才有这一行
我接下来需要 …
【停泊点】Turn 47 已完成 · 边界 seq=14950 · 可回读指针 340 处 · sourceSessionId=…
【已按语义瘦身】丢弃：2 条已解决的报错、1 段报错正文、812 字符中间叙述；需要时按 seq 回读原文。
```

- **最终结果**：`git commit <sha> 成功` / `git push 成功（main）` / `测试 N 通过` / `写入 <file> 完成`，
  每种都带 `seq`，所以它是**可核对**的声明而不是一句总结；
- **已解决的冲突/报错强制丢弃**：扫描自新到旧，遇到第一个成功就停；比它更早的失败都算已被覆盖
  （计入 `resolvedErrors`，**不进新上下文**）；
- **唯一例外**：一直没有被后续成功覆盖的那条报错，保留**一行**（正文 160 字符 + seq），因为它是
  **下一步的阻塞**，属于「未执行的下一步」的一部分；
- **丢弃必须声明**：`【已按语义瘦身】` 列出丢了什么。静默删除是这套系统一贯要避免的失效模式；
- **指针坐标保留**：`（本轮过程指针：seq=9,15,23；正文按 seq 回读）`——散文丢了，可达性没丢，
  「每个结论都有 seq 可开」这条契约不变；
- **点火指令不算人类约束**：`extractConstraints` 跳过带 `[dsh-graft-slice 点火]` 标记的消息。
  它是以真实 `user/message` 投递的，按来源看像人话，但它是我们写的引导语；把它当硬约束传下去，
  下一代就会把「继续执行任务」当成人亲口声明的规则。

### 2. 物理点火（新会话自己开跑）

在此之前，每个版本产出的目标都是**正确但静止**的：目标拿着 goal、磁带、指令卡和约束，然后**等人点它**。
而它替换掉的源会话已经被退休——**交接成功的那一刻，工作停了**。插件自己写的
`selfSliceBootstrap`（「无需等待用户确认」）只是一句写给目标的话，而没人启动的目标收不到任何话。

宿主有这个通道：`sessionController.prompt(request, signal)` ——「Admit one prompt after explicitly
resuming its Session」。它正是 Web 输入框走的那条路，会**从持久化里冷恢复**会话，所以它也是插件让
冷目标跑起来的正规接口。`graft_slice_and_inject` 在 `handle.flush()` **之后**、退休事务提交**之后**
调用它一次，往目标投递：

```
[dsh-graft-slice 点火] 你刚刚完成了一次物理切片：上一段会话的上下文已经交接给你…
```

幂等与诚实：

| 情形 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| 通道存在、接受 | `ignition.ok=true`，记录 `channel`，清空队列 |
| 通道缺失 | `attempted=false` + 原因；**迁移仍然成功**；意图落盘排队重试 |
| 调用抛错/超时（20s） | `ok=false` + 原因；**不回溯迁移**；同样排队重试 |
| 目标日志里已有点火消息 | `alreadyIgnited=true`，**不再投递**——重复投递会让目标把同一句话读成两轮用户意图 |
| 连续失败 3 次 | 放弃并审计 `ignite-failed`（目标仍在，可人工打开） |

队列文件 `<dataDir>/.graft-pending-ignition.json`，`apply()` 末尾 `resumePendingIgnitions()` 消费；
审计线记 `ignite` / `ignite-failed` / `ignite-skipped`。控制台新增「物理点火」卡片：开关、投递方式
（`queue` / `steer`）、以及**未点火会话列表**（含重试次数）。

### 3. 补正：`ask` 走真正的审批通道（v0.18 的权宜之计被替换）

v0.18 把 `autonomous` 下的 ask 写成「拒绝 + 让 agent 自己去要确认」。核对宿主契约后这不该由模型代劳：

| 通道 | 能表达 | 性质 |
|---|---|---|
| `tools.guard()` | 只能返回拒绝字符串 | **单调**：没有 guard 能推翻另一个 guard 的拒绝 |
| `tools/pre-execute`（瀑布） | `allow / deny / cancel / ask(reason, displayReason)` | 可被下游覆盖，但**缺少审批支持时 `ask` 自动降级为拒绝**（天然 fail-closed） |

所以两个决策各走各的通道：**`deny` 走 guard**（要它无法被撤销），**`ask` 走瀑布**（要真的弹给用户）。
顺序上 guard 在瀑布之后，因此 `deny` 仍然压过 `ask`——更严的判定存活。

## v0.18.0：风险与策略分离、动态水位、硬约束零丢失、台账 epoch

审计的判词是「字符串防御」：`scanAgentCommand` 同时干了两件事——判定命令**是什么**（证据，正则擅长）
和决定**拦不拦**（策略，该由一张操作员能读能改的表决定）。这一个版本把四件事分开焊死。

### 1. 风险（evidence）与策略（policy）分离

- `classifyAgentCommand(command, workspace)` → `risk: safe | unknown | destructive`，**只给等级，不给裁决**；
- `policyDecision(risk, mode)` → 决策表，一处可读：

| risk | `strict` | `balanced`（默认） | `autonomous` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `safe` | allow | allow | allow |
| `unknown` | deny | deny | allow |
| `destructive` | deny | deny | **ask** |

`unknown` 是"无法证明它被限制在工作区内"的变更类命令。`destructive` 在 `autonomous` 变成 **ask 而不是
allow**：模式可以降低仪式感，但**没有任何模式会静默执行无界删除**。`tools.guard()` 是同步的、只有"拒绝"
一个返回通道，所以 ask 表达为**指名确认步骤的拒绝**：调用不执行，并告诉 agent 先把确切命令与影响交给用户确认。

审计线区分 `command-blocked` 与 `command-asked`。

### 2. 动态水位（写死的 0.70 / 0.75 退休）

```text
estimateGraftCost(window) = fixed(6000) + package(窗口的一半字符 / 4) + growthPerTurn × growthReserveTurns
safeCeiling = 1 - estimatedGraftCost / windowLimit
hardAt      = clamp(safeCeiling, 0.50, 0.75)      # 0.75 = 历史实测的"最晚可切点"，是天花板
warnAt      = hardAt - 0.05                        # 永远留出模型自救的窗口
```

- 大窗口（128k）：估价装得下 → 仍然 0.75 / 0.70（**不回归**，写成断言）；
- 小窗口（32k）：`hardAt = 0.6125`，**比旧的 0.75 更早切**；
- 2.6k 这种装不下一次交接的窗口：`feasible: false` 明确报出来（面板/调试面板都显示），而不是切在 50% 装作没事；
- `growthTokensPerTurn` 就是"工具长尾"的增长预测（默认 1200 tok/轮）；
- `watermarkMode: 'fixed'` 原样恢复两个常量——它就是给差分测试用的。

### 3. HARD CONSTRAINTS 零丢失

旧选择器是 `candidates.slice(0, 8)` + 8000 字符 `break`，两者都**静默**：第 9 条规则不进目标，没人知道。
现在按**容量**打包（`constraintBudgetChars`，默认 8000），逐条不截断；装不下的规则进入 `dropped` 报告，
`assertConstraintsPreserved()` 直接抛 `GRAFT_ABORTED: constraints truncated`——**缩水的规则集不上路**。
`buildInjectionPlan` 是所有路径（prepare / commit / auto）的唯一收口，所以没有构建器能绕过。
能返回的计划都带 `constraintIntegrity`（budgetChars / totalChars / kept / candidateCount / dropped: 0）作为正向证据。

### 4. 台账 epoch（跨进程防撕裂）

`.retired.json` / `.transferred.json` 现在写成信封 `{epoch, at, pid, payload}`。读取端四种结局：
无信封（epoch 1，v0.17 的旧形状，**继续读**，并在下一次写入时就地升级）、`epoch == 2` 信任、
`epoch > 2` **拒读并等下一次重试**、信封缺 payload **拒读**。`dsh-memory` 侧同样实现，且：
`memory_migrate_evidence` 在台账被拒时**不再猜"最新会话"**，harvest 报告里带 `ledger.deferred` 说明原因。

## v0.17.0：宿主噪音过滤（tape 不再携带别人的机器路径）

审计发现：tape 里带着**源会话所在机器**的路径（`C:\Users\<user>\AppData\...`、`/home/...`、`/tmp/...`），
以及整盘扫描命令的输出。红线告诉模型不要去那里；`stripHostNoise()` 不再把路指给它。

三条规则，全部在 `buildInjectionPlan` 的**单一收口处**执行，所以每个 chunk 都被覆盖：

1. 只含宿主路径的段落 → 整段替换为 `[宿主环境噪音，已过滤]`（**声明式省略**，绝不静默删除——静默删除正是
   逐轮预算规则存在的理由）；
2. 同时含宿主路径与项目路径的段落 → 保留项目内容，只把宿主 token 换成 `[宿主路径已过滤]`
   （丢掉整段会丢掉真实工作）；
3. 全盘扫描命令的输出（`Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse`、`rg /`、`find /`…）若不包含项目内路径 →
   `[命令输出已折叠]`；工作区内部的搜索原样保留。

`renderWorkspaceState()` 同样过滤：产物索引里出现宿主路径，等于告诉目标"这是你的工作区文件"。

**验收测试**：往日志的 assistant 结论与 tool/result 里塞 `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\...\logs`，
切片后目标会话里**不再出现该路径**，且省略处有显式标记（6 项测试，含工作区索引那一路）。

## v0.16.0：Web 控制台（不再手改配置 + 不再重启）

在此之前，改一个开关意味着：找到 `cordis.patch.yml` → 改 YAML → 重启宿主 → 丢掉当前会话。结果是**这些开关
在实战里等于冻结**。现在有两个面板（本插件一个、`dsh-memory` 一个），从侧栏进入：

| 面板 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| **转生控制台** | `modelDrivenGraft` / `autoGraft` 开关；`modelDrivenGraftAtRatio` / `autoGraftAtRatio` 滑条+输入框；护栏开关（`workspaceRedline` / `commandGuard`）；**实时水位表**（每个活动会话的 token 用量、百分比、距 70% 与 75% 还差多少 token、第几代迁移、是否在 grace 保护期内） |
| **记忆控制台** | 由 `dsh-memory` 提供：`retrieval` / `workspaceIsolation` / `semanticFilter` 开关、按 scene 过滤的技能清单、一键清空当前工作区记忆 |

### 为什么这需要一个新的写入路径

面板不能把值写进插件内存里——那样重启就丢，等于换个地方手改。所以两个面板都走宿主的
**`configEditor.edit(entry, change)`**：找到自己那一行（`patchId: 'dsh-graft-slice'`），在 `current` 之上
spread 一个键，宿主完成校验、落盘与 Loader 调和。**值写进的就是 profile 配置本身**，因此既无需重启、
也能活过重启。

同样的操作还注册成**命令**（`/graft-console`、`/graft-console-set modelDrivenGraftAtRatio 0.70`）。
UI 与命令共用一份实现，而且在客户端 bundle 尚未加载时，命令是立刻可用的退路。

### 已验证 / 未验证（如实标注）

- ✅ **宿主侧逻辑**：6 项新测试覆盖取值白名单（拒绝 `0` 与 `≥1` 的水位，而不是静默 clamp）、
  patch 合并保留未管理键、写入目标是**自己那一行**、`configEditor` 缺失时**报错而不是假装保存**。
- ✅ **面板与命令同源**：命令 handler 直接调用与面板相同的函数。
- ⚠️ **页面内的按钮点击**：客户端→宿主调用的**客户端侧参数形状**无法从 bundle 里确证（各宿主版本不同）。
  因此桥接层按顺序尝试若干形状，并把**实际生效的通道名**显示在面板顶部；全都失败时它给出确切要输入的命令，
  而不是一个永远转圈的按钮。
- ⚠️ **需要一次宿主重启 + 一次页面刷新**：`dsh.client` 是宿主动态扫描的字段，而客户端半边是**新加**的，
  宿主要重新扫描才会把它放进 boot graph（之后改面板代码只需刷新页面，改配置则完全不用重启）。

  以及 memory 侧承载的 D3 工作区硬隔离 / D4 注入前防污染 / D7 一次性约束过滤）+ `graft_debug_status` 调试面板。
  详见下面 v0.14.0 与 v0.13.0 两节。
- **memory 侧**：双时态记忆（`valid_at` / `invalid_at` / `superseded_by`）、取代裁决（LLM 判定 → 互链 → 审计
  `.memory-audit.jsonl`，且 `human` 来源不可被推断失效）、来源分级（`human` / `tool` / `inferred`，
  非 human 的提示带 `[来源：工具推断，请核实]`）。
