evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @filipeesch/dsh-design-bundle

Installable DSH bundle for the design plugin. The bundle ships the host service,
the preset-scoped design tools and auto-validation, the design preset
registration, the embedded client contribution, and the built renderer.

Install with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<checkout>/packages/bundle`
after `pnpm run build` in this repository. See the repository README for
install, update, and removal.

# dsh-design

The design plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It lets an agent sketch a
clickable, responsive web app in a restricted JSX-style DSL, preview it live in
the browser, and iterate with validation feedback attached to every edit.

This repository implements the `add-design-foundation`,
`add-design-journeys-and-checks`, `add-design-panel-and-comments`,
`add-design-variants`, `anchor-design-comment-composer`, and
`add-design-handoff` OpenSpec changes. The plugin is developed here,
outside the DSH source tree, and installed into a DSH profile with `dsh plugin`.

## Requirements

- DSH `>=0.2.2-rc.3 <0.3.0` with plugin installation enabled.
- For building from source: Node.js 24.9 or newer and pnpm 11.
- Optional: a Playwright Chromium for headless journeys, lint, layout snapshots,
  and screenshots. Preview and static tools work without one.

## Build

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build
pnpm run test
pnpm run check   # build, lint, format, EOF-newline check, tests
# real Chromium regressions run when a Playwright browser is available; otherwise they skip
# install the matching browser for the full suite:
pnpm exec playwright install chromium
```

## Install

### From a GitHub Release

Releases publish a prebuilt bundle. The DSH installer handles package
installation; there is no source checkout, local build, or plugin build-script
approval.

Paste this stable URL into the DSH plugin installer:

```text
https://github.com/filipeesch/dsh-design/releases/latest/download/dsh-design-bundle.tgz
```

After installation, select **Enable now** if offered, then restart the
profile if DSH prompts. The optional CLI equivalent is:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/filipeesch/dsh-design/releases/latest/download/dsh-design-bundle.tgz
```

The latest URL always serves the current latest stable release and is mutable.
For a fixed version, use the version-specific asset URL; this is v0.1.0:

```text
https://github.com/filipeesch/dsh-design/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-design-bundle.tgz
```

Each release also publishes `dsh-design-bundle.tgz.sha256`. Releases do not
update an installed profile automatically. Pin the version URL when you need the
same bytes later, and follow [Update](#update) to move to a newer release.

Do not paste the repository URL. It selects this monorepo root
(`@filipeesch/dsh-design-workspace`), not the installable bundle. If you already
did, see [Remove](#remove).

### From a local checkout

Build first: the bundle serves the built renderer, fonts, and client files.

Linked development checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:<checkout>/packages/bundle
```

Reproducible local artifact (works from a fresh clone after `pnpm install`):

```sh
pnpm run pack:bundle
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <checkout>/dist/filipeesch-dsh-design-bundle-0.1.0.tgz
```

Either local route installs the same built bundle; the tarball does not require
the profile to see the source checkout. Restart DSH after installing. The
profile then lists the **Design** agent preset, and the preview route answers
under `/design/<session-id>/` on the DSH web server. Opening a design session
gives the agent `design_init`, `design_status`, `design_validate`,
`design_view` (including measured layout), `design_catalog`,
`design_run_journey`, `design_lint`, `design_screenshot`, `design_query`,
`design_diff`, and `design_handoff`.

Maintainer release steps and the asset contract are in
[`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md).

Live capture of external development applications is deferred and is not
included in this bundle. Preview and handoff operate on local design sources.

A session whose working directory contains `design/design.json` gets a live
preview. The agent shares the URL from `design_status`; open it in a normal
browser tab while signed in to DSH, or use the native **Design** action in the
session header to place the same preview beside the conversation.

## Update

Release installs are explicit and never automatic. Remove the installed bundle,
then install the version-specific asset URL for the target release:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @filipeesch/dsh-design-bundle
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add 'https://github.com/filipeesch/dsh-design/releases/download/<tag>/dsh-design-bundle.tgz'
```

Replace `<tag>` with the new release tag (for example, `v0.1.0`).

Remove and reinstall instead of reinstalling the mutable latest URL in place:
this avoids a cached resolution of the same URL and keeps the installed version
explicit. Use the latest URL only for a deliberate fresh install. Restart DSH
after the reinstall.

For a linked development checkout, rebuild instead:

```sh
pnpm run build
```

The linked bundle picks up the new `lib/` output on the next DSH start. No
profile reinstall is needed for code changes; reinstall only if the bundle
manifest or patch changes.

## Remove

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @filipeesch/dsh-design-bundle
```

Restart DSH. The preset, tools, route, and client contribution are gone; DSH
starts normally. Design folders in target repositories stay as plain files.

If you previously pasted the repository URL, DSH installed the monorepo root
instead of the bundle. Remove that entry by its recorded package name, then
install the release asset:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @filipeesch/dsh-design-workspace
```

If the profile lists a different name for the incorrect entry, remove exactly
that name. Neither command deletes the checkout or design folders.

## Packages

| Package    | Role                                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `core`     | Design tree, parser, validator, tokens, project loading, scaffolding, view projection |
| `kit`      | Component metadata and React components                                               |
| `renderer` | Standalone preview app (chrome, interpreter, live reload, state)                      |
| `host`     | DSH host plugin: registry, watcher, routes, tools, auto-validation                    |
| `client`   | DSH client plugin: native session Design tab, header action, preview frame            |
| `preset`   | `design` agent preset and prompt section                                              |
| `bundle`   | Installable DSH bundle composing the above                                            |

Design files in a target repository are versioned sources: `design/design.json`,
`design/tokens.json`, `design/screens/*.dsx`, optional
`design/fixtures/*.json`, and optional `design/journeys/*.dsx`. Derived files
(including screenshots) belong only in `design/.cache/`, which the scaffolded
`.gitignore` excludes.

## Variants

A screen can hold mutually exclusive alternatives. The normal preview, journeys,
checks, and handoff always use the chosen branch; exploring an alternative never
changes the source.

```jsx
<Variants id="layout" chosen="compact">
  <Variant branch="compact">
    <Stack gap="spacing.sm">...</Stack>
  </Variant>
  <Variant branch="spacious">
    <Stack gap="spacing.lg">...</Stack>
  </Variant>
</Variants>
```

A whole-screen group at the file root wraps one `<Screen>` per branch with the
same id. Stable node ids may repeat across exclusive branches. Every branch is
validated, and wrappers never render.

- `/design/<session>/<screen>?variant=layout:spacious` opens one branch.
- `/design/<session>/<screen>?compare=layout:compact:spacious` keeps both
  branches side by side at the same breakpoint and state. Panes are isolated and
  scroll internally on narrow hosts.
- `design_view`, `design_query`, and `design_screenshot` accept
  `variant: "group:branch"`; screenshots for different branches never overwrite
  each other.
- `design_diff` compares two branches or the chosen projection at two local Git
  revisions without checking out or writing anything.

Promotion is an ordinary source edit: record rejected branches under
`design/.discarded/`, replace the `<Variants>` block with the winning children,
and validate. Clean that folder only when the owner explicitly asks. See
[`docs/variants-workflow.md`](docs/variants-workflow.md).

## Named states, fixtures, and journeys

A screen can declare deterministic starting points:

```jsx
<Screen id="orders" states={{ "filter-open": { open: ["filters"], values: { search: "acme" } } }}>
```

Open one with `/design/<session>/orders?bp=mobile&state=filter-open`. The state is
seeded once per screen/state route transition, survives valid hot reloads, and
does not reseed when only the breakpoint changes.

Fixtures are bounded, project-local JSON arrays of flat fictitious objects with
unique kebab-case `id`s. Bind them without writing logic:

```jsx
<List id="orders" items={fixture("orders")}>
  <ItemTemplate>
    <Text>{item("name")}</Text>
  </ItemTemplate>
</List>
<Table columns={[{ label: "Name", field: "name" }]} rows={fixture("orders")} />
<Select id="plan" options={fixture("plans")} />
```

Journeys live in `design/journeys/*.dsx` and use stable design ids:

```jsx
<Journey id="checkout" start="orders" state="filter-open" breakpoint="mobile">
  <Choose target="plan" value="pro" />
  <Type target="email" value="ada@example.com" />
  <Tap target="place-order" />
  <ExpectScreen screen="confirmation" />
</Journey>
```

See [`examples/synthetic-checkout`](examples/synthetic-checkout) for a runnable,
entirely fictitious project covering states, fixtures, tables, lists, selects,
and two journeys.

## Design panel and review comments

The plugin contributes a native, session-scoped **Design** tab to the DSH right
sidebar and a **Design** action in the session header. The tab frames the same
owner-authenticated interactive preview on the same origin, offers **Open in
tab**, and offers **Back to chat** for narrow layouts. The frame is limited to
the owning origin; deterministic documents stay unembeddable and carry no review
controls.

In the interactive preview, **Comment** turns component selection on. A click or
the keyboard picker (arrow keys move, Enter selects, Escape exits) targets a
rendered component without activating it. A draft captures the screen,
breakpoint, component type, stable design id or a visibly unstable structural
address, the named state, open overlays, tab selections, and the design
revision. Structural anchors also carry a content fingerprint of the rendered
screen, so an unchanged preview after an idle runtime reset keeps its pin while
a same-address edit does not; the numeric revision is diagnostic only. Free-form
field values, secrets, and arbitrary DOM content are not captured. Drafts live in DSH host memory keyed by session, not in the design
repository: they survive a browser reload and separate tabs of the same session,
but not a DSH process restart. Removing the DSH session (or disposing the
plugin) clears its drafts; a browser reload does not. Two sessions over one project have separate
pending sets.

Keyboard selection moves through the visible components, selects a
non-focusable structural node, exits with Escape without closing an open
drawer, and restores focus. The editor is a balloon beside the selected
component with a pointer, kept inside the visible preview pane on a desktop
browser at the desktop and Mobile breakpoints and in a narrow sidebar; the
pin reopens it at the same component. The open editor follows the same anchor
rules as its pin: another screen, state, variant, changed structural content, or
a short pane with no non-overlapping side drops the arrow and keeps the text
editable until the original anchor is valid again. A draft whose target is no
longer available keeps its text editable from Pending without a false pointer.
One session holds at most 50 pending comments; the
batch limit is the same, so every accepted draft can be sent together, and the
Comment control explains when the limit is reached.

**Send** submits the exact reviewed draft revisions as one ordinary queued user
message. Rejected delivery keeps the drafts and its retry; a replay of an already
accepted batch returns its acknowledgement without enqueuing another message.
Drafts added or edited while a batch is in flight stay pending. The success
message counts the versions the session accepted, separately from the drafts
it cleared and any that remain.

See [`docs/review/panel-review.md`](docs/review/panel-review.md) for the
disposable desktop and 390 CSS pixel review and
[`docs/verification.md`](docs/verification.md) for recorded evidence.

## Headless checks

`design_run_journey` executes the declared steps on the real kit controls and
stops at the first failed step with a bounded semantic snapshot. `design_lint`
measures every configured breakpoint for canvas/container overflow, peer
overlap, clipped text, pointer targets under 44 CSS pixels, and validator
off-token warnings. `design_screenshot` is opt-in and writes a deterministic
canvas-only PNG under `design/.cache/screenshots/`. `design_view` with an
explicit `breakpoint` returns computed boxes; without it, it stays browser-free.

Browser work is lazy: one Chromium per active DSH session, serialized per
session, fresh isolated context per check at the project breakpoint width and a
fixed 900 CSS px viewport height, and disposed with the session or the plugin.
Chromium always launches with its sandbox enabled and the tool never falls back
to an unsandboxed browser. Missing Chromium and sandbox failures are reported
explicitly. Configure an executable with
`DSH_DESIGN_CHROMIUM_PATH` (or `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_PATH`), or install the
browser matching the installed `playwright-core`:

```sh
pnpm exec playwright install chromium
```

## Implementation handoff

`design_handoff` generates a reproducible implementation package on demand under
`design/.cache/handoff/<content-id>/`. It resolves the requested screen, named
state, and breakpoint matrix before opening a browser, then writes:

- chosen-only, editable `screens/*.dsx` with stable ids, interactions, and named
  states, and no variant wrappers or discarded branches;
- the necessary `tokens.json`, `tokens.resolved.json`, `design.json`, local
  raster assets, and relevant `journeys/*.dsx` acceptance flows;
- a bounded chosen-source closure for selected `navigate()` targets and journeys:
  supporting screens are marked and get DSX only, never extra projections;
- matching semantic layout JSON and canvas PNGs from the same committed canvas;
- a sorted `manifest.json` separating the requested `selection` from the
  `support` closure, with explicit dimensions, choices, browser/kit identity,
  artifact sizes, and SHA-256 digests. `design.json` keeps every configured
  breakpoint so responsive maps remain valid, even for a narrower evidence set.

Omitted selectors default to every valid chosen screen, the unnamed state plus
every named state, and every configured breakpoint, bounded to 24 projections and
32 screens. Use `states: ["$default"]` for the unnamed state; a named state is
selected by its literal name, including `"default"`. Projection ids are
collision-free length-prefixed tuples. The package is content-addressed and
verified before reuse; invalid, stale, interrupted, or partially published output
fails explicitly. It is derived cache, never committed. A coding agent in any
preset can read the manifest and package with ordinary file tools; handoff stays
in the Design preset.

The import workflow is out of scope for this repository change: no import
tooling, settings, or artifacts are shipped.

See [`docs/handoff.md`](docs/handoff.md).

## Development notes

- The preview is served only by the local DSH web server. The route demands
  `required` admission and additionally checks the owner principal, following
  DSH's open-in-app pattern. It never deploys anywhere.
- Project media is a separate route from trusted bundle assets. It serves only
  bounded, signature-checked passive raster images (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP) from the
  canonical design folder, with `nosniff`, no-store, sandbox CSP, and
  same-origin resource policy. SVG, HTML, JavaScript, and arbitrary project
  files are never served.
- The `css` escape hatch uses one shared parser/validator in core; the renderer
  turns its declarations into authoritative node-scoped rules and rewrites
  local `url()` targets through the project-file route.
- Deterministic mode serves one self-contained document: project state,
  renderer code/styles, bundled Inter fonts, and bounded validated local raster
  bytes are inlined. After the initial navigation there are no project, asset,
  font, or image requests, including interactions and screen changes. A strict
  CSP disables connections, the rendering clock is fixed, and icons are inline
  SVG.
- The bundled Inter files cover the Latin subset declared by their
  `unicode-range`. Characters outside that range use the browser's fallback
  font, which is not bundled; deterministic rendering of such text therefore
  depends on the platform font.
- `pnpm run pack:bundle` produces the local artifact used for non-link
  installs. The distributed artifact is the GitHub Release asset
  `dsh-design-bundle.tgz`, built from the same bundle. A direct source
  repository URL is not an install path: it selects the monorepo root. Local
  checkout and local tarball installs remain supported; maintainer steps are in
  [`docs/releasing.md`](docs/releasing.md).
- The bundle deliberately imports no `@deepseek-ai/*` runtime module, so a
  public checkout installs with plain `pnpm install`.
- Fixtures and journeys are read on every project load, participate in the
  watcher fingerprint, and report diagnostics through the same file/screen
  scopes and automatic edit summaries as screens.
- Browser checks reuse the existing self-contained deterministic document, bind
  a synthetic local origin, fulfill only that document, and block every other
  request and service worker.
- Named states and fixture expansions are validated before they reach the
  renderer; repeated ids derive from the list id, fixture key, and template
  identity, never from array position.
- The design preset copies DSH's shipped `standard` composition; a drift test
  compares it when `DSH_CHECKOUT` points at a DSH checkout.
- Verification evidence from the implementation run is in
  [`docs/verification.md`](docs/verification.md).

# dsh-stl-viewer An **STL / STEP 3D preview** for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh) side card. Click any `.stl`, `.step`, `.stp`, `.iges`, `.igs` or `.brep` in the [dsh-better-sidebar](https://github.com/H-h-Hh/dsh-better-sidebar) file tree and the file renders in place, with the controls of a normal 3D viewer. STL is parsed in the page; STEP and the other B-rep formats are tessellated by OpenCascade on the host, in a worker, and come back as the very same triangles the rest of the plugin already knows how to draw, measure and weigh. ``` left-drag orbit around the model — freely: the camera tumbles 360° in any direction, straight over the north pole and on under the model, with no gimbal stop wheel zoom right-drag pan (Shift + left-drag does the same; two-finger scroll zooms) double-click reset the view (the 复位视角 button and the R / 0 keys do too) measure click 测量 (or press M), then click two features — the cursor snaps to a vertex, an edge, a whole face or a circular rim, the way Bambu Studio's measure tool does. Shift-click takes an arbitrary point on the surface instead. Dragging still orbits, Esc or 测量 again leaves the mode view the 视图 menu holds front / top / right / iso (keys 1 / 2 / 3 / 4, animated), wireframe (W), turntable (A), the XYZ triad (G) and "save image" — plus a shortcut card (?) convert a .step / .iges / .brep file is posted to the host, which tessellates it with OpenCascade in a worker; a small overlay counts the seconds and can cancel ```

A 47,068-triangle gear cover (176 × 176 × 40 mm) in the real side card, next to the chat that produced it.

No viewer installed: “此文件类型不支持预览 / 下载查看”. With the plugin: a 2,912-triangle enclosure lid and a 17,136-triangle stencil, both in the side card.

点到点: the cursor snaps to the corner you are aiming at, the picked point is drawn as a dot on the model, and the readout carries the straight distance plus ΔX / ΔY / ΔZ: 58.0 mm across the diagonal of a plate, the two farthest corners the test could find.

面到面: click one face, then another. Coplanar triangles are flood-filled from the picked one, so you measure a real face — not one triangle — and two parallel faces give the gap between them: 36.0 mm here, with ΔX / ΔY / ΔZ underneath.

圆: hover a rim and the whole rim is one pick — here the 20 mm bore of a washer, with the 40 mm outer rim available as a second, separate pick. The panel in the top-left corner gives Ø and R (and, while measuring, the pair type plus ΔX / ΔY / ΔZ), the way Bambu Studio does it.

视图: front / top / right / iso, wireframe, turntable, save image and the shortcut card in one menu, with the model's volume, surface area and watertightness in the bottom-left corner.

STEP: this is stencil_top.step, opened the same way. A B-rep file has no triangles in it — the host tessellated its surfaces with OpenCascade and the plugin drew the result, all 17,136 of them, which is exactly the count the STL export of the same part gives. Measuring, volume and the view menu work because what arrives is ordinary triangles.

> **Why a separate plugin?** > DeepSeek Harness ships previews for text, images, PDFs and Markdown. Binary CAD > formats such as `.stl`, `.obj`, `.step` fall through to “this file type cannot be > previewed”. This plugin registers an `stl` file viewer on the `betterSidebar` > service, so `.stl` stops being an opaque blob — and it adds a host route so the > same viewer can open the B-rep formats too. ## Features - **STL, STEP, IGES and BREP** — STL is parsed in the page. The others are B-rep: there is no triangle to draw until someone tessellates the surfaces, so the bytes are posted to a host route, an OpenCascade WebAssembly build runs them in a `worker_threads` worker (the reader is synchronous and would otherwise freeze the whole Host), and the result comes back as a packed triangle buffer that the client decodes into the same pipeline STL uses. A 6 MB stencil: 17,136 triangles in about ten seconds, then cached by SHA-1 - **Binary and ASCII STL** — sniffed, not guessed from the extension: exact `84 + 50·N` size match first, then an ASCII scan, then a tolerant binary pass for files with trailing bytes - **Correct normals** — recomputed per facet; STLs in the wild carry zeroed or plainly wrong normals, and exported meshes often mix winding orders - **Two-sided shading** — `gl_FrontFacing` flips the normal, so inverted facets still read as solid rather than a black hole - **Z-up → Y-up** — CAD and 3D printing export Z-up; the viewer stands models upright instead of showing them lying on their back - **Frame-fit camera** — the orbit distance is derived from the bounding sphere and the FOV, so a 0.6 mm thick stencil and a 300 mm part both fill the panel on open - **360° free tumbling** — a drag accumulates a quaternion on top of the base orientation, so the camera rolls over the poles and straight under the model instead of stopping at ±83°. No gimbal wall, no flip at the zenith, no camera roll creeping in: the basis is rebuilt from the quaternion every frame and stays orthonormal, and the XYZ triad keeps agreeing with what is on screen - **Measure the way a CAD tool does** — the pointer snaps to a **vertex**, an **edge** or a whole **face**, like [Bambu Studio's measure tool](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/software/bambu-studio/measure): corners within 12 px win over edges within 8 px, which win over the face underneath, and Shift-click takes an arbitrary point instead. Only real creases snap (boundary edges, or neighbours more than 20° apart), so a finely tessellated cylinder does not turn into a field of snapping edges. The pair decides what is measured — point/point is the straight distance, point/face the perpendicular distance, edge/edge the angle plus the gap, face/face the plane gap when parallel and the true shortest distance plus the angle when not — and every readout carries ΔX / ΔY / ΔZ. Picking is a ray–triangle intersection against the real mesh, and the numbers come from the raw file coordinates rather than the normalised render space, so they are the same numbers you would measure in CAD - **Circles are picked as circles** — a rim on a bore, a boss or a cylinder is a chain of very short creases, and edge snapping alone would only ever catch one facet of it. Hovering a rim therefore traces the loop and fits a circle to it, which turns the whole rim into a single pick: the 20 mm bore and the 40 mm outside of a washer are two separate features, so an inner and an outer diameter can be read on their own. Clicking **inside** the hole works the same way — the bore wall is one smooth region whose boundary is that circle, so you do not have to land on the rim itself. The fit rejects what is not round (a hexagon is not a circle) and a chain that does not close - **A readout panel in the corner** — the picks are listed in the top-left corner the way Bambu Studio does it: `直径 Ø 20.0 mm` and `半径 R 10.0 mm` for a circle, the pair type and the distance for a measurement, with ΔX / ΔY / ΔZ underneath - **Volume, surface and watertightness** — the corner readout also answers the first question a print checks: how much material is this, and is the mesh closed? Volume comes from the divergence theorem, area from the facet areas, and both are divided back out of the render normalisation, so they are the file's own numbers (`cm³` / `cm²` under the mm assumption). "Not closed" means some edge belongs to a single facet — a hole in the shell - **Standard views, animated** — front / top / right / iso on keys `1`–`4`, with a 260 ms eased transition that moves the orbit angles only, so your zoom and focus point survive - **Wireframe and turntable** — `W` and `A`, or the same rows in the view menu. Wireframe draws the triangle edges over a dimmed solid (with polygon offset, so the lines do not z-fight), which is how you see how a model was tessellated - **Save the picture** — the current frame as a PNG named after the file. It is drawn on demand before `toDataURL`, not grabbed from a stale buffer - **An XYZ triad** — bottom right, red / green / blue, drawn as SVG so the letters stay crisp: it turns with the camera, dims the axis pointing away from you, and draws the axis pointing at you as a ring. `G` or the view menu hides it - **Menus, not a button wall** — three buttons stay on the model, the 视图 menu holds the rest, and `?` opens a card listing every gesture and key - **Themed** — transparent clear colour and `currentColor` chrome, so the panel follows the app's dark/light theme instead of stamping a white box on it - **No build step, no dependencies** — `lib/client.js` *is* the artifact ## Requirements - DeepSeek Harness `>= 0.2.0` - [dsh-better-sidebar](https://github.com/H-h-Hh/dsh-better-sidebar) `>= 0.32.0` — it owns the file tree, the tabs and the `betterSidebar` service this plugin registers into. The client half declares `inject: ['betterSidebar']`; from Cordis 0.32 on, reading a service without declaring it throws, and an `apply` that swallows that error registers nothing at all — which is exactly how an older build of this plugin went silent after a DSH update - A browser with WebGL 1 (everything current; the software rasteriser is enough) - For STEP / IGES / BREP nothing else is needed: the host half pulls in [`occt-import-js`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/occt-import-js), OpenCascade compiled to WebAssembly, as its one dependency ## Install In DSH, or from the plugin manager page → *install from a local directory*: ``` plugin_manager install_bundle target: file:D:/path/to/dsh-stl-viewer ``` Then reload the page. Open any `.stl` or `.step` from the file tree; if the file is already open in a tab as an unsupported binary, close that tab and click the file again. Uninstall: ``` plugin_manager remove_bundle target: dsh-stl-viewer ``` ## How it works The plugin is a bundle with a host half and a client half. | half | file | what it does | | --- | --- | --- | | host | `lib/index.js` | registers `POST /dsh-stl-viewer/convert` on `ctx.webServer`, SHA-1s each body, serves repeats from an LRU cache and from a disk cache, and hands the rest to a resident worker | | worker | `lib/convert.worker.mjs` | `occt-import-js` reads STEP / IGES / BREP, tessellates, and transfers back a packed triangle buffer | | manifest | `package.json` | `dsh.bundle.patch` makes it a bundle, `exports["./client"]` + `dsh.client.platform: "web"` publish `/plugins/dsh-stl-viewer/client.js` | | patch | `cordis.patch.yml` | the one `insert:` line that puts the plugin in the layer stack | | client | `lib/client.js` | parse (or fetch the converted mesh) → normalise → WebGL → input → registration; a classic script, run by the DSH module loader, `require('react')` resolving to the host's React | The host half mounts its routes inside `ctx.inject(['webServer'], …)`. Cordis refuses to read `ctx.webServer` before the dependency is declared — and it throws at activation, not at call time — while an object-level `inject` would defer the whole `apply()` until the service exists. Wrapping just the mount block defers nothing else. The viewer descriptor covers the extensions, one component for all of them: Registration is one call, and the model bytes come from the sidebar's own route: ```js ctx.betterSidebar.registerFileViewer({ id: 'dsh-stl-viewer:stl', title: () => t('title'), icon: (size) => cubeIcon(size), exts: ['stl', 'step', 'stp', 'iges', 'igs', 'brep'], priority: 10, fetchStrategy: 'mediaUrl', // the host hands over the raw-bytes URL component: StlViewer }) ``` `fetchStrategy: 'mediaUrl'` means the viewer gets `mediaUrl` as a prop and does a plain `fetch()`, so no host RPC, no base64 over the wire. Everything after that is local: | step | detail | | --- | --- | | read | `fetch(mediaUrl, { credentials: 'same-origin' })` → `ArrayBuffer` | | parse | 80-byte header + `uint32` count + 50 bytes/facet, or `vertex x y z` triples (ASCII capped at 6 M numbers) | | normalise | centre on the bbox, scale to a max edge of 2, per-facet normals, Z-up → Y-up | | render | WebGL 1, three lights + specular, one `drawArrays`, redraws only on demand | STEP takes one extra hop, and the rest is shared: | step | detail | | --- | --- | | fetch | the same `mediaUrl` fetch — the sidebar's route already knows how to hand over the bytes | | post | `POST plugins/dsh-stl-viewer/convert` with the bytes and an `x-dsh-stl-name` header (a relative URL, so a reverse-proxied Host works too) | | tessellate | the host reads the body (128 MB cap), SHA-1s it, and runs OpenCascade in a resident worker with `linearDeflection: 0.0012` of the bounding box | | pack | `'DSHM'` + version + triangle count + part count, then 9 float32 per triangle — 616 KB for the 17 k-triangle stencil above, instead of the 6 MB file | | decode | header check, one `Float32Array` view, then the same `finalizeMesh`, so measuring, circles, volume and the view menu see ordinary geometry | The plugin also registers a cube file icon for all six extensions, so the file tree stops showing a generic blob. ## Notes and limits - **Sizes carry no unit.** STL stores bare numbers; the `size X × Y × Z` readout is the raw bounding box, not mm or inch. A STEP file *does* declare a unit, so the converter is asked for millimetres and the numbers are real mm. - **Volume and area inherit that assumption.** They are reported as `cm³` / `cm²`, i.e. the file's numbers read as mm. An inch-authored part will show numbers that are 16 387× off, which is the same caveat the measurement readout already carries. - **"Closed" is about holes, not about manifoldness.** A mesh counts as closed when no edge belongs to just one facet. Edges shared by three or more facets (self-intersections, duplicated coplanar facets) do not make it "not closed", because there is no hole for resin or filament to leak through — they are a different kind of problem, and the viewer does not claim to find them. - **Measurements say `mm`, because CAD STL almost always is.** The number is the raw coordinate distance in the file; if your model is authored in inches, read it as inches. - **"A face" is a coplanar region, found by flood fill.** Curved surfaces are therefore many faces, which is what you want when measuring a flat pad against a plate, but a fillet is not a single face. Faces are grown along shared edges only, so a mesh with welded vertices gives the best regions. - **Snapping needs the crease topology, which is built on first use.** Finding corners and creases means an edge sweep over the mesh — 0.6 s for 47 k facets — so it happens the first time you hover in measure mode instead of when the file opens. Meshes above 400 k facets skip it and fall back to face picking. - **A circle is recognised, not assumed.** The rim must close (no turn sharper than 60° per step) and fit a circle within 2% of its radius, checked at the vertices, at the midpoint of every segment and against the rim plane — a 48-sided bore reads as round, a hexagon does not. Circles ride on the same crease topology as snapping, so they also wait for that first hover. The wall of a hole is treated as a circle too: it is grown as one smooth patch (across every edge that is not a crease), and its boundary has to be a circle whose axis the patch's own facets face sideways; a flat disc has both boundaries round but faces along the axis, so it stays a face. Small openings in that wall do not spoil it — a set-screw hole breaks the bore into a ring with two big and two little loops, so the widest group of equal radii wins and the patch still has to be a true cylinder (every vertex within 2% of one radius) - **Z-up is assumed.** Models authored Y-up will lie on their side. Axis guessing is deliberately left out — a wrong guess is more confusing than a predictable default. - **Large files are parsed whole.** A few hundred thousand facets take 1–2 s and one `drawArrays` call; there is no streaming and no LOD. - **STEP is tessellated on the host, once per file.** The time is OpenCascade parsing the B-rep and building its topology — roughly 1.2–2 s per megabyte, single-threaded, and tessellation settings only change the triangle count, not the wait (a 6 MB stencil: 12.8 s at any deflection). So the wait is made to happen once: a progress overlay counts the seconds and offers cancel, the converter runs in a worker kept alive across requests, and every finished mesh is cached by SHA-1 in memory (8 files / 192 MB) **and on disk** in `%TEMP%/dsh-stl-viewer-cache` (24 files / 512 MB), so reopening a file — even after a DSH restart — is instant. Measured on the 6 MB stencil: 12.5 s cold, 6 ms from memory, 8 ms from disk. Detail is relative to the bounding box, which is what keeps a 0.6 mm stencil and a 300 mm part both sensible — but it also means a huge assembly comes out coarse. - **What arrives from STEP is triangles, not surfaces.** Measuring, circles and the volume readout work on the tessellation, exactly as they do for STL: a bore is a bore because the fitted rim really is round, not because the STEP says `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`. - `.obj`, `.glb`, `.3mf` are out of scope. - **No WebGL → a message, not a white panel.** ## Tests ```bash npm install # only dependency: occt-import-js, used by the host half node --check lib/client.js node test/smoke.cjs # client, in a vm sandbox, no browser node test/host.mjs # host routes, real OpenCascade, real STEP fixture ``` `test/smoke.cjs` runs `lib/client.js` in a `vm` sandbox with a minimal React hooks stub and a replaceable `fetch`, and asserts the module contract, the viewer descriptor, a hand-built binary cube (12 facets, size 20), an ASCII single triangle, the three error paths (garbage bytes, empty file, failed fetch), the face-to-face geometry — plane fitting, point-to-triangle and triangle-to-triangle distance — and the feature topology: 8 corners and exactly 12 creases on a cube (the 6 in-plane diagonals do not count), plus point/segment/plane helpers. The circle fit gets its own group: a 24-gon traces back to its start and fits r = 10, a hexagon, a square and an open chain are all rejected, and a washer fixture yields exactly two rims, R10 and R20. The last group checks the model stats against arithmetic: the 20 mm cube fixture is 8000 mm³ and 2400 mm², the washer matches π(R² − r²)h within the polygonal approximation, the two plates add up to 43200 mm³, and a single triangle has area but no volume and is not closed. The last group is the STEP plumbing: the five extensions are recognised, a hand-packed `'DSHM'` buffer decodes back to 18 floats, the decoded mesh reads as a 10 mm square of 100 mm², and a foreign magic number is rejected. No browser needed. `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs the same on every push. `test/host.mjs` loads `lib/index.js` as a plain module with a fake Cordis context, captures the two routes it registers, and drives them with Node-style request/response objects: the health route reports the five formats, `GET` on the converter is a 405, the junk-bytes case comes back as a JSON 500, and `test/fixtures/cube.step` — a 20 mm cube generated by `test/fixtures/make-step.cjs` — round-trips through the real worker and OpenCascade as exactly 12 triangles, 20 × 20 × 20 mm and 8000 mm³, with the second request served from cache in under 200 ms. The end-to-end check uses a real renderer: `test/harness.html` mounts the component with React UMD builds, `test/shoot.cjs` screenshots it through a headless Electron (`--enable-unsafe-swiftshader --use-gl=swiftshader`). That is how the images above were produced. `test/measure.cjs` drives the same harness with synthetic pointer events: it looks up the screen pixels of the two plate faces through the viewer's `_test` handle, clicks 测量, clicks both faces, and asserts the label reads `36.0 mm` with `面到面 · 平行面间距`, that `_test.measure().parallel` is true, and that Esc clears everything again. The fixture `test/fixtures/plates.stl` comes from `test/fixtures/make-plates.cjs`: two 80 x 60 mm plates 36 mm apart, the top one covering half of the bottom one. The same fixture doubles as the snapping check: `test/snap-points.cjs` scans the canvas for pixels that snap to a `point`, picks the two farthest apart and asserts the label reads `58.0 mm` — the diagonal of the top plate — with ΔX 40 / ΔY 0 / ΔZ 42. `test/circle.cjs` covers the rims, on a washer made by `test/fixtures/make-ring.cjs` (Ø40 outside, Ø20 bore, 6 mm thick, 48 segments, normals written as zero so the plugin has to recompute them). It sweeps the canvas through `_test.pickFeature`, keeps the pixels that snap to a circle and asserts there are exactly two of them, then clicks the bore and reads the corner panel: `直径 Ø 20.0 mm` and `半径 R 10.0 mm`. `test/view.cjs` drives the view menu through its real DOM: it opens 视图, clicks 俯视 and asserts the camera really is looking down (pitch 1.5607) with the zoom untouched, turns wireframe on, starts and stops the turntable (checking the yaw moved while it ran), grabs a snapshot and asserts the result is a PNG data URL, opens the shortcut card and closes it again, presses `2` on the focused canvas and expects the same top view, and finally drags the canvas 400 px upwards with synthetic pointer events: the camera must end up **under** the model (`dir[1] < -0.3`), the triad must still read X / Y / Z, and dragging back must return to the starting direction — the free-tumble regression. ```bash env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -u NODE_OPTIONS test/measure.cjs \ "test/harness.html?file=./fixtures/plates.stl" out.png env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -u NODE_OPTIONS test/snap-points.cjs \ "test/harness.html?file=./fixtures/plates.stl" out.png env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -u NODE_OPTIONS test/circle.cjs \ "test/harness.html?file=./fixtures/ring.stl" out.png env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -u NODE_OPTIONS test/view.cjs \ "test/harness.html?file=./fixtures/ring.stl" out.png env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -u NODE_OPTIONS test/hub.cjs \\ "test/harness.html?file=./some/real/part.stl" out.png 47 ``` `test/hub.cjs` is the regression for bores that are not clean: the last argument is the diameter to look for in mm, and it clicks every circle it can find on a real part until one answers with that Ø. It needs a model of your own, so it stays out of CI. `test/step.cjs` is the end-to-end for the new formats, and the only test that uses the real host: it starts an HTTP server inside the Electron main process that serves the harness and the plugin's own convert handler, loads the page over `http://`, lets the viewer fetch the STEP bytes and post them back to the host, and then reads the corner readout. With the fixture cube it asserts 12 triangles and 8.00 cm³; pointed at a real 6 MB part it reports 17,136 triangles — the same count that part's STL export gives. ```bash env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -u NODE_OPTIONS test/step.cjs out.png ./fixtures/cube.step env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE -u NODE_OPTIONS test/step.cjs out.png ./_your_part.step ``` The second form is how the STEP screenshot above was made: copy a model into `test/` (the harness serves that directory) and pass it as a relative path. ## 中文速览 给 DSH 侧边栏加一个 **STL / STEP 三维预览**：文件树里点开 `.stl`、`.step`、`.stp`、`.iges`、`.igs`、`.brep`，右侧面板直接渲染，交互同常规 3D 看图。 ```bash plugin_manager install_bundle target: file:D:/path/to/dsh-stl-viewer ``` - 左键旋转，**可 360° 自由翻滚**：一路拖过天顶翻到模型背面乃至底下，没有 ±83° 的极点死角、过顶也不会突然翻转 / 滚轮缩放 / 右键平移 / 双击复位（`R`、`0` 也复位） - 点「测量」（或按 `M`）后光标会像 Bambu Studio 那样吸附到**顶点 / 棱 / 面 / 圆**：两个点的直线距离、点到面的垂直距离、两棱的夹角与间距、两面平行取间距、不平行取夹角 + 最短距离、圆心距等，读数都带 ΔX/ΔY/ΔZ；`Shift` + 点击取任意表面点；拖动仍可旋转，`Esc` 退出 - 悬停圆孔/圆柱的边一圈即整圈选中，**内径与外径是两个独立的圆**可分别点；左上角面板显示 `直径 Ø` 与 `半径 R`，和 Bambu Studio 的读数面板一致 - 二进制与 ASCII STL 都能读；法线逐面重算、双面打光，Z-up 自动立起来 - **STEP / IGES / BREP**：B-rep 文件里根本没有三角面，字节会先 POST 给插件的宿主路由，由 OpenCascade（`occt-import-js`）在 worker 线程里三角化，再回传紧凑网格——遮罩上显示转换秒数、可取消。慢的是 OpenCascade 解析 B-rep：约每 MB 1.2–2 秒，且与三角化参数无关（6 MB 的钢网无论怎么调都是 12.8 秒）。所以只让它算一次：worker 常驻复用，结果按 SHA-1 缓存在内存（8 个 / 192 MB）和 `%TEMP%/dsh-stl-viewer-cache`（24 个 / 512 MB），重开同一文件甚至重启 DSH 后都是秒开——实测冷 12.5 秒、内存 6 ms、磁盘 8 ms。6 MB 钢网得到 17,136 个三角面，与同零件的 STL 导出完全一致 - 相机按包围球自适应，0.6 mm 的钢网和 300 mm 的零件都会铺满面板 - 「视图」菜单：正视 / 俯视 / 右视 / 等轴（`1`–`4`，260 ms 缓动过渡，缩放保持不变）、线框（`W`）、自动旋转（`A`）、坐标轴（`G`）、保存当前画面为 PNG，以及 `?` 快捷键卡片 - 右下角有红/绿/蓝 **XYZ 三脚标**：跟着相机转，背向你的轴压暗，正对你的轴画成圆环；用 SVG 画所以字始终清晰，`G` 可关 - # dsh-agent-herald

Herald, the sovereign release agent: a publisher that earns its keep
releasing files whose decryption is earned through ownership — hold a
DataDAO community's token and its corpus opens for you.

## The definition

| File | Prompt section | Order | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `soul.md` | `agent:soul` | -500 | Who Herald is: goal, community covenant, money ethics, custody |
| `process.md` | `agent:process` | -400 | What Herald does: release pipeline, gate selection, money loop, community ops |
| `workflow.md` | `agent:workflow` | -350 | Stage manual: source→ingest→analyze→seal→upload→sync→cleanup, all harness-native |
| `reference/aol-protocol.md` | `agent:aol-protocol` | -300 | Haven-AOL v1/v3/v4 mechanics: derivation, epochs, market-cap math, errors |

`apply()` reads the four docs and registers each as a system-prompt
section (the tool-bash pattern). Sections render before the deployment
persona prefix (identity first, then deployment instructions, then
first-party guidance). No config — the docs are the config. A missing
or empty doc throws at apply: an agent never boots without its soul.

Token cost is fixed per deployment (the docs are static, prefix-stable
for KV cache); edits to any doc change every subsequent prompt.

## Money loop

Release tokens launched with the agent as fee recipient earn
mint/burn royalties; venue fees accumulate in routers and sweep on
cadence; v4 drips tie unlocks to market cap so community buying
drives both unlocks and royalties. `process.md` §3 is the procedure.

## Sealing is harness-native

`aol_seal` (v1/v3/v4) seals in-container under the canister-fetched
verification key. Herald seals its own releases, verifies the
binding (`aol_gate_info`), and trial-decrypts before announcing.

## Note: the dead `persona` key (2026-09)

`dsh-persona/cordis.patch.yml` and `docker/profile.patch.yml` set
`system-prompt.config.persona`, which the installed
`dsh-system-prompt` (0.1.7-rc.2 and 0.2.1-alpha.1 alike) never reads — its schema declares
`personaPrefix`/`personaSuffix` (`Config({persona: ...})` parses but
the constructor ignores the key). Until this package, the deployment
ran with an empty persona. Herald's sections are the live identity
now; those `persona` rows are inert documentation. If they are ever
migrated to `personaPrefix`, that text will render *after* these
sections (order 0) — keep it short or fold it here.

# dsh-web3

## Quickstart

One-shot get-started (builds latest `02ca906` stack, tests, starts `xmtp-prod`, spits QR + wallet):

```sh
bash quickstart.sh
# or: MUSE_SPARK_API_KEY=<your-key> bash quickstart.sh
```

Spits `Invite URL: https://popup.convos.org/v2?i=...` + ANSI QR (`qrencode -t ANSIUTF8`) and wallet `0xa85dD3FbD8C2c831Ef156036F14638CcFf03b44e` (dynamic `wallet_info`→`ctx.wallet.address`). Also available: `./show-convos-qr.sh` / `./show-xmtp-qr.sh` for QR-only.


Reimplementation of the sovereign web3 agent harness using DeepSeek harness as core, where everything is a plug-in. Replaces https://github.com/Haven-hvn/haven-core and https://github.com/Haven-hvn/haven-adapters

There is deliberately **no aggregate bundle**: people may want one capability
and not another, so each package ships its own `dsh.bundle.patch` →
`cordis.patch.yml` inserting only its own rows, and installs independently:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-haven/<package>
```

## The packages

| Package | Haven concept | dsh seam it lands on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`dsh-wallet`](./dsh-wallet) | `WalletIdentity` custody ("the key never leaves this boundary") + the `CryptoAdapter` contract | `ctx.wallet` service; credentials resolved through `ctx.credentials` per operation — configuration carries *references*, never keys |
| [`dsh-wallet-ethereum`](./dsh-wallet-ethereum) | `EthereumCryptoAdapter` → OWS migration plan | provider plugin registering a `CryptoAdapter` per chain family, backed by `@open-wallet-standard/core` (sign-only; the standard handles all chain families) |
| [`dsh-treasury`](./dsh-treasury) | `Treasury` machine: balances, expenses, FUNDED/LOW/CRITICAL/DEPLETED survival gradient | storage-domain tables + derived state; a policy plugin short-circuits `agent/request` and `tools/pre-execute`, metered off `llm/token-meter` |
| [`dsh-channel-xmtp`](./dsh-channel-xmtp) | `XmtpChannel` direct agent↔user messaging | one dsh agent per conversation (`ctx.agents`), inbound via `agent.followup`, replies via `sendText`; EOA identity signs through `ctx.wallet` |
| [`dsh-storage-synapse`](./dsh-storage-synapse) | `SynapseStorageAdapter` + `StorageBackend` pinning | `ctx.synapse` + `synapse_pin` / `synapse_pin_status` agent tools; every node request wallet-signed per operation |
| [`dsh-wallet-tools`](./dsh-wallet-tools) | wallet address/balance exposure (replaces hard-coded persona) | `wallet_info` tool via `ctx.tools` + `ctx.wallet.address()` live (no hard-coded `0x...`) |
| [`dsh-persona`](./dsh-persona) | Haven persona / system instructions | `agent/request` composition; generic instruction to call `wallet_info` when address/balance/funding asked |
| [`dsh-tool-prowlarr`](./dsh-tool-prowlarr) | Prowlarr indexer search bridge (use-case agnostic) | `prowlarr_indexers` / `prowlarr_search` read-only tools via `ctx.tools`; no wallet seam |
| [`dsh-tool-acquisition`](./dsh-tool-acquisition) | Download/acquisition arm (Haven `acquisition/` port, torrent clients outsourced) | `acquire_submit` / `acquire_status` tools via `ctx.tools`; qBittorrent → Transmission failover, no wallet seam |

## Composition

`dsh-wallet` is the custody root; the other packages build on it:

```
dsh-wallet  ←  dsh-wallet-ethereum   (registers the evm CryptoAdapter)
    ↑
    ├── dsh-channel-xmtp             (signs XMTP identity per signature)
    ├── dsh-storage-synapse          (signs node requests per request)
    └── dsh-wallet-tools             (exposes wallet_info via ctx.tools → ctx.wallet)
dsh-persona                           (composes agent/request; calls wallet_info, no hard-coded address)
dsh-treasury                          (independent; needs the storage stack)
```

A typical full install:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-wallet \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-wallet-ethereum \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-treasury \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-channel-xmtp \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-storage-synapse \
  @open-wallet-standard/core @xmtp/node-sdk
```

The two SDKs are optional peers: every package loads, mounts, and tests
without them (lazy imports with actionable errors; tests substitute
`internals.*` seams).

## Prerequisites

- **Storage stack** (`dsh-treasury` only): the profile must mount `storage`,
  `storage-json`/`storage-sqlite`, and `storage-domain` rows (present in
  `dsh-web-app`; absent in `dsh-base`). The treasury patch does NOT insert
  them — a row id inserted by two layers mounts the plugin twice.
- **Agent stack** (`dsh-channel-xmtp` only): agents/sessions/llm, present in
  any agent-running profile.
- Plugins with unmet `inject` lists stay dormant instead of failing, so
  install order is free.

## Design decision: isolated bundles, coupled seams

Web3 plugins are **isolated as code, coupled at the seam** — a direct consequence of
how the DeepSeek harness composes.

* **Isolated** — every package is a standalone Cordis plugin (`export const name`,
  `export const inject`, `export function apply(ctx, config)`) with its own
  `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`. There is no aggregate bundle; `dsh plugin add`
  installs one capability at a time and `inject` ordering is free (unmet `inject` stays
  dormant). This is why `dsh-wallet`, `dsh-channel-xmtp`, `dsh-storage-synapse`,
  `dsh-treasury`, and `dsh-wallet-tools` each build via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`) and test
  without the others (`internals.*` seams).

* **Coupled at the seam** — isolation would break without declared contracts:
  `ctx.wallet` (custody), `ctx.tools` (model-facing tools), `ctx.agents`/`ctx.sessions`
  (per-conversation agents), `ctx.synapse`/`ctx.treasury` (storage). Plugins declare
  this with `inject` — e.g. `inject = ['wallet','tools']` in `dsh-wallet-tools` and
  `dsh-storage-synapse` — so they mount only when the seam exists, and call it
  per-operation (`ctx.wallet.address()`, `ctx.wallet.signMessage()`, `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))`).

Harness limitations that force this shape:

1. **Singleton tool runtime.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` exposes one scheduler (`ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare`). If two instances are deduped incorrectly the `Symbol` mismatches and every `tool/call` fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`. Bundles therefore depend on `dsh-tools` as a **peer** (`0.2.1-alpha.1`, exact — dsh also rejects a bundle whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers do not match the running CLI) and `link:` installs must dedupe to one copy.

2. **Wallet custody is per-operation.** Configuration carries only `keyRef`/`wallet` names; `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs inside `signMessage`/`address` and is dropped. Consumers (XMTP identity in `dsh-channel-xmtp`, per-request `x-synapse-*` headers in `dsh-storage-synapse`, `wallet_info` in `dsh-wallet-tools`) see only addresses/signatures. Hard-coding an address in persona (`When asked for address, answer with 0x...`) breaks rotation and wallet-agnostic installs — the correct seam is a tool that resolves `ctx.wallet.address(config.wallet)` live.

3. **Channel is per-conversation, not per-process.** `dsh-channel-xmtp` creates one `ctx.agents` session per XMTP conversation (`SessionId` derived from `conversationId`), handles `conversations.sync()` before `getConversationById`, reconnect/consent sweep, and dedup. The channel owns transport; the agent owns the turn.

Result: add `dsh-wallet` once, then compose any subset. `dsh-wallet-tools` (`wallet_info` tool, `presentCall: {kind:'read'}`) makes the EVM address model-reachable without persona shortcuts; `dsh-channel-xmtp` makes it XMTP-reachable; `dsh-storage-synapse` makes it storage-reachable — all through `ctx.wallet`, none by sharing key material.

## Custody model (the through-line)

Haven's rule — *the private key never leaves its layer; everything else
requests signatures* — maps to one dsh pattern used everywhere here:

1. Configuration carries **names and credential references** (`keyRef`,
   `dbEncryptionKeyRef`). A pasted raw key fails loud at plugin load because
   key material cannot syntactically be a `CredentialRef`.
2. Secrets exist only **inside one operation**: `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs
   per call, the provider signs, every reference is dropped. Rotation reaches
   the very next operation without restart.
3. Consumers (XMTP signer, Synapse requests, future channels) see only
   **addresses and signatures** through `ctx.wallet`.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install       # workspace of five packages
pnpm vitest        # specs live in <package>/tests/**
```

Each package builds self-contained via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`), so git or
path installs work without monorepo context. Money figures are integer µUSD
(USD × 1e6) throughout, matching haven-core.

# dsh-channel-xmtp

XMTP channel for DeepSeek Harness: direct agent↔user messaging over the XMTP
network, ported from Haven's `XmtpChannel` (haven-adapters).

Inbound XMTP text reaches a dsh agent; assistant output is sent back to the
same conversation — both replies to inbound and output of turns the channel
did not start (background-job completion wakes, subagent returns,
schedules). Identity is an Ethereum EOA signed through `dsh-wallet` — this
channel never holds key material.

## Transport model

The channel is a session **observer** (the `dsh-acp` bridge pattern), not a
turn caller:

- **Inbound only enqueues.** `agent.followup` (or `agent.steer` with
  `busyInbound: steer`), never awaiting a turn. An inbound that arrives
  while the agent is mid-turn gets one busy ack per running interval and
  runs as its own turn afterwards.
- **One outbound path for every turn.** Committed session events drive a
  per-conversation send tail that reads forward from a persisted cursor.
  Turns an inbound started (correlated through `agent/inbox/claimed`) are
  `reply` sends; every other turn is `proactive`. A turn with no assistant
  output sends nothing.
- **Exactly-once across restarts** with `outboxPath`: the inbound outbox
  stops redelivered messages re-entering the agent; the outbound cursor
  makes a restart send committed-but-unsent output and never re-send.

Pair it with `tool-jobs.maxConsecutiveWakes` in the profile so a
self-waking job chain cannot spam the chat.

## Concept transfer

| Haven `XmtpChannel` | Here |
| --- | --- |
| `walletAddress` + `signMessage` callback config | the `ctx.wallet` seam: each XMTP signature runs dsh-wallet's resolve → load → sign → drop pipeline |
| `InboundMessage` → MessageBus → AgentLoop session per `sessionKey(channel, chatId)` | one dsh agent per conversation (`ctx.agents.create`, session id `<channelName>-<conversationId>`), inbound via `agent.followup`, output via a `session/event` observer → `conversation.sendText` |
| Disconnected/Connecting/Connected/Reconnecting machine | reconnect loop with the same policy (attempt cap 10, delay 5000ms), reported as `xmtp/status` events |
| `dbEncryptionKey` (raw hex in config) | `dbEncryptionKeyRef` — a `ctx.credentials` reference resolved at each connect |
| `setActiveGroupId()` runtime setter | `activeConversationId` config |
| text-only / own-message / dedup filters, consent auto-allow sweep (15s), dedup cap 5000 → prune to half | preserved verbatim |

Not ported: the installation-limit auto-revocation recovery (deep SDK surface;
revoke stale installations with XMTP tooling if `Client.create` reports the
limit).

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-wallet /path/to/dsh-wallet-ethereum /path/to/dsh-channel-xmtp @xmtp/node-sdk
```

All bundles are independent; each inserts only its own row. `@xmtp/node-sdk`
is an optional peer — the package loads, mounts, and tests without it (lazy
import with an actionable error; tests substitute `internals.sdk`). The
channel requires the agent stack (agents/sessions/llm) present in any
agent-running profile.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: channel-xmtp
  name: 'dsh-channel-xmtp'
  config:
    wallet: agent              # dsh-wallet entry (EVM — XMTP identity is an Ethereum EOA)
    env: production            # production | dev | local
    channelName: xmtp          # session-id prefix; distinguishes parallel mounts
    # dbPath: /var/lib/dsh/xmtp.db3
    # dbEncryptionKeyRef: XMTP_DB_KEY   # credential REFERENCE, never a key value
    # activeConversationId: <id>        # restrict to one conversation
    # maxReconnectAttempts: 10
    # reconnectDelayMs: 5000
    # outboxPath: /var/lib/dsh/xmtp-outbox.json  # inbound outbox + outbound cursors
    # replyMode: turn          # turn: one reply per turn | message: every assistant message live
    # busyInbound: queue       # queue: own turn after the running one | steer: joins the running turn
    # busyAck: "Still working on the previous request — I'll get to this next."  # '' disables

# Recommended alongside: bound background-job wakes per conversation agent.
- id: tool-jobs
  config:
    maxConsecutiveWakes: 3
```

## Events

- `xmtp/inbound` `{ messageId, conversationId, senderInboxId, sentAtMs }` —
  one accepted inbound message (post-filter, pre-agent). Never carries content.
- `xmtp/outbound` `{ conversationId, kind, turn?, inboundMessageId? }` — one
  successful send; `kind` is `reply`, `proactive`, or `ack`. Never carries content.
- `xmtp/status` `{ status, reason }` — connection lifecycle
  (`connecting` / `connected` / `reconnecting` / `disconnected`).

## Custody

The signer's `signMessage` is one `ctx.wallet.signMessage` operation per XMTP
signature request: the wallet credential resolves inside that call and is
dropped on return. Configuration carries wallet *names* and credential
*references* only.

# dsh-exactly-once

Transparent exactly-once guard for DeepSeek Harness write tools. A
`tools/execute` wrapper (the timeout-policy shape) that needs no model
cooperation and adds no tools or parameters:

- **Redelivery dedup by call identity.** One model call block carries one
  `callId`, so a redelivered call shares `(agent, rootCallId, callId)` and
  a model retry does not. Repeats of an in-flight call attach to it;
  repeats of a settled call replay the recorded result. The body runs
  once.
- **Session-ledger repeat evidence.** Canonical values are deliberately
  omitted from durable events and the harness never re-dispatches a
  settled callId after restart (repair closes dangling calls with
  synthetic errors), so the cold path reads last-outcome evidence from
  the `exactlyOnce` session projection — an incremental fold of
  `tool/call` + `tool/result` events, checkpointed with the session —
  instead of replaying successes. A human `user/message` clears the
  evidence inside the fold, matching the `agent/pre-step` reset.
- **Repeat-after-ambiguous checks.** An exact repeat (same agent, tool,
  canonical arguments) following a non-success consults that tool's
  read-back hook when one is registered through
  `ctx.exactlyOnce.registerCheck`; without a hook the call dispatches
  and the attempt is recorded. Ambiguous errors (timeout, abort,
  unclassified throws) carry an attempt trailer; classified failures
  (`INVALID_ARGS`, treasury denials) pass through byte-identical.

Reads and unlisted tools pass through with zero tracking.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-exactly-once
```

`inject = ['tools', 'sessionProjections']` — the projection registry is
required (present in any agent profile via `dsh-base`). The
`agent/pre-step` repeat reset rides the context event without a service
dependency.

## Config

```yaml
- id: exactly-once
  name: 'dsh-exactly-once'
  config:
    writes: ['synapse_pin', '*_submit', 'erc8004_register']  # *-wildcards; default covers the stack writes
    exempt: []  # exempt wins over writes
```

## Tests

```sh
pnpm vitest run dsh-exactly-once/tests/guard.spec.ts
```

Redelivery, replay, transparency, and hook verdicts run through the real
executor; cold-session paths run the wrapper against real sessions whose
`tool/call`/`tool/result`/`user/message` events drive the projection.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- Repeat-after-ambiguous without a registered hook re-dispatches. The
  stack's write surfaces register hooks (`erc8004_register`,
  `rr_launch`/`rr_sweep`/`rr_heartbeat`, `<prefix>_submit`,
  `synapse_pin`, `arkiv_create_entity`/`arkiv_create_entities`/
  `arkiv_update_entity`); XMTP
  answers through its reply outbox instead (a channel, not a tool).
- Cross-conversation retries of one intent need explicit keys (out of
  scope); treasury re-meters replayed successes as estimate noise.

# dsh-haven-aol

Haven-AOL token-gated seal/decrypt/attest for DeepSeek Harness: `ctx.aol` plus six model-facing tools over the `haven-aol` TypeScript SDK and the ICP backend canister (mainnet `3gzy3-kaaaa-aaaan-q6y6q-cai`).

> TEMP: `haven-aol` is not on npm despite its README claim, so `package.json`
> uses `file:../../haven-aol/packages/typescript` (requires `npm install` +
> `npm run build` there first for `dist/`). This breaks isolated-bundle
> installs elsewhere — publish `haven-aol` to npm and revert to `"=0.1.0"`.

## Tools

| Tool | Kind | Versions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aol_gate_info` | read | v1/v3/v4 | Pure metadata parse. v4 includes Bond-pin pre-check. |
| `aol_epoch` | read | — | Current 30-day epoch + rollover (advisory). |
| `aol_market_cap` | read | v4 | Live cap in whole reserve units (300s canister burst cache). Fails closed client-side on non-Bond oracles. |
| `aol_decrypt` | execute | v1/v3/v4 | Full gated decrypt; dispatches on metadata version. Keys never leave the call. |
| `aol_seal` | execute | v1/v3/v4 | Harness-native encrypt: AES-GCM key (shared per epoch bucket for v3, fresh per seal for v1/v4, fresh IV always) + IBE wrap under the canister-fetched DPK. No wallet, no signature. |
| `aol_attest_holding` | execute | — | Canister-signed holding attestation (`payload.attn`, haven-cli single shape bound to the record `sha256_ct`). One signature + one canister call per record; denials surface as tool errors. |

Gate denials (`InsufficientBalance`, `MarketCapNotReached {required, actual}` in whole reserve units, `InvalidSignature`, `InvalidEpoch`, `InvalidOracle`) surface as tool errors the model can report verbatim.

## Sourcing rules

- Pure protocol (derivation preimages, epoch math, metadata build/parse, EIP-712 typed-data builders) is imported from the `haven-aol` SDK verbatim — fixture-pinned across Motoko/Python/TS, never re-derived here.
- v1 canister calls use the SDK's own `canister.ts` wrappers.
- v3/v4 canister calls (`requestDecryptionKeyV3/V4`, `getMarketCap`) are vendored in `src/aol.ts` following the SDK's IDL-factory pattern; record shapes copied from `src/backend/backend.did`. Upstream them to the SDK when convenient.

## The EIP-712 signing spike (resolved via raw-key provider)

The EIP-712 gate signature is the only signing operation. `ctx.wallet.signMessage` is **EIP-191** (personal prefix); the canister verifies `ecrecover` over the **raw EIP-712 digest** (`\x19\x01‖domain‖structHash`). A personal-prefixed signature is rejected with `#InvalidSignature`, and OWS exposes no `signDigest`/`signTypedData` through its Node wrapper (see `spike-ows-eip712.mjs`).

Resolution: skip OWS for the signing wallet — `dsh-wallet-ethereum` with `provider: raw` signs the digest raw via `ctx.wallet.signDigest`, which this plugin already prefers (`runtimeForCall`). No code changes were needed here:

```yaml
- id: wallet
  config:
    wallets:
      agent: { chain: evm, wallet: agent, keyRef: PRIVATE_KEY }
- id: wallet-ethereum
  config: { chains: [evm], provider: raw }
- id: haven-aol
  config:
    wallet: agent
    canisterId: 3gzy3-kaaaa-aaaan-q6y6q-cai
    icpHost: https://icp-api.io
    fetchRootKey: false
```

Without a wired `signDigest` (default OWS path), the `signGate` seam stays **unset and every gated call throws `AolSigningError`** — fail-loud, no silently-invalid signature ever produced. Reads (`aol_gate_info`, `aol_epoch`) and client-side `aol_market_cap` Bond-pin rejection work without any signer.

## Config

```yaml
- id: haven-aol
  config:
    wallet: agent
    canisterId: 3gzy3-kaaaa-aaaan-q6y6q-cai
    icpHost: https://icp-api.io
    fetchRootKey: false   # local replica only — never mainnet
    keyStorePath: /data/haven-aol/keys.json  # optional; unset = memory-only
```

`inject = ['wallet', 'tools']`. `ctx.synapse` is best-effort via `ctx.get()` — `aol_decrypt {cid}` needs `dsh-storage-synapse` mounted, otherwise pass `path`.

## Deferred (deliberately absent)

- `attestHolding` — no wrapper exists in any SDK yet (TS, Python, or here).

Sealing (`aol_seal`) is harness-native: v3/v4 metadata builders and derivation inputs stay SDK-verbatim, the v1 builder is ported from Python `core.py`, file bytes ship in haven-cli's framed chunk layout (`[12-byte base IV][u32LE index][u32LE length][ciphertext+tag]*`, 1 MiB chunks — players refuse unframed payloads over 32 MiB), and the IBE wrap runs against `@icp-sdk/vetkeys` under the **canister-fetched** verification key. Seal here, upload the sealed bytes plus `gateMetadataJson` via the storage tools. Decrypt dispatches on framing, so pre-framing legacy rows stay open.

## Key reuse (epoch buckets)

Upstream Bugs 4–6 fixed in the port: v3 is one key per epoch, not one per file.

- **Seal side** (`EpochAesKeyCache`): one AES key + wrapped blob per `(chain, token, threshold, epoch)` bucket. Every file sealed in the epoch carries the same `encryptedAesKey`; `keySha256` is the bucket commitment. v1 (per-file) and v4 (per-rung — sharing across rungs would let one unlock open later files) still mint per seal. IVs are fresh per seal in all versions, so every seal's bytes stay unique.
- **Decrypt side** (`VetKeyCache`): one signed canister round-trip per bucket, then local unwraps for every file in it. Lookups key off the derivation input from the gate metadata epoch — never the wall clock.
- **Custody**: both caches are memory-first with an optional durable store. The keys are tiny (32-byte AES, 48-byte vetKeys) and append-only, so a configured `keyStorePath` (e.g. `/data/haven-aol/keys.json`) keeps them across restarts in versioned JSON (0600, atomic tmp+rename, merge-on-save across runtimes — the xmtp outbox convention); unset keeps memory-only. Either way there is deliberately no revocation within an epoch (a member who held a bucket key could have saved the unwrapped file keys anyway). Gate denials are never cached.

# dsh-web3

## Quickstart

One-shot get-started (builds latest `02ca906` stack, tests, starts `xmtp-prod`, spits QR + wallet):

```sh
bash quickstart.sh
# or: MUSE_SPARK_API_KEY=<your-key> bash quickstart.sh
```

Spits `Invite URL: https://popup.convos.org/v2?i=...` + ANSI QR (`qrencode -t ANSIUTF8`) and wallet `0xa85dD3FbD8C2c831Ef156036F14638CcFf03b44e` (dynamic `wallet_info`→`ctx.wallet.address`). Also available: `./show-convos-qr.sh` / `./show-xmtp-qr.sh` for QR-only.


Reimplementation of the sovereign web3 agent harness using DeepSeek harness as core, where everything is a plug-in. Replaces https://github.com/Haven-hvn/haven-core and https://github.com/Haven-hvn/haven-adapters

There is deliberately **no aggregate bundle**: people may want one capability
and not another, so each package ships its own `dsh.bundle.patch` →
`cordis.patch.yml` inserting only its own rows, and installs independently:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-haven/<package>
```

## The packages

| Package | Haven concept | dsh seam it lands on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`dsh-wallet`](./dsh-wallet) | `WalletIdentity` custody ("the key never leaves this boundary") + the `CryptoAdapter` contract | `ctx.wallet` service; credentials resolved through `ctx.credentials` per operation — configuration carries *references*, never keys |
| [`dsh-wallet-ethereum`](./dsh-wallet-ethereum) | `EthereumCryptoAdapter` → OWS migration plan | provider plugin registering a `CryptoAdapter` per chain family, backed by `@open-wallet-standard/core` (sign-only; the standard handles all chain families) |
| [`dsh-treasury`](./dsh-treasury) | `Treasury` machine: balances, expenses, FUNDED/LOW/CRITICAL/DEPLETED survival gradient | storage-domain tables + derived state; a policy plugin short-circuits `agent/request` and `tools/pre-execute`, metered off `llm/token-meter` |
| [`dsh-channel-xmtp`](./dsh-channel-xmtp) | `XmtpChannel` direct agent↔user messaging | one dsh agent per conversation (`ctx.agents`), inbound via `agent.followup`, replies via `sendText`; EOA identity signs through `ctx.wallet` |
| [`dsh-storage-synapse`](./dsh-storage-synapse) | `SynapseStorageAdapter` + `StorageBackend` pinning | `ctx.synapse` + `synapse_pin` / `synapse_pin_status` agent tools; every node request wallet-signed per operation |
| [`dsh-wallet-tools`](./dsh-wallet-tools) | wallet address/balance exposure (replaces hard-coded persona) | `wallet_info` tool via `ctx.tools` + `ctx.wallet.address()` live (no hard-coded `0x...`) |
| [`dsh-persona`](./dsh-persona) | Haven persona / system instructions | `agent/request` composition; generic instruction to call `wallet_info` when address/balance/funding asked |
| [`dsh-tool-prowlarr`](./dsh-tool-prowlarr) | Prowlarr indexer search bridge (use-case agnostic) | `prowlarr_indexers` / `prowlarr_search` read-only tools via `ctx.tools`; no wallet seam |
| [`dsh-tool-acquisition`](./dsh-tool-acquisition) | Download/acquisition arm (Haven `acquisition/` port, torrent clients outsourced) | `acquire_submit` / `acquire_status` tools via `ctx.tools`; qBittorrent → Transmission failover, no wallet seam |

## Composition

`dsh-wallet` is the custody root; the other packages build on it:

```
dsh-wallet  ←  dsh-wallet-ethereum   (registers the evm CryptoAdapter)
    ↑
    ├── dsh-channel-xmtp             (signs XMTP identity per signature)
    ├── dsh-storage-synapse          (signs node requests per request)
    └── dsh-wallet-tools             (exposes wallet_info via ctx.tools → ctx.wallet)
dsh-persona                           (composes agent/request; calls wallet_info, no hard-coded address)
dsh-treasury                          (independent; needs the storage stack)
```

A typical full install:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-wallet \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-wallet-ethereum \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-treasury \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-channel-xmtp \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-storage-synapse \
  @open-wallet-standard/core @xmtp/node-sdk
```

The two SDKs are optional peers: every package loads, mounts, and tests
without them (lazy imports with actionable errors; tests substitute
`internals.*` seams).

## Prerequisites

- **Storage stack** (`dsh-treasury` only): the profile must mount `storage`,
  `storage-json`/`storage-sqlite`, and `storage-domain` rows (present in
  `dsh-web-app`; absent in `dsh-base`). The treasury patch does NOT insert
  them — a row id inserted by two layers mounts the plugin twice.
- **Agent stack** (`dsh-channel-xmtp` only): agents/sessions/llm, present in
  any agent-running profile.
- Plugins with unmet `inject` lists stay dormant instead of failing, so
  install order is free.

## Design decision: isolated bundles, coupled seams

Web3 plugins are **isolated as code, coupled at the seam** — a direct consequence of
how the DeepSeek harness composes.

* **Isolated** — every package is a standalone Cordis plugin (`export const name`,
  `export const inject`, `export function apply(ctx, config)`) with its own
  `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`. There is no aggregate bundle; `dsh plugin add`
  installs one capability at a time and `inject` ordering is free (unmet `inject` stays
  dormant). This is why `dsh-wallet`, `dsh-channel-xmtp`, `dsh-storage-synapse`,
  `dsh-treasury`, and `dsh-wallet-tools` each build via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`) and test
  without the others (`internals.*` seams).

* **Coupled at the seam** — isolation would break without declared contracts:
  `ctx.wallet` (custody), `ctx.tools` (model-facing tools), `ctx.agents`/`ctx.sessions`
  (per-conversation agents), `ctx.synapse`/`ctx.treasury` (storage). Plugins declare
  this with `inject` — e.g. `inject = ['wallet','tools']` in `dsh-wallet-tools` and
  `dsh-storage-synapse` — so they mount only when the seam exists, and call it
  per-operation (`ctx.wallet.address()`, `ctx.wallet.signMessage()`, `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))`).

Harness limitations that force this shape:

1. **Singleton tool runtime.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` exposes one scheduler (`ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare`). If two instances are deduped incorrectly the `Symbol` mismatches and every `tool/call` fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`. Bundles therefore depend on `dsh-tools` as a **peer** (`0.2.1-alpha.1`, exact — dsh also rejects a bundle whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers do not match the running CLI) and `link:` installs must dedupe to one copy.

2. **Wallet custody is per-operation.** Configuration carries only `keyRef`/`wallet` names; `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs inside `signMessage`/`address` and is dropped. Consumers (XMTP identity in `dsh-channel-xmtp`, per-request `x-synapse-*` headers in `dsh-storage-synapse`, `wallet_info` in `dsh-wallet-tools`) see only addresses/signatures. Hard-coding an address in persona (`When asked for address, answer with 0x...`) breaks rotation and wallet-agnostic installs — the correct seam is a tool that resolves `ctx.wallet.address(config.wallet)` live.

3. **Channel is per-conversation, not per-process.** `dsh-channel-xmtp` creates one `ctx.agents` session per XMTP conversation (`SessionId` derived from `conversationId`), handles `conversations.sync()` before `getConversationById`, reconnect/consent sweep, and dedup. The channel owns transport; the agent owns the turn.

Result: add `dsh-wallet` once, then compose any subset. `dsh-wallet-tools` (`wallet_info` tool, `presentCall: {kind:'read'}`) makes the EVM address model-reachable without persona shortcuts; `dsh-channel-xmtp` makes it XMTP-reachable; `dsh-storage-synapse` makes it storage-reachable — all through `ctx.wallet`, none by sharing key material.

## Custody model (the through-line)

Haven's rule — *the private key never leaves its layer; everything else
requests signatures* — maps to one dsh pattern used everywhere here:

1. Configuration carries **names and credential references** (`keyRef`,
   `dbEncryptionKeyRef`). A pasted raw key fails loud at plugin load because
   key material cannot syntactically be a `CredentialRef`.
2. Secrets exist only **inside one operation**: `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs
   per call, the provider signs, every reference is dropped. Rotation reaches
   the very next operation without restart.
3. Consumers (XMTP signer, Synapse requests, future channels) see only
   **addresses and signatures** through `ctx.wallet`.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install       # workspace of five packages
pnpm vitest        # specs live in <package>/tests/**
```

Each package builds self-contained via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`), so git or
path installs work without monorepo context. Money figures are integer µUSD
(USD × 1e6) throughout, matching haven-core.
