# @natgurlain/dsh-browser-agent

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

The plugin of [dsh-browser-agent](https://github.com/natgurlain/dsh-browser-agent). It was named `dsh-browser-agent` from v0.3.1 to v0.3.4 and `@natgurlain/dsh-bridge-browser` before; both names are deprecated.

The **browser-operation bridge** for dsh mounts a token-authenticated WebSocket carrier (`/ext/bridge`) for the browser extension, projects its calls onto DSH Typert Remotes, follows Session and Remote Event streams, and registers tools for reading and operating the controlled tab, capturing screenshots, and using developer tools. The browser retains its login state, and the side panel provides the conversation UI.

Page snapshots contain structured text with numbered controls and masked form fields. Actions target element numbers or selectors. Screenshots and chat images use DSH's durable attachment service; deferred sessions expose image limits when the host mounts that service.

## Config

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token` | `string` | generated | Fixed bearer token. When absent, a token is generated on first boot and saved to `~/.dsh/ext-bridge-token` (chmod 0600). The boot log shows the file path. |
| `pairing` | `boolean` | `true` | Let an extension without a token (a store or Brave build, Firefox) ask to pair: its panel shows a six-character code that the user types into DSH. `false` accepts only the provisioned or pasted token and the configured extension IDs. |
| `toolTimeoutMs` | `number` | 90000 | Per-tool-call budget, leaving time for the extension's 60-second approval window. |
| `snapshotMaxChars` | `number` | 32000 | Upper bound on one rendered snapshot's characters, minimum 500 (also negotiated to the extension via `hello.ok` caps). |
| `maxInteractiveItems` | `number` | 60 | Upper bound on interactive inventory items per snapshot. |
| `devToolsMaxChars` | `number` | 24000 | Upper bound on one developer-tools result's characters, minimum 500. |
| `sessionWorkspacePath` | `string` | `~/.dsh/browser-sessions` | Dedicated Host Workspace for extension-created sessions. The plugin creates and idempotently registers the directory on the first implicit `session.create`; the session cwd becomes this path, so the GUI shows a `browser-sessions` workspace group. Set `""` to keep sessions Ungrouped. |
| `deferSessionCreate` | `boolean` | `true` | Sessions materialize only on the first message: `session.create` answers with a provisional id (nothing persisted), history reads empty, and the first `session.prompt` creates the real session (same id, original payload). Opening the panel without chatting leaves zero trace in the session store/GUI. |
| `beacon` | `boolean` | `true` | Also answer the discovery endpoint on a fixed loopback port, so a randomly assigned Web port (DSH Desktop starts its host with `--port 0`) stays discoverable. Binding failures are diagnostics only; the bridge itself is unaffected. |
| `beaconPorts` | `number[]` | `43189…43198` | Candidate beacon ports, tried in order until one binds; the first free port wins, which keeps several local instances discoverable. Ignored when `beacon` is false. |
| `mcp.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Serve a loopback MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP) so Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other MCP clients can drive the browser. See [MCP clients](#mcp-clients). |
| `mcp.port` | `number` | `0` | Loopback port of the MCP endpoint (`0`: any free port; the URL is written to `~/.dsh/browser-mcp.json`). |
| `devLoop.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Turn the dev loop on. While off, the panel cannot list or link coding sessions and nothing is captured. See [Dev loop](#dev-loop-coding-sessions). |
| `devLoop.trustLoopback` | `boolean` | `true` | Loopback dev-loop injections do not taint the coding session. Set `false` if your dev server renders untrusted data; the bridge then also ignores taint-exemption vouchers that rest on a local page. |
| `honorTaintExemptions` | `boolean` | `true` | Honour the extension's taint-exemption vouchers (a browser result read only from the user's own local pages or from sites the user trusts does not taint its session). `false`: every browser result taints. |
| `devLoop.allowedOrigins` | `string[]` | `[]` | Extra exact origins (beyond localhost / 127.0.0.1 / [::1]) a tab may have to be linked to a coding session. See [Dev loop](#dev-loop-coding-sessions). |

Workspace grouping is best-effort. If the composition has no workspace domain, directory creation fails, or `workspace.create` rejects the path, the plugin logs one warning and sends every session creation without an injected workspace so browser chat remains usable.

## Usage

See the root README for [installation, updates, startup, and uninstall](../../../README.md#detailed-installation-and-usage).

## Development

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch` as `./cordis.patch.yml`. The installer registers the local package in the `web` profile, which loads that patch.

The bridge and extension share one pnpm workspace. Bridge source imports `@deepseek-ai/cordis` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` directly, and its DSH dependencies match the workspace's pinned release. The root build builds the bridge before the extension.

The package manifest declares that support itself: `engines.dsh` (`^0.2.2-rc.1`, the releases recorded in `docs/dsh-matrix.md`) and `dsh.manifestVersion: 1` let dsh refuse an incompatible host before loading the plugin, and the Plugins page reads the localized title and description from `locale/en.json` / `locale/zh.json` plus the icon from `icon.svg` without activating the plugin.

## Host methods the panel drives

Beyond plain gateway passthrough (`rpc`), the adapter composes a few Host
methods the side panel needs. They are the panel's only vocabulary for the
composer's permission, model, command, and skill controls, and they are never
offered to the model as tools.

| Panel method | Payload | Host work | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `permission.catalog` | `{}` | `permissionPresets/catalog` | `{ options, defaultOptions, defaultPreset }` |
| `session.permissions` | `{ sessionId }` | the catalog plus the Session's `permissions` projection | `{ current, defaultPreset, options, defaultOptions, routable, provisional }` |
| `session.setPermission` | `{ sessionId, preset }` | validates the preset, then `commands/execute` with `/permission <preset>` | `{ preset, commandId, result }` |
| `commands.list` | `{ sessionId }` | `commands/list` scoped to the Session's agent | `{ commands: [{ name, description, hint?, definitionId? }], provisional }` |
| `commands.execute` | `{ sessionId, line }` | `commands/execute` with the empty attachment list | `{ commandId, result }`; an unknown line is a `bad-request` |
| `skills.list` | `{ sessionId }` | `skills/list` for the Session composition | `{ skills: [{ name, description, whenToUse?, modelInvocable, path? }], provisional }` |

Opening `session.history` activates the Session through `session/follow`; requests with `beforeSeq` use `session/events` for older pages. `session/observeState` supplies the bridge's `session/state` events, and `session/observeProjections` supplies `session/projection` events with `{ sessionId, seq, changes }`.

`session.attachment` takes `{ sessionId, attachment }` with the complete image reference. When the `conversationContinuation` projection permits it and the Session is idle, the panel continues with `session.prompt` and `content: []`. Session deletion waits for the Host's archive-triggered worktree cleanup before removing its log.

Failure semantics: a Host that does not mount the permission service answers
`session.permissions` with `routable: false` instead of failing, so the panel
can hide the control; a method the deployed bridge does not implement answers
`not-found` (`… is unavailable`), which lets a newer panel degrade instead of
breaking. `commands.execute` refuses a line without the Host command grammar,
and an unknown command name from the Host is reported as `bad-request` rather
than an empty success.

## Deferred Sessions

`deferSessionCreate` (default `true`) answers `session.create` with a
provisional id and materializes the real Session on the first `session.prompt`.
Composer methods respect that: a provisional id answers `session.permissions`
from the process catalog plus the remembered choice, `session.setPermission`
records the choice, and materialization replays `/permission <preset>` before
the model selection and before the first prompt is admitted (a failure keeps
the prompt queued for retry instead of running it under the wrong policy).
`commands.list` and `skills.list` need a real agent, so a provisional id
answers empty with `provisional: true`; `commands.execute` accepts only the
permission switch and answers `provisional-session` for everything else.

## Security model

- The bridge route lives **outside** the `/api` trust fence (which only guards client-connection's routes), so it carries its own bearer-token authentication: the first frame must be `hello` with the token within 5s, verified in constant time. Failed auth closes the socket.
- Gateway methods the `/api` carrier pins to loopback (`settings.*`, `credentials.*`, `host.pickDirectory`, `host.openPath`) are refused for non-loopback remotes **even with a valid token** — defense in depth for `--host 0.0.0.0` deployments.
- One active connection at a time; a new authenticated socket replaces the previous one.
- The discovery beacon (`/ext/bridge-config` on a fixed loopback port) only names the bridge URL, the host pid, and its start time. It binds `127.0.0.1`, sends no CORS headers (a web page can see the connection but cannot read the body), rejects a `Host` header that is not `127.0.0.1`/`localhost` on that port (DNS rebinding), and never carries the bearer token. It is skipped entirely when the host binds a non-loopback interface.
- The bridge is a confused-deputy boundary, not a general auth layer: never expose `dsh web --host 0.0.0.0` on untrusted networks.
- **Session taint and its exemption.** Any `browser_*` result taints its session on the Host (shell, file-writing, network and delegation tools off until the panel's Clear), failed results included. The one exception is a result the extension vouched for: a `tool.result` frame carrying `taintExempt: true`, which the extension sets only when everything the result could quote came from the user's own loopback pages or from sites the user marked trusted, and its own record of the session is untainted (`extensions/dsh-browser/README.md`, Taint exemptions). The extension decides because only it sees which frames a result read; the bridge matches the voucher to the exact tool call (session and call id, every extension result of that call) and taints when it is missing, late, or for another call. This keeps the existing trust direction: the paired extension may lower the bridge's restriction (as its Clear does), while the agent and page content cannot, since the flag is on the authenticated frame and not in the result. A snapshot injection carries the same flag; watcher wakes, selections the extension reports, and dev-loop injections outside `devLoop.trustLoopback` always taint. A voucher that rests on a local page carries `taintExemptLocal: true`; the bridge ignores those while `devLoop.trustLoopback` is false, and every voucher while `honorTaintExemptions` is false. What it honours is sent in the server caps (`taintExemptions: { local, trusted }`), so the extension turns the matching exemption off and both records agree. A session with a vouched-exempt read is remembered: calls of its forks and subagents carry `inheritedExemptReads: true`, and the extension then counts an unknown source for them, so no origin is ever such a session's only taint source.
- Extracted page text is marked as untrusted model input. Page reads honor the extension's ask/auto/off policy, while state-changing tools require an origin-scoped side-panel decision and fail closed without a panel. Same-origin repetition can be trusted for the current panel session; permanent trust remains an explicit setting.

## Wire protocol

Frames are JSON objects discriminated by `t`, defined in [`protocol.ts`](src/protocol.ts) and shared with the extension through the workspace package's `./src/*` export. The built package exposes `@natgurlain/dsh-browser-agent/protocol` for external consumers.

- Client → server: `hello` (auth + caps), `rpc` (gateway method passthrough), `respond` (resolve a host interaction by its RPC id), `tool.result`, `pong`.
- Server → client: `hello.ok` (echoes negotiated caps), `rpc.result`, `respond.result` (correlated acceptance or error), `event` (bridge-owned projection of dsh Remote streams and waterfalls), `tool.call`, `tool.cancel`, `ping`, `error`.

Each `respond` carries a globally unique transport id as well as the host interaction's `rpcId`. The extension routes its receipt only to the panel that initiated it and rejects pending responses on timeout, panel closure, or bridge disconnection.

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `browser_snapshot` | Structured text snapshot (title/URL/main/inventory/forms); `delta: true` returns only changes, `frame` reads one iframe, and `query` locates elements by text/selector/role and returns their selectors. |
| `browser_click` | Click or double-click by index or selector; supports mouse buttons and modifiers. |
| `browser_type` | Enter text by index/selector or into the focused element; `replace` selects existing content first, and `mode` chooses caret insertion or per-character keys. |
| `browser_press` | Single keys or chords (`modifiers`), `action: down/up` to hold a key across calls, `repeat` to repeat. |
| `browser_clipboard` / `browser_upload` | Write/paste text and rich HTML; attach local files to a file input (Chrome for system paste and upload). |
| `browser_scroll` / `browser_navigate` / `browser_open_tab` / `browser_back` / `browser_forward` / `browser_reload` | Page scrolling and navigation; `frame` selects an iframe for scrolling. |
| `browser_get_text` / `browser_wait` | Read regions / settle detection. |
| `browser_hover` / `browser_drag` | Real-pointer hover; drag to an element or offset (HTML5 drag-and-drop for draggable sources). |
| `browser_dialog` | Answer the JavaScript dialog blocking the tab (Chrome); blocked calls fail fast with `dialog open: …`. |
| `browser_downloads` | List or wait for downloads; returns local paths (optional `downloads` permission, asked on first use). |
| `browser_save_pdf` / `browser_pdf_text` | Save the tab as a PDF under `<sessionWorkspacePath>/pdf` (Chrome); extract the text of a PDF tab. |

Clicks, text entry, and scrolling run in the selected document, including cross-origin iframes. Chrome uses its debugger for native keyboard events, caret insertion, system paste, and file uploads. Screenshots require an active tab in a focused window; `browser_follow_tab { activate: true }` brings the controlled page to the front.

### Developer tools (high privilege)

This group is registered only while the connected extension advertises the `devTools` capability, which Chrome builds do and Firefox builds do not. Each call requires consent through **Allow developer tools** in Settings, a current side-panel session grant, or a per-call approval (allow once / trust this session / deny). Session trust expires when the last panel closes or the worker restarts. The blanket browser-control switch and the persistent origin allowlist do not cover this group.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `browser_devtools_elements` | Inspect an element (computed CSS, box model, matched rules, attributes) by CSS selector or `browser_snapshot` index. |
| `browser_devtools_set_element_style` / `browser_devtools_set_element_attribute` | Live-debug CSS on an element (inline style or the matched stylesheet rule) and read/set/remove one attribute. Script-capable attributes are refused. |
| `browser_console_eval` / `browser_console_logs` | Run JavaScript in the page's own context (optionally awaiting a promise) and read the console output recorded since attach. |
| `browser_devtools_network` | Start/stop/status network capture for the controlled tab. |
| `browser_devtools_list_requests` / `browser_devtools_get_request` / `browser_devtools_request_body` | List captured requests, read one in full, and fetch a request or response body. Credential headers (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, …) are redacted unless the caller opts in per call, and bodies of authentication-shaped URLs are redacted by default. |

Capture notes: Chrome allows only one debugger per tab, so the browser's own DevTools cannot stay open on a tab while capture is attached; the error names that cause. Capture is in-memory, bounded (200 requests, 500 console entries) and resets on attach and on every top-level navigation. All returned page data is untrusted input.

## MCP clients

With `mcp.enabled: true` the plugin serves an MCP endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`. Other agent harnesses reach it through the `dsh-browser-mcp` stdio shim ([setup for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex](../mcp-server/README.md)).

While the endpoint is enabled, or while the bridge holds workflow schedules for a browser, that browser's extension keeps its bridge connection with no side panel open and reconnects by itself. The bridge says so in the `hello.ok` caps (`standing: { schedules, mcp }`, bound into the server proof) and in a sealed `bridge/standing` event when the schedule count changes; extensions that do not advertise `standingUpdates` are not sent the event. The hint only keeps the connection up: every call still passes the extension's gates.

- **Same tool path.** `tools/list` returns the registered `browser_*` definitions from `ctx.tools`, with the same schemas and descriptions DSH Agents get. `tools/call` runs those same definitions. An execution carries an external-caller marker instead of an Agent (`external-caller.ts`), so every call becomes a normal `tool.call` frame to the extension. The pause gate, site policy, taint rules, kill switch, payload-bound approval cards and the audit log all apply unchanged.
- **One external session per MCP connection.** `initialize` mints `mcp-<uuid>` and records it in the session ledger as *external*. It never counts as an owned DSH session, so every Host session method refuses it (`bridge-policy.ts`), as do snapshot injection and purge. Its audit log stays readable from the panel, and the panel may clear its taint.
- **Approvals.** Each frame carries the client's sanitized, self-reported name as `requester`. The approval card and the OS notification show "Requested by MCP client “<name>”". These approvals are never forwarded to DSH's approval service, because no DSH turn exists to ask. They are answered in the browser only.
- **Hardening.**
  - Binds `127.0.0.1` only and refuses non-loopback peers.
  - Uses a separate 0600 token (`~/.dsh/browser-mcp-token`), compared in constant time.
  - Refuses any `Origin` header (browser CSRF) and any `Host` other than the loopback address and bound port (DNS rebinding).
  - Accepts JSON bodies only, with a 1 MB cap. JSON-RPC batches are not supported.
  - Allows at most 16 sessions and expires them after 1 h idle. `DELETE` ends a session, and a dropped HTTP request cancels its call and withdraws its card.
- **Refusals.** Tools that write into a DSH workspace (`browser_save_pdf`, `browser_extract { saveTo }`) refuse MCP callers. `browser_screenshot` returns an MCP image block.

## Dev loop (coding sessions)

The dev loop is off until the Host operator sets `devLoop.enabled: true` in the bridge-browser plugin config.

In **Settings → Dev loop**, open a localhost page (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`) in the panel's window. Click "Link this tab to a coding session…" and pick one of your DSH coding sessions. Only sessions on a restricted permission preset (`read-only`, `workspace-write`, or a preset the operator lists as safe) are offered or can be linked; a session on `danger-full-access`, `auto` or an unknown preset never is, and a linked session switched to such a preset is unlinked at its next capture. The picker sees only each session's id and title (never its directory, project or run state). Bridge sessions are never offered, nor are subagent or MCP sessions. After each turn of that session that edited files (a successful `edit`, `write`, `apply_patch`, `str_replace_editor` or `notebook_edit`), the following happens:

1. The bridge sends the reserved `browser_devloop_capture` action to the extension. It is an ordinary `tool.call`, so the pause gate, kill switch, site policy, taint rules, read-approval settings and the audit log all apply. It is not a model tool, and it is never served over MCP.
2. The extension refuses the action unless that session has a link made in this browser, and unless the linked tab is still on the linked origin.
3. Otherwise it answers with:
   - the console errors, uncaught exceptions and failed `fetch`/XHR requests that a small main-world collector recorded since the previous turn;
   - a `browser_snapshot { delta: true }` of the page.

   If that page read is refused, nothing from the page is shared.
4. The bridge injects the answer into the session as read-only browser context, inside an untrusted boundary the bridge writes itself (fresh nonce per injection; any boundary text from the extension or the page stays inside it). The injection does not wake the session. The model sees it with the user's next message.

Rules that still hold:

- **Linking is not prompting.** The session still cannot be prompted, steered, re-permissioned or snapshot-injected from the browser (`bridge-policy.ts`).
- **Origins.** Only loopback origins by default. `devLoop.allowedOrigins` (exact `http(s)://host[:port]`) adds others.
- **Taint.** By default (`devLoop.trustLoopback: true`) an injection does **not** taint the coding session on the Host when every origin the capture read (the linked page and each of its frames) is loopback. That taint would make its edit tools read-only and break the loop. The source is the user's own dev server, and the payload is fenced as untrusted text. An injection that read any non-loopback origin (a third-party iframe, an allowed non-loopback origin, or a capture that cannot say which origins it read) **does** taint it. On the browser side, the capture taints that session's browser actions like any other page read.
- **Caveat.** A local dev server that renders untrusted data (user-generated content, scraped or proxied pages) can put that text into the coding session through the dev loop. For such apps, set `devLoop.trustLoopback: false`: loopback injections then taint the session like any web content.
- **Lifetime.** Links live in the bridge's memory and in the extension's session storage. After DSH restarts, opening the panel's settings re-asserts them. A link ends when its tab closes, and the kill switch removes every link on both sides.

## Browser subagent and skills

- **Agent preset `browser`.** When the Host has the agent-preset registry, the plugin registers a preset with one row, `lib/browser-preset.js`. That row restricts the agent's tools to the registered `browser_*` tools, and to `skill` when that tool is global. It re-applies the restriction when the developer-tools group comes or goes, and it adds a short role prompt. You can also start a session on the "Browser" preset directly in DSH.
- **Delegation: `delegate_browser_task { task, label? }`.** The plugin registers this tool for every agent when the Host has the subagent manager with the in-process `spawn` backend (the shipped web profile has it). The tool runs the task in a child agent on the `browser` preset and returns only the child's summary, so large page snapshots never enter the caller's context. A tainted session cannot delegate: the taint guard denies it. The child is linked into the bridge's taint lineage (its session header names the caller), so its page reads taint the caller and delegation cannot launder page content. No profile change is needed.
- **Skills.** The package ships `skills/*/SKILL.md`: `fill-form-safely`, `extract-table-to-csv`, `research-across-tabs` and `debug-localhost-page`. They are registered on `ctx.skills` as bundled skills, so the `skill` tool lists them for every session.

## Extension points

- The tool set is the consumer surface; the seam is the bridge wire (`protocol.ts`). Add tools by registering on `ctx.tools` and dispatching over the bridge; the extension's content script dispatches by action name.
- Negotiated caps (`hello.ok`) let the plugin dictate snapshot budgets to the extension without a shared config file.

## Known limitations

- One active extension connection at a time.
- Accessible cross-origin iframes are snapshotted and operated with stable `(frame, index)` addresses. Restricted or short-lived frames are reported as unavailable without failing the whole page snapshot.
- Token rotation is manual (edit `~/.dsh/ext-bridge-token` or set `token` in config); no expiry. An extension that obtained the token by pairing must pair again after a rotation.
- Pairing (for extensions without an installer-written token) is a password-authenticated key exchange keyed by a six-character code the extension shows and the user types into DSH; see `docs/store/README.md`. Paired extensions (Chrome IDs and Firefox origins) are kept in `~/.dsh/browser-paired-extensions.json` and can be unpaired in DSH Settings or with `/browser-pair unpair <extension>`: the extension's connection is closed and its origin refused. Unpairing does not take the token back; "Reset bridge token" (or `/browser-pair reset-token`) replaces it and disconnects every browser. A Firefox extension that is reinstalled gets a new origin, so for Firefox only the token reset is a complete cut-off.

# dsh-browser-agent

**English** | [中文](README.zh.md)

Let [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) work in the browser you already use. The agent reads the page you are on, clicks, types, navigates and manages tabs, in your own Chrome, Brave or Firefox (other Chromium browsers should work too), with your logins and cookies, and you watch and approve what it does from a side panel.

<div align="center">
  <video src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a71fb20-f4c0-46be-b9fa-c8b64f15f2ba" width="900" controls></video>
</div>

<p align="center"><sub>Auto approve in 33 seconds: a form filled in from an email, timesheets approved, three shops compared. A real recording of the extension; the model's replies are scripted and the pages are local demo pages. <a href="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a71fb20-f4c0-46be-b9fa-c8b64f15f2ba">Direct link to the video</a>.</sub></p>

> Based on [dsh-browser](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-browser) by Yuxiang Lin and contributors (MIT). See [NOTICE](NOTICE).

**Contents:** [What it is](#what-it-is) · [Why this one](#why-this-one) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Install from a release](#install-from-a-release) · [Core capabilities](#core-capabilities) · [Detailed installation and usage](#detailed-installation-and-usage) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) · [Development](#development) · [Security](#security)

## What it is

Two parts that ship together in this repository:

- **A browser extension** (Manifest V3) with a side panel for the conversation. It turns the page into structured text with a numbered list of everything you can interact with, and carries out the agent's actions in the real tab.
- **A DSH plugin** (the "bridge") that gives DSH the `browser_*` tools and talks to the extension over a local, authenticated connection.

It works with the DeepSeek Harness desktop app and with `dsh web`, uses whatever models you have configured there, and can also be driven from Claude Code, Cursor or Codex through MCP.

## Why this one

- **Your real browser, not a robot browser.** No separate profile, no re-login, no headless window: the agent works in the tab you are looking at.
- **You stay in charge.** Actions that change something show an approval card with exactly what will be clicked, typed or opened. You can pause, take over the page, or hit Stop, which cuts everything off at once.
- **Built for hostile pages.** Once the agent has read a web page, sending data to another site, the clipboard or a file asks first, and shell and file tools are switched off for that conversation, so a page that tries to hijack the agent has nowhere to send what it finds. Banking, password and cloud-console sites are read-only by default.
- **A locked front door.** The extension and DSH prove themselves to each other on every connection with a shared secret that never crosses the wire; other programs and other extensions on your machine cannot connect.
- **A record of everything.** Every action, approval and stop is written to a tamper-evident audit log you can export.
- **More than clicking.** Tables to CSV, PDFs, downloads, file uploads, hover and drag, dialogs, parallel reading across tabs, page watchers, and saved workflows you can replay or schedule.
- **Comfortable to use.** Light and dark them

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-cnblogs [![check](https://github.com/Niobium-41-nb/dsh-cnblogs/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Niobium-41-nb/dsh-cnblogs/actions/workflows/check.yml) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-cnblogs)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-cnblogs) [![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Niobium-41-nb/dsh-cnblogs)](https://github.com/Niobium-41-nb/dsh-cnblogs/blob/master/LICENSE) A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that lets the agent publish to **博客园 (cnblogs)** on its own: list and read posts, create or update one from a markdown file, upload the images the markdown references, and manage categories, tags and 闪存. It registers eight `cnblogs_*` tools, starts no daemon, listens on no port, and keeps the personal access token out of the configuration. It talks to the same HTTP endpoints as the official [`cnblogs/vscode-cnb`](https://github.com/cnblogs/vscode-cnb) extension (`write.cnblogs.com/api` for posts, `api.cnblogs.com/api` for the account and 闪存), so a blog driven from the editor and a blog driven by the agent are the same blog. The published write-up (in Chinese, written and published by this plugin): [让 Agent 自己发博客：dsh-cnblogs 插件](https://www.cnblogs.com/vanadium-23/p/23781111/dsh-cnblogs). Install into a profile — `dsh.bundle.patch` inserts its row, so no hand-written profile patch is needed: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cnblogs ``` > 中文完整说明见下方 [中文文档](#中文文档)。 ## Tools | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | `cnblogs_account` | `status` verifies the token and reports the account; `save` stores a token after verifying it; `clear` forgets it | | `cnblogs_list_posts` | One page of posts with ids, state, dates and view counts; optional title search and category filter | | `cnblogs_get_post` | One post as markdown plus tags, categories, state and URL; the body is capped by `maxBodyChars` | | `cnblogs_save_post` | Create or update a post from `file` or inline `body`; rehosts images; reads the post back and reports `verified` | | `cnblogs_delete_posts` | Deletes posts by id and reports per-id failures | | `cnblogs_upload_image` | Uploads one local file, remote URL or data URL and returns the hosted URL | | `cnblogs_taxonomy` | Lists categories (ids, counts) and tags; creates and deletes categories | | `cnblogs_ings` | Lists, publishes and comments on 闪存 | `cnblogs_save_post` is the one that replaces the editor workflow: pass a local markdown file and the post id recorded for that file is reused, so saving the same file again updates the published post instead of creating a duplicate. ## Token Create a personal access token at , then pick one source: 1. **Environment** — `CNBLOGS_PAT` in the environment of the harness process. 2. **Token file** — `/dsh-cnblogs/token`, one token per line. The plugin creates this file on start as a comment-only template (an untouched template still means "no token"), and `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/init-token.mjs` creates it on demand. The token is read on every call, so writing the file is enough — no restart. 3. **Inline configuration** — `token` in the plugin's `cordis.yml` row. Discouraged: configuration files get synced and shared. `cnblogs_account` action `save` also works, but a token passed as a tool argument is recorded in the session log, so prefer the environment or the file. When the harness credential service is available the plugin stores the token as the `CNBLOGS_PAT` credential record instead of a file; the file is the fallback. ## Front matter A post file may open with a YAML block. The plugin reads it, removes it from the uploaded markdown (a `---` rule renders as a horizontal line), and lets explicit tool arguments win over it. `keepFrontMatter: true` in the configuration keeps the block. ```markdown --- title: 用 DeepSeek Harness 发布博客园 tags: [dsh, cnblogs] categories: - 后端 status: publish slug: publish-with-dsh summary: 一段摘要 --- 正文…… ``` Recognized keys: `title`, `tags`, `categories`, `status` (`draft` / `publish`), `access` (`public` / `login` / `owner`), `slug`, `summary`, `pinned`, `comments`, `postId`. ## Images `cnblogs_save_post` scans markdown images and `` tags: - relative and absolute local paths are uploaded, then rewritten to the blog's image host; - base64 `data:image/...` URLs are uploaded and replaced; - images already on a `*.cnblogs.com` host are left alone; - third-party HTTP images are left alone unless `extractWebImages` is on (rehosting them uploads someone else's image to the blog); - an image that cannot be uploaded is reported in `imagesFailed` and left unchanged, so the post is still saved. `cnblogs_upload_image` handles the case where the URL itself is needed. ## Configuration | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | Mount the tool set | | `token` / `tokenFile` | `''` / `/token` | Inline token, or the file to read | | `stateDir` | `/dsh-cnblogs` | File → post mappings, cached account, token file | | `blogBackend` / `openapi` | cnblogs URLs | Base URLs; override only for a compatible host | | `timeoutMs` | `30000` | Per-request deadline | | `maxBodyChars` | `200000` | Largest body accepted; also the default read cap | | `maxUploadBytes` | `10485760` | Largest single image | | `extractImages` / `extractWebImages` | `true` / `false` | Rehost local and data URLs / also third-party URLs | | `keepFrontMatter` | `false` | Keep the YAML block in the published markdown | | `defaultStatus` / `defaultAccess` | `draft` / `public` | Applied to a **new** post when the caller is silent | | `promptSection` | `true` | Add the short usage section to the system prompt | ## What it does not do These are editor-side features of `vscode-cnb` that do not belong in an agent tool set: - PDF export — needs a local Chromium; use the harness's browser tooling instead. - Blog backup export/download — a long-running server job with a zip download. - Clipboard image upload — a tool argument is the boundary; pass a file or a data URL. - Workspace activation — there is no editor workspace; every tool acts on an explicit path or id. - Browser OAuth login — the agent has no browser session; a personal access token plays that role. ## Development ```bash pnpm install --ignore-scripts node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc -b tsconfig.json node node_modules/tsdown/dist/run.mjs node --experimental-strip-types tests/unit.test.mjs # 106 checks node --experimental-strip-types tests/plugin.test.mjs # 66 checks node tests/bundle.smoke.mjs # 10 checks, needs a build node --experimental-strip-types tests/live.check.mjs # read-only live check, needs a token ``` The plugin test mounts the real `apply()` against a fake Cordis context and an in-memory cnblogs backend, so it covers request building, the file mapping, image rewriting, failure paths and every tool's output schema without touching the network. **A live-endpoint run needs your own token**; until then the request shapes are verified only against the endpoints read from `vscode-cnb` 1.8.58 and the fake backend. --- ## 中文文档 ### 它是什么 `dsh-cnblogs` 让 DeepSeek Harness 的 Agent **自己把文章发到博客园**：列博文、读博文、按本地 Markdown 新建或更新博文、把文中引用的图片转存到博客园图床、管理分类/标签、看和发闪存。 推介文章（由本插件自己写出并发布）： [让 Agent 自己发博客：dsh-cnblogs 插件](https://www.cnblogs.com/vanadium-23/p/23781111/dsh-cnblogs)。 它调用的是博客园官方 VS Code 扩展 [`cnblogs/vscode-cnb`](https://github.com/cnblogs/vscode-cnb) 的同一套 接口，所以「编辑器发的」和「Agent 发的」是同一个博客、同一批博文。 八个工具： | 工具 | 作用 | |---|---| | `cnblogs_account` | 验证令牌并报告账号；保存令牌；清除令牌 | | `cnblogs_list_posts` | 一页博文（id、状态、时间、阅读数），可按标题搜索、按分类过滤 | | `cnblogs_get_post` | 读一篇博文的 Markdown 正文与元数据（正文超过上限会截断并说明） | | `cnblogs_save_post` | 按文件或内联正文新建/更新；自动转存图片；保存后**读回校验**并报告 `verified` | | `cnblogs_delete_posts` | 按 id 删除，逐个报告失败原因 | | `cnblogs_upload_image` | 上传单张图片（本地文件 / 网络 URL / Base64），返回图床 URL | | `cnblogs_taxonomy` | 列分类（含 id 与篇数）、列标签、新建分类、删除分类 | | `cnblogs_ings` | 闪存：列表、发布、评论 | ### 安装 **从 npm 装（推荐）** —— `dsh.bundle.patch` 会自己把这行 `insert` 挂进 `dsh.profile.bundles`： ```bash DSH="/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd" "$DSH" plugin --profile web add dsh-cnblogs ``` **从源码装**（改代码时用）—— pnpm 的 `file:` 依赖按内容快照安装，改完要 `remove` 再 `add`： ```bash cd dsh-cnblogs pnpm install --ignore-scripts pnpm build "$DSH" plugin --profile web add file:/dsh-cnblogs ``` 装好后模型会多出 8 个 `cnblogs_*` 工具（新进程生效）。 ### 令牌怎么给 在 创建个人访问令牌（PAT），然后三选一： 1. **环境变量**：harness 进程的 `CNBLOGS_PAT`； 2. **令牌文件**：`/dsh-cnblogs/token`，一行一个令牌。插件启动时会把这个文件**建成一个只有注释的模板** （模板没填就等于「还没有令牌」）；文件不存在也可以手动生成：`node --experimental-strip-types scripts/init-token.mjs`。 令牌是**每次调用现读**的，所以写进文件就生效，不用重启； 3. **配置里的 `token`**：不推荐，配置文件会被同步、被看到。 不建议让 Agent 用「把令牌贴进对话」的方式保存：工具参数会进会话日志。`cnblogs_account` 的 `save` 只是给「用户已经主动贴了」的情况兜底。 ### 一次发布长什么样 ``` cnblogs_save_post({ file: "E:/blog/我的文章.md" }) → 读文件、拆 front matter、取模板或已有博文 → 找到相对路径图片，逐张上传到博客园并改写链接 → POST /posts，拿到 id 与 URL → GET /posts/{id} 读回，比较标题与正文 → 结果：created post #123、state、verified: ok、warnings ``` 同一个文件再存一次就是**更新**，不是新建：插件把 `文件 → 博文 id` 记在 `/dsh-cnblogs/state.json` 里（权限 0600）。换机器或换目录时用 `postId` 显式指定。 ### 关于「已验证」 - **单元 + 装配测试共 172 项**（106 + 66），覆盖 front matter、图片发现与改写、分类解析、令牌来源、 令牌模板、状态文件、新建/更新、图片转存、删除、失败路径，并逐一校验每个工具的输出结构与其声明一致； 另有 10 项针对**构建产物** `lib/index.js` 的冒烟检查。 - **真实接口尚未验证**：那需要一个真实的 PAT。请求的形状来自官方扩展 1.8.58 的源码 （`rs/src/cnb/**`、`src/service/**`），本地用一个内存假后端跑通了全流程。两个接口主机已确认可达且 未认证时返回 401（`write.cnblogs.com/api/posts/list`、`api.cnblogs.com/api/users`）。 - 写好令牌后，用**只读**检查确认：`node --experimental-strip-types tests/live.check.mjs` —— 它只调用「查账号」和「列 3 篇博文」，不写、不删、不发。 ### 明确不做的事 PDF 导出（需要本地 Chromium）、博客备份导出/下载（服务端长任务 + zip）、剪贴板上传（工具参数边界之外）、 工作空间自动激活（没有编辑器工作空间）、浏览器 OAuth 登录（Agent 没有浏览器会话，用 PAT 代替）。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# SoloPup Memory **让 DSH 记住你的工作偏好和项目约定，下次继续时少一些重复交代。** SoloPup 是 DeepSeek Harness（DSH） 的文字记忆插件。它尝试保存值得长期保留的信息，帮助 DSH 在后续工作中找回并参考。**当前稳定版为 0.26.0。** 记忆可能保存或召回失败，重要内容请核对。 [安装稳定版](docs/guides/quickstart.md) · [0.26.0 发行页](https://github.com/OakcoderX/solopup-memory/releases/tag/v0.26.0) · [历史评测](docs/runs/2026-11-18-memory-delivery.md) · [历史 12 题逐题成绩](docs/runs/2026-11-20-frontiermemory-text.md) · [做梦交互演示](https://oakcoderx.github.io/solopup-memory/dreaming/) · [0.24 做梦历史实验](docs/research/dreaming-in-dsh/README.md) · [更多示意案例](docs/README.md) · [常见问题](docs/faq.md) · [English](README.en.md) ## 试用 0.27.0-beta.2 的闲置更正 **项目约定改了，下次打开 DSH 就能用。** 为选定项目开启自动应用（`dream.autoApply`）后，SoloPup 会在闲置时核对本次运行收到的明确更正。能对上原话和唯一一条现行约定时，它会更新受支持的一个值，保留原有条件和例外。做梦报告会列出改了什么、依据哪条消息。自动应用默认关闭，试行或证据不足的更正留待复核。 [设置、查看回执与撤回](docs/dream-review.md) 同一台 Mac 上用 DSH 和 DeepSeek Flash 跑了一次对照。后台**只出报告花了 600 token**，重启后新会话仍回答「正式交付用中文」。**自动应用花了 605 token**，重启后回答「正式交付用英文」。内部审片批注用中文的例外在两组都保留。这个结果来自普通 DSH 的一个语言更正案例。 [实测设置、前后台用量与结果](docs/runs/2026-11-25-dream-auto.md) 新版也能在受支持的宿主上打开记忆对应的 DSH 原消息，查看本轮实际保存了什么、模型请求里带了什么、交付文件核对到了哪一版。 [本版完整更新](RELEASE.md) 日常使用请安装上方的稳定版。单独试用时请先备份，再安装指定的测试版。新版刚发布时，也可以下载核对过的归档离线安装。 [测试版下载与校验](https://github.com/OakcoderX/solopup-memory/releases/tag/v0.27.0-beta.2) ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add solopup-memory@0.27.0-beta.2 --ignore-scripts ``` ## DSH 养鱼：换个会话，大肥鱼还记得你刚改的称呼吗？ 如果你在 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的原生文字会话**里养大肥鱼、聊看片单或一起写点东西，可以用 SoloPup Memory 试着保存几条长期偏好。它不是桌宠，也不接管 QQ、B 站机器人或其他插件的记忆库。如果你用的桌宠已经有独立记忆，先用同一方法测试现有方案，不必叠装。 **三步自测：** 在不含私人资料的试用工作区，先说「记住：只在这个养鱼测试工作区叫我小柚」，看到正式写入成功后，再说「把这个工作区的称呼改成小栗，替换旧称呼，不是再加一个」。确认替换成功，然后在**同一工作区开不继承历史的新会话**，只问「这个工作区你该怎么称呼我？可以给我看你依据的原话吗？」不要在新会话里透露答案。 答「小栗」且能指出更正的来源，是这次召回的预期结果。再换到一个没有这条约定的工作区问一次，那里不应沿用这个项目称呼。如果仍答旧称呼，或工具显示待审、拒绝、未应用，就不要记作成功。这是可以自己复跑的虚构案例。试用时请检查是否真正写入和召回。 [完整养鱼教程：改称呼与新会话自测](docs/guides/dsh-fish-memory.md) · [开始安装和核对版本](docs/guides/quickstart.md) · [如何验证跨会话记忆](docs/guides/fresh-chat.md) ## 用起来是什么感觉？ **改哪一稿，交回的文件末行对不对？** 在普通会话首行写 `本轮稿本：审读版`。已保存且带稿本条件的项目约定就能按本轮选择判断适用性。对已按约定格式保存的精确末句，DSH 可以重新读取作者指定的 Markdown 文件并返回核验结果。[选稿与核验示例](docs/guides/manuscript-delivery.md) 下面是**虚构的使用示意**，帮助理解用途，并非实测对话： **今天，你说：**“记住，我希望邮件简洁、礼貌，不要太正式。”
**SoloPup：** 检查并尝试保存这条偏好。 **以后，你说：**“帮我写一封会议后的感谢邮件。”

原话来源会怎样返回？ 下面是 **2026-11-07 在 Linux x64 / Node v24.22.1 实际执行的离线示例输出**，使用虚构消息、生产工具处理函数和脚本化宿主；审查回复由测试桩固定通过。写入、同项目检索、另一项目检索分别在三个新 Node 进程中运行，后两者不继承旧消息。**这不是实际 DSH 聊天或真实模型的语义验收。** ```text synthetic user: 记住：本项目的交付说明统一用中文。 memory_write: recorded (scope=project, meaning=decision) fresh process / memory_search("交付说明"): 1 hit (scope=project) current text: - [project] 本项目的交付说明统一用中文 — 索引摘要 history source: synthetic-demo-write:1; quote: 记住：本项目的交付说明统一用中文。 other project / current + history: 0 + 0 hits ``` 当前查询返回有效摘要；另一次 `memory_search({query: "交付说明", mode: "exact", view: "history"})` 返回原话及消息来源，历史内容不能当作当前指令。以上六行是工具结果摘要，完整返回值和局限见[运行记录](docs/runs/2026-11-07-source-recall.md)。在源码目录运行 `node scripts/demo-source-recall.mjs` 可复现；真正的[换聊天验收](docs/guides/fresh-chat.md)仍需在 DSH 中另做。 ## 个人资料与按需读取 已识别的生日、性别、健康、亲密关系和私人联系方式默认不进入自动索引投影，也不作为无关后台整理或写入审查的旧记忆发送。普通 `memory_search` 默认隐藏这些内容；用户询问相关资料时，才明确使用 `includePrivate: true`。主题文件含有未分段的敏感内容时，普通搜索会保守跳过整个主题文件，安全的索引摘要仍可检索。 这是内容规则提供的降载保护，不是完整的隐私分类器。未识别的改写仍可能漏过；文件工具仍能读原始文件，按需读取结果也会进入当前会话日志和模型请求。此版本没有把原始 `MEMORY.md` 改成无明文的指针库，没有擦除既有日志、缓存、备份或已发送数据。`memory_forget` 表示停止使用索引条目，不表示彻底删除个人信息。 ## 工作过程 1. 从本会话已接收的用户消息提出候选，并绑定原话引用。 2. 独立检查持久价值、归属、措辞、认识类型、适用条件、信念归属和修订关系。审查不能改写候选。 3. 通过检查后才发布到有效记忆。明确拒绝的不写入；无法判断的新候选可以留在不自动注入的待审区。未通过的替换请求不降格成普通追加。 4. 后续对话自动得到受预算限制的索引；检索同时查当前项目与全局库，结果标明归属。其他项目不会因此自动变成当前项目的记忆。 用户明确要求记住持久信息时，插件指令要求本轮使用正式 `memory_write`，等待实际结果再确认；不等待后台整理。本人陈述的个人资料按未独立核实的 `claim` 保存，助手猜测不能冒充本人确认。模型仍可能不遵循指令，因此需要实际调用与新会话验收。 默认每四轮尝试一次后台整理。主动 `memory_write` 也经过来源审查。`pending-review`、`rejected`、`not-applied` 都不表示已经记住。 ## 记忆的层次 | 层次 | 内容与用途 | |---|---| | 来源 | 用户原话与消息身份；工具观察另带当时输出的核对证书 | | 候选 | 尚待判断的解释；待审内容不进入常规有效记忆 | | 有效记忆 | 全局个人约定或当前项目内容，带条件、例外及可选期限 | | 修订历史 | 解释旧值与新值的关系；旧值不能继续冒充当前默认值 | | 认识状态 | 偏好、决定、未核实主张、暂定信念、价值取向、查证入口和经历分别表示 | “我负责剪辑”可以保存为本人报告的分工，但不等于外部事实已被独立证实。信念可以保留竞争解释和反证条件；这不是完整的 POMDP 概率求解器。记忆也不构成发邮件、购买、删除或发布的操作授权。 ## 存储与修改 Markdown 索引和主题正文便于阅读；来源、候选、历史与调用记录使用有格式校验的本地账本；独立 SQLite 控制库维护受管身份、撤回和协调状态。不要只备份 Markdown 就认为已完整备份系统。 改同一条约定的值时，`supersedes` 指向唯一现行旧行，默认保留原来的归属、认识类型、条件、例外和期限及其来源。改变这些边界时使用完整重述路径 `revisionMode=replace`，由本轮用户来源支持全部新内容。仅确认“其他项目也一样”不应再建副本。兼容补充不自动变成一般规则的例外。 条件全部成立才满足 `conditions`；任何一个例外成立就命中 `except`。同一条件不能既必须成立又必须排除。来源上限超出时明确拒绝，不截掉必要来源来凑数。 ## 跨 worktree 项目记忆（0.23 测试版） 以下功能从 0.23.0-beta.1 开始提供，不属于 0.22.0-beta.3。默认各工作目录仍使用各自的项目库。若主 Agent 与 Worker 使用同一 Git 仓库的不同 worktree，可在源码或安装包目录中通过本地命令显式关联： ```sh node scripts/projects.mjs link --cwd /path/to/worker-worktree --owner /path/to/project-worktree # 核对预览后，将返回的 reviewed 填入： node scripts/projects.mjs link --cwd /path/to/worker-worktree --owner /path/to/project-worktree --apply --reviewed-link ``` 来源目录须已有项目库；Worker 若已有独立项目库，命令会拒绝，不会合并或覆盖。关联会检查本地仓库身份，不自动关联克隆；仓库或文件系统迁移后可能需要重新登记。取消关联同样先预览、再使用 `reviewed` 执行，且不删除记忆： ```sh node scripts/projects.mjs unlink --cwd /path/to/worker-worktree node scripts/projects.mjs unlink --cwd /path/to/worker-worktree --apply --reviewed-link ``` 取消关联只改变之后的目录解析，不是运行中任务的即时撤权：已解析出的项目库路径、正在处理的捕获任务及已进入会话的内容不会因此自动失效或删除。需要停止使用该共享关系时，先停止相关 Worker 和记忆捕获，再取消关联；历史副本须另行检查。 超级 Agent 的准备命令可以在创建 worktree **之后**，显式追加以下命令，自动登记该次 Worker 目录。请将路径替换为本机的绝对路径；这是一项用户主动配置，不会自动改写超级 Agent 设置。若创建或登记失败，本次启动会停止；超级 Agent 原型重试时可能因目录已存在而跳过准备命令，不能直接重试，须先检查残留目录并确保准备步骤会重新执行。 ```sh node /absolute/path/to/solopup-memory/scripts/superagent-worktree.mjs --owner /absolute/path/to/project-worktree --apply ``` 该命令读取超级 Agent 提供的 `DSH_SUPERAGENT_DIR`，仍执行同仓库和已有独立库检查；`--apply` 表示用户在准备配置中授权执行关联。 在测试的超级 Agent 原型中，Worker 的默认工具限制不开放 `memory_search` 或 `memory_write`。关联可以让已登记的项目记忆进入 Worker 上下文，但不表示 Worker 可直接调用这些记忆工具；不要将其视为 Worker 主动写入记忆的支持。 关联不会清除已发送给模型或保存在普通会话中的副本。真实模型语义质量和全部跨平台环境尚未验收。 从 0.23.0-beta.2 起，记忆协议提示模型在任务历史与长期记忆不一致时核对来源、范围和时间；用户明确更正后按新要求工作，无法判断时向用户澄清。提示不能保证模型一定判断正确，也不会自动更改历史任务、清除会话副本或代替现有记忆写入审核。Worker 未配置记忆工具时，不能声称已经写入记忆。 ## # dsh-peak-cost [![CI](https://github.com/ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://github.com/ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost/releases) [![CodeQL](https://github.com/ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost/actions/workflows/codeql.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost/security/code-scanning) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) A [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/en/guide/quickstart) plugin that adds one ambient line under the composer: ```text ● Off-peak · ≈ $0.338 · bal $7.27 ``` ![The composer dock line in DeepSeek Harness: peak status, session estimate and account balance, to the right of the shipped step counter and token meter](assets/composer-dock.png) It answers three questions about the session you are in: 1. **Is DeepSeek billing in peak hours right now?** 2. **How much has this session cost so far, in US dollars?** 3. **What is left in your DeepSeek account?** Hovering the line opens a panel with the cost attribution: the billing window and the time until it flips, the account balance and both wallets, and a per-category table showing what each kind of content cost when it first entered the context versus what it costs on every later call that re-sends it. The screenshot above is unedited: the line sits beside the shipped turn/step counter and token meter, and reads `● Off-peak · ≈ $0.338 · bal $7.27` for a session at 9 turns and 264 steps with a 99.6% cache hit rate.

## Behavior | | | |---|---| | Slot | `conversation.composer.dock` (below the composer card, beside the shipped activity and context-usage entries) | | Scope | Per session | | Updates | Spend follows every settled model call; the status label re-evaluates against the clock every 30 s; the balance refreshes every 60 s | | Locales | English and Chinese, following the app's language setting | ### Balance Next to the session estimate the line also shows your DeepSeek account balance: ```text ● Off-peak · ≈ $0.18 · bal ¥7.26 ``` It is read from the Host's account Remote (`ctx.remote.account.getBalance`) every 60 seconds and whenever the window regains focus — the same call the Settings → Account page makes — and **both wallet kinds are summed**: the recharge wallet plus any bonus/grant wallet, which is why it can differ from a single number on a top-up page. The panel always lists both. The account face is a Typert Remote namespace rather than a plain service, so the plugin captures it through a scoped `ctx.inject(['remote.account'], …)` and still falls back to `ctx.remote.account` on the root context. That keeps it independent of load order: the cost line renders immediately, and the balance appears as soon as the transport is reachable. The balance is optional in every direction: a signed-out account, an API-key-only setup, a failed read, or a build without the account transport all simply drop it, leaving the cost line intact. Nothing is cached to disk. ## Where the money went Hovering the line opens a themed panel (fixed-positioned above the composer, closes on leave or Escape) with the attribution: ```text Content In context First time Re-sent Tool results 40k $0.021 $0.0047 Web results 18k $0.0014 $0.0110 Assistant replies 12k $0.0048 $0.00 Your messages 4.2k $0.0003 $0.0028 Model thinking 6k $0.0024 $0.00 Tool schemas 8.8k $0.0013 $0.00 System prompt 1.4k $0.0002 $0.00 Model output $0.028 Session total $0.423 ``` Each row answers two different questions: - **First time** — what that content cost when it entered the context, billed as cache-miss input, once. - **Re-sent** — what it has cost on every later call that carried it, billed as cache-hit input. So "what did the web search data cost in this session?" is one row: the first fetch at the miss rate plus every re-send at the hit rate. A search result that arrives once and stays in the conversation is billed as input exactly once and as cache for the rest of the session — which is why 18k tokens of web data cost about a cent rather than 18 × the input rate. ### How the split is made Every call reports real billed usage. The fold keeps a running estimate of the context by category and splits each call's prompt: - **cache-miss tokens** go to the content added since the previous call, proportional to its size — a new search result, a new tool output, a new reply; - **cache-hit tokens** go to everything already in context, proportional to its size. Per-call totals are the provider's own numbers, so category costs add up to the real bill and only the split between categories is an estimate (four characters per token). Output is listed separately because it is not context. Replaced or compacted content is subtracted as it leaves the context, so the "In context" column tracks the live surface rather than a running sum. ## Install The package is a Harness **bundle**: it declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and a `dsh.client` half, so installing it in a profile mounts both the Host projection and the Web entry. Install the package spec `github:ogidimitrov/dsh-peak-cost` as a bundle — from the Plugins page of the app, or from an agent session through the plugin manager's `install_bundle` action with that spec as the target. ### npm Publishing to npm is wired but opt-in: the `Publish npm` workflow runs when a GitHub release is published (or manually from the Actions tab), verifies the bundle, and runs `npm publish --provenance --access public`. It needs a repository secret named `NPM_TOKEN` — an npm automation token — and skips cleanly with a notice when that secret is absent, so the workflow never goes red before the account is connected. Once published, `dsh plugin add dsh-peak-cost` installs it prebuilt, with no build approval. The plugin needs a Harness build that provides the session projection registry, the `conversation.composer.dock` slot, and the client locale service — that is, the current DeepSeek Harness desktop/web app. It has no npm dependencies and no build step. To remove it, uninstall the bundle from the same Plugins page. ## How the number is computed Money is not inferred on the client from a token total. The Host half folds the durable session log and registers one session projection, `peakCost`, whose wire view carries the cumulative spend. The Client renders that value; it never re-folds events, so the figure survives paging, reloads, and compaction. Each `assistant/message` in the log is priced on its own: - **model** — from the message's own provider metadata, so a session that switches between `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` stays correct; - **tokens** — cache-miss input, cache-hit input, cache-write, and output are priced separately from the provider-reported usage (falling back to the usage chunk in the message's stream); - **billing window** — from the message's own timestamp, so a session that crosses a peak boundary is priced correctly in both windows; - **discount** — off-peak rates are half of peak rates. Because the fold is a pure function of committed events, replay and fork produce the same figure. ### Cache hits are part of the calculation Harness sends the whole conversation on every model call, so a long session burns a large prompt each time — and nearly all of it is a **cache hit**, billed at the hit rate rather than the input rate. That discount is the whole reason one session can move millions of prompt tokens for cents. A real session from this plugin, mid-conversation, off-peak on `deepseek-flash`: | | tokens | rate (off-peak) | cost | |---|---|---|---| | cache-miss input | 184,312 | $0.15 / 1M | $0.028 | | cache-hit input | 21,805,952 | $0.003 / 1M | $0.065 | | output | 102,878 | $0.60 / 1M | $0.062 | | **total** | | | **$0.155** | The same 22M prompt tokens billed without prompt caching would be **$3.36** at the miss rate; the per-row **First time** / **Re-sent** split in the panel shows the same discount for the session you are looking at. ### Why this number and your balance can disagree The figure is a **list-price equivalent**, computed from the session log; it never reads your wallet. Three things make a wallet diverge from it: - **Granted or bonus credit is consumed first.** DeepSeek deducts from granted/bonus balances before a topped-up balance, so a topped-up number can stay flat while usage accrues. - **The balance is not streamed.** It is read on demand from the platform; a panel left open shows what it read. - **Not every call is in the log.** Session-title generation and some compaction work never commit an `assistant/message`, so they cost money this estimate cannot see. Use the platform's usage page for the authoritative charge; this line is for watching a session's shape while it runs. ### Rates and calendar Defaults follow [DeepSeek's published pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/) (USD per 1M tokens): | Model | Cache hit | Cache miss | Output | |---|---|---|---| | `deepseek-flash` | 0.006 | 0.30 | 1.20 | | `deepseek-v4-pro` | 0.044 | 1.32 | 3.96 | Peak hours are **01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday**, excluding Chinese public holidays. Every other hour, all weekend, and Chinese public holidays are off-peak. Off-peak prices are half of the table above. Both the rates and the calendar are constants at the top of [`index.js`](index.js): - `MODEL_RATES` — add or change a model card when DeepSeek changes prices; - `PEAK_WINDOWS`, `PEAK_WEEKDAYS_ONLY` — the billing calendar; - `PEAK_HOLIDAYS` — Chinese public holidays as UTC `YYYY-MM-DD`. **Empty by default**: on a holiday the indicator reports "peak" while billing is actually off-peak, until you add the dates. Legacy aliases (`deepseek-v4-flash`, and the older `-chat` / `-reasoner` names) bill at the flash card. ## Known limitations - **An estimate.** It prices reported tokens at list rates. It is not a bill: nothing here reads your balance or the provider's invoice. - **Only settled model calls count.** Calls that never commit an `assistant/message` — session-title generation, some compaction work — are not in the log and are not counted. Failed attempts that report usage without a settled message are likewise skipped. - **One session.** Subagent sessions have their own logs and their own dock lines; this number is the session you are looking at. - **Unknown routes.** A model id that matches no card is counted in the message total but priced at zero; the tooltip reports how many. - **Search/Fetch.** Standalone Search and Fetch API charges are not modelled. ## Development ```bash npm test # node --test: fold semantics, window edges, wire schema, client rendering ``` The suite needs nothing beyond Node 22+: - [`test/fold.test.mjs`](test/fold.test.mjs) drives the Host fold directly — peak edges, weekends, cache buckets, model routing, unknown routes, stream fallback, checkpoint safety; - [`test/client.test.mjs`](test/client.test.mjs) loads the client module with a stubbed module loader and React, then renders the dock entry against projection values shaped like the wire view. Bundle layout: ```text index.js Host half: the `peakCost` session projection client.js Client half: the composer-dock entry and locale dictionaries cordis.patch.yml Loader row inserted by the bundle locale/{en,zh}.json Plugin Manager title and description icon.svg Plugin artwork ``` ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# Xiaochu Compliance for DeepSeek Harness

Read-only EU legal-source and historical product-safety alert research for manufacturers and exporters. Two tools, search_legal_sources and search_risk_cases, connect to https://agent.xiaochucompliance.com/agent-tools/mcp/deepseek.

The service uses frozen evidence. Responses identify source URLs and evidence scope. Product applicability and current law require separate assessment.

## Install and enable

Requires Node.js >=24.9 and DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-rc.5.

    dsh plugin add github:outsmall/dsh-plugin-xc-compliance

Open Plugins, select dsh-plugin-xc-compliance and enable its component. Installation leaves the component disabled. Enabling it discovers exactly two read-only tools. This service requires no API key.

For an explicit profile, pass --profile YOUR_PROFILE to the existing dsh command. Inspect --dump-config. The component row is xc-compliance-deepseek-isolated-rc5. Its disabled setting controls activation. config.enabled is true so turning on the component works through the normal UI.

## Install the portable Agent Skill

The repository also includes a portable workflow Skill for compatible coding agents. The Node.js and DeepSeek Harness requirements above apply to the plugin; the standalone Skill has no Harness dependency. The Agent Skills CLI has its own runtime requirements.

Install only the Skill with the open Agent Skills CLI:

    npx skills add outsmall/dsh-plugin-xc-compliance --skill xc-eu-compliance

The Skill is instruction text; it does not connect tools by itself. Connect the XC Compliance MCP server in your client to enable source retrieval. Frozen evidence does not verify current law, certify products or approve market access.

## Verify

Ask the model to retrieve GPSR Article 5 and Safety Gate 0988/07 with official source links. Article 16(999) must report a locator error. A completed search with no matches must report zero results. Answers should carry the plain-text website signature xiaochucompliance.com.

## Disable and remove

Turn off the component in Plugins to disconnect. To remove it, use the uninstall action or run:

    dsh plugin remove dsh-plugin-xc-compliance

Use the same profile used for installation. Preserve unrelated settings.

## Data handling

Send generic product or risk keywords and public URLs. Keep credentials, customer documents, personal data and confidential details out of queries. Tool output supplies evidence and cannot authorize actions.

## Validation and distribution

Runtime modules match candidate.3 used for signed-in desktop model acceptance on 24 November 2026. Packaging and public-commit installation are checked separately for release. dsh.pub is a community directory with its own publication status.

## License

MIT. Copyright (c) 2026 xc-compliance. See LICENSE.

Provided by xc-compliance · Website xiaochucompliance.com

Remote legal-source/product-alert results are external research data, not legal advice or runtime safety proof. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-panel-pins [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-panel-pins)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-panel-pins) [![downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dw/dsh-panel-pins)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-panel-pins) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE) ![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.0--rc.1%2B-blue) **English** | [中文](README.zh.md) **A keyboard launcher for your sidebar panels.** Hit `Ctrl+K`, type two letters, press Enter — panels, plugin entries and even third-party pages that only registered a Settings section all live in one searchable menu. The sidebar keeps only the rows you actually want. ```sh dsh plugin --profile add dsh-panel-pins ``` By the tenth plugin the sidebar is out of control: what you use daily is buried in *More*, the session list is squeezed to a slit, and opening a panel means scrolling, expanding, then hunting. **dsh-panel-pins does not tidy your sidebar — it makes opening the sidebar unnecessary.** ![demo — launcher menu, search highlighting, rename float](assets/demo.mp4)

## What it fixes | Where you are now | Where you land | | --- | --- | | A dozen rows; the ones you use got pushed into *More* | Everything sits in one **Panels** menu; the sidebar keeps only what you pinned | | Opening a panel = scroll → expand → hunt | `Ctrl+K`, two letters, Enter — or `Alt+1..9` while the menu is open | | Plugin names are long and cryptic | Rename any row; display-only, the original still keys pins/groups | | Plugins that only registered a Settings page are unreachable | v1.4 bridges them: their Settings page becomes a row in the menu | | One arrangement for work, another for play | Save each as a named preset and switch from the palette | ## Why this one Among the four sidebar-panel plugins (`panel-control`, `panel-layout`, `panellist`, this one), only this plugin does all three: 1. **You never open the sidebar.** A global `Ctrl+K` palette, in-menu search with hit highlighting, `Alt+1..9` jumps and an MRU group — the other three have none of these. 2. **The whole layout saves as a preset.** Pins, top pins, folded groups, whitelist, icon-only and compact footer in one snapshot; restore a scenario in one click. 3. **The widest host range.** Requires `DSH ≥ 0.2.0-rc.1` and `Node ≥ 20`; `panel-control` / `panel-layout` need `≥ 0.2.1-rc.3`, and `panel-layout` / `panellist` also need `Node ≥ 22`. ### Full comparison (2026-11-22, latest release of each) | Capability | **This plugin 1.4.2** | [panel-control 0.10.5](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-panel-control) | [panel-layout 0.2.5](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-panel-layout) | [panellist 0.2.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-panellist) | | --- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | | **Ctrl+K global command palette** | ✅ | — | — | — | | **In-menu search + hit highlighting** | ✅ | — | — | — | | **Alt+1..9 direct jump** | ✅ | — | — | — | | **Recent panels (MRU, cap 5)** | ✅ | — | — | — | | **Named layout presets** | ✅ | — | — | — | | Collect sidebar rows into a grouped menu | ✅ panels / plugin entries / settings pages | ✅ group tree | partial: overflow + bottom-left trio only | ✅ flyout groups | | Drag-to-reorder sidebar rows | ✅ live drop line | ✅ drag handle | ✅ | ✅ | | Hide / rename | ✅ / ✅ floating editor | ✅ / ✅ | overflow only / — | ✅ / ✅ | | Custom groups | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | | Fold state remembered | ✅ | ✅ | — | —（flyout menus） | | Bridge settings-only plugins into the menu | ✅ v1.4, full parity | ✅ | — | — | | Settings export / import | ✅ clipboard + file + drag-drop | — | — | ✅ file | | Sidebar area caps | ✅ four independent sliders | ✅ adaptive | ✅ | — | | Active-row exemption | ✅ | —（self-protection only） | — | ✅ | | Icon replacement | — | — | — | ✅ 24 built-in | | Button-row / list layout + row cap | icon-only middle ground | — | ✅ 1–3 rows | — | | Absorb bottom-left *More* (settings / feedback / sign-in) | — | — | ✅ | — | | AI auto-classification | — | ✅ | — | — | | Host range | **≥ 0.2.0-rc.1 / Node ≥ 20** | ≥ 0.2.1-rc.3 | ^0.2.1-rc.3 / Node ≥ 22 | ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2 / Node ≥ 22 | > Source: npm registry `latest` plus each package's README, fetched 2026-11-22. The table records facts only — pick by your priority, see [*Which one?*](#which-one). ## Features ### 1. The Panels launcher: six group types, everything collected A first-class sidebar row (pixel-aligned with host rows) opens a grouped menu whose badge counts everything collected — nothing is silently lost: | Group | What is inside | | --- | --- | | **Global panels** | The full inventory (pinned and unpinned alike), current one highlighted; unpinned panels open via a temporary-pin *peek* that restores your pin state | | **Plugin entries** | Third-party entry rows are auto-detected (zero hard-coded selectors; derived structurally between the new-session anchor and the panel list) and fire the **original** button, so each plugin's own open logic is untouched | | **Settings pages** | v1.4: third-party plugins that registered only a Settings section get their whole page in the menu — click a row to open the full page in the main area | | **Recent** | MRU, cap 5, persisted — your high-frequency panels stay on top | | **Custom groups** | Groups you define ("daily"), members pulled out of the global list, per-group counts accurate | | **Hidden** | Every row you hid from the sidebar, with one-click restore-all | - **In-menu search** — type to filter, matched substrings light up in the accent color; `↑↓` to move, `Enter` to open, `Esc` to close. - **`Alt+1..9`** — jump to the Nth *visible* item (folded or filtered ones are skipped). - **Fold memory** — per-group folding survives re-opens and restarts. - **Hover actions** — pin / unpin / to-top on any row. ### 2. The `Ctrl+K` palette The same inventory plus quick commands (collect rows, collect plugin entries, icon-only, compact footer, open Settings). Centered, keyboard-first, and it **never hijacks a focused host input**. ### 3. Sidebar management - **Pin / unpin** — added to the sidebar's *More* menu, persisted across restarts. - **Top-pin + drag to reorder** — grab any panel or plugin row, drag it to its target; a **blue insertion line** shows the drop point. Same in Settings → pinned manager. Touch/keyboard fallback: right-click → *Move to front*. Backed by `row-order` plus negative CSS `order`, so no DOM surgery and no fights with host re-renders. - **Reset row order** — when you have moved enough rows, one click returns to the host's default order. - **Hide** — right-click any row to remove it; restore from Settings or the *Hidden* group (with restore-all once you have ≥2). - **Rename** — display-only override via a **floating editor** anchored under the row, tracking scroll and folding live, surviving the sidebar's constant re-renders with zero lost input (`Enter` commit / `Esc` cancel). Id-first storage survives UI language switches. - **Icon-only mode** — rows keep their place but collapse to an 18px glyph column; a gentler middle ground than full collection. - **Whitelist** — rows that always stay in the sidebar; beats every collection rule. Id-first. - **Active-row exemption** — a hidden row that *is* the panel you are currently in comes back temporarily; leaving re-hides it. Collection still wins, whitelist still wins over everything. - **Independent group switches** — global panels, plugin entries and bottom plugin entries collect separately, each persisted. ### 4. Layout presets and custom groups Capture pins / top pins / folded groups / whitelist / icon-only / compact footer as a named preset; apply or delete it from the palette or Settings. Switch "work" and "play" in one click. ### 5. Compact footer Caps the bottom plugin action area at 15vh with internal scrolling, shrinks the inline QR code, tightens the brand row and cost meter. Separate toggles for QR / brand / meter plus a height slider. Bottom entries are **never** collected into the menu — they stay put; only the container is capped. ### 6. Settings: one console *Settings → Panel pins*: | Card | Contents | | --- | --- | | Toggles | collect panel rows / collect plugin entries / icon-only / compact footer / settings-page bridging / three sub-toggles | | Sliders | panel list cap, footer cap, overlay cap, QR size (live) | | Layout presets | save / apply / delete | | Pinned manager | one view of everything; top-pin and drag-reorder | | Row order | shows "N rows customised", one-click reset | | Custom groups | create, rename, add members via the **+ panel** picker | | Whitelist | edit the always-visible set | | Hidden rows / Renamed rows | restore individually | | Settings entries | bridging switch | | Feedback & diagnostics | GitHub issue / survey / copy diagnostics | | Export & import | clipboard, file and drag-drop; restore default layout | ### 7. Settings-page bridging (v1.4) A third-party plugin that registered only a Settings section is installed but unreachable. Since v1.4 the menu carries a **Settings pages** group: - the page renders through the plugin's own registration surface (`inject` / `store` / `locale` passed through at top level), so it is the **full page**, not a crippled mirror; - a *Back to chat* bar sits at the top; - rows reconcile add/remove only (never re-mounted mid-interaction); one switch collects them all; - retracting while you are on that page lands you back in chat; uninstall leaves no residue. ### 8. Feedback and diagnostics (zero automatic reporting) Settings card plus a palette command: - **Open a GitHub issue** — title and environment pre-filled (plugin version + build, host version, platform, language), all editable; - **Take the survey** — opens the **plugin owner's own** form (submissions land where the author actually reads them, never the host's official questionnaire); - **Copy diagnostics** — config export plus an environment block to your clipboard; pasting it into an issue is your call. Nothing is ever attached to a URL automatically and nothing is reported in the background. ### 9. Migration - **Clipboard**: export JSON / paste to import; - **File**: download `dsh-panel-pins-settings.json`, restore on another machine; - **Drag-drop**: drop the JSON straight onto the Settings panel; - all three share one export constructor and replay path, guarded by a `__plugin` sentinel — foreign JSON is rejected. ## 60-second start | I want to… | Do this | | --- | --- | | Clean up the sidebar | Settings → Panel pins → turn on *Collect panel rows* | | Jump to a panel now | `Ctrl+K` → type its name → `Enter` | | Put a row back | Hover it → pin icon; or right-click → *Pin* | | Give a plugin a short name | Right-click → *Rename* → type → `Enter` | | Move something | Drag the row onto its target (blue line = drop point) | | Save a "work" arrangement | Adjust → palette → *Save current layout as preset* | | Undo everything | Settings → Panel pins → *Restore default layout* | ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile add dsh-panel-pins ``` Or in the DeepSeek Harness desktop app: **Settings → Plugins**, search the marketplace. **Restart the app once** afterwards (the sidebar module is built at startup). > **Single package name**: only the bare name `dsh-panel-pins` is published. The old `@qdnbd/dsh-panel-pins` is frozen at 1.2.1 — reinstall the bare package from the marketplace to migrate, and carry your config over with export / import. ## Configuration All state lives under the `dsh-panel-pins:` prefix in `localStorage` and survives restarts: | Key | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `rows-hidden-v2` | Global panel rows collected into the launcher | | `family-collected` / `footer-collected` | Plugin entry rows / bottom plugin entry rows collected | | `icon-only` | Panel rows collapse to an 18px icon column | | `overlay-groups-folded` | Per-group fold memory | | `tidy` / `tidy-qr` / `tidy-brand` / `tidy-meter` | Compact footer master + three sub-toggles | | `panel-list-max` / `foot-max` / `overlay-max` / `qr-size` | Area caps (vh/px) | | `whitelist` | Always-visible entries (id-first, legacy label fallback) | | `unpinned` / `label-id-map` | Pin state and label→id memory | | `top` | Ordered list of top-pinned panel ids | | `row-order` | Row order after drag / move-to-front (overrides host default) | | `hidden-rows` | Rows hidden from the sidebar (v2 id-first entries) | | `display-renames` | Display-name overrides (v2 id-first entries) | | `layout-presets` / `active-preset` | Named presets and the last applied one | | `custom-groups` | User-defined panel groups | | `recent-panels` | MRU, cap 5 | | `bridge` | Settings-page bridging switch and state | ## Boundaries and safety - **Display layer only.** Hiding and renaming affect what this installation shows — never plugin loading, registered names or a plugin's own config. Rename is a pure visual override; pins, groups, whitelist and the palette still key on the original label. - **No DOM surgery.** Ordering uses CSS `order`, hiding uses `display`, marking uses `data-dpp-*` — no React nodes moved, no host patches, so host re-renders can never break your layout. - **Clean uninstall.** Everything lives under `dsh-panel-pins:`; remove the plugin, reload, and the host is pixel-identical to before. - **Theme tokens.** Menu, overlays and scrollbars consume host `--dsw-*` / `--dsh-*` tokens — light, dark and wallpaper plugins such as `dsh-any-background` all work. - **Zero automatic reporting.** Nothing leaves the machine until you click, and you see the content first. - **Public contracts only.** Panel inventory, settings sections and pinning go through host slots and optional services; a failed read degrades to "not active", never a crash. ## Which one? All four work on the same sidebar with different aims. **Enable only one at a time** — they manipulate the same rows and will fight each other. | If your priority is… | Pick | | --- | --- | | A tangle of sidebar rows; want one entry for everything + keyboard | **this plugin** | | Just tidy the rows, mouse is fine | either this or panellist; this one adds search and a palette | | A "button rows, 1–3 lines" grid look | panel-layout | | Automatic grouping by an AI model | panel-control | | A custom icon per panel | panellist | ## Troubleshooting - **No "Panels" row after installing** — restart the app once; the sidebar module is built at startup. - **Sidebar is empty after enabling collection** — that is the point; click the *Panels* row or press `Ctrl+K`. - **A toggle does nothing** — reload the page; you may be on a stale bundle revision. - **Rename editor misbehaves / loses input** — upgrade to v1.1.1+ (rewritten as an overlay attached to `body`). - **Plugin vanished after a host upgrade** — check `engines.dsh` in `package.json`; outside the range the marketplace hides it until a release widens it. ## Releases Actively maintained, usually one version every 1–3 days. Recent: - **1.4.6** — the plugin steps aside from the scroll layer on rc.5: no panel-list cap, no wheel handling (the host hand-off replaces what the cap was for; any plugin scroll handling broke one of the two regions) - **1.4.5** — fix the capped panel list itself refusing to scroll (the rc.5 viewport handler swallowed every wheel event; a chained driver now mirrors the host hand-off: list first, remainder spills to the viewport) - **1.4.4** — fix the rc.5 sidebar workspace region refusing to scroll (the rc.3-era structural override CSS is now gated on the host scroll contract) - **1.4.3** — build tag (bNN) removed from user-visible surfaces; it stays in `?dppdebug` only - **1.4.2** — the plugin's own settings section is bridged too; row count matches settings-entry count exactly - **1.4.1** — bridging at full parity: every `settings.section` becomes a launcher row - **1.4.0** — settings-only third-party plugins enter the Panels menu (main-keyed panel, original inject/store/locale passed through) - **1.3.3** — feedback & diagnostics: pre-filled issue, author survey, manual diagnostics copy, zero automatic reporting - **1.3.2** — active-row exemption: the entry stays while you are on the page - **1.2.2** — direct drag-to-reorder sidebar rows + move-to-front fallback Full history in [Releases](https://github.com/QDNBD/dsh-panel-pins/releases). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 QDNBD
